title: Require theme creation before opening a mix in a club
description:
Admins must not be able to open a mix without first creating a theme. All themes for a club must be defined before any mix can be opened in that club.

Scope:

* Block "open mix" action if no theme exists for the club/round
* Validation/guardrail on admin flow to require theme creation first
* Ensure all themes are defined upfront before any mix opens (not just the current round's)
* Error/UX messaging when an admin attempts to open a mix out of order

Release blocking.

title: Round: organizer can extend the voting deadline by 4h increments
description:
Urgent, requested directly by Dawn.

## Problem

A round's voting deadline is currently only fixable by an arbitrary-datetime PATCH; there's no dedicated "give it more time" action, and extending the deadline doesn't tell participants anything changed.

## Scope

* New endpoint: organizer/co-organizer (same permission level as other round-management actions — theme, deadlines, closing) can extend a round's `voting_deadline` by a fixed 4-hour increment, repeatable, only while the round is still `open_voting`.
* Concurrency-safe against the deadline auto-advance job and vote-cast auto-close (same `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` re-verify pattern already used by the [MYS-168](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-168/organizer-roll-a-round-back-from-voting-to-submission) rollback path).
* Resets the "12h left" warning marker so the deadline job can send a fresh warning against the new deadline.
* New `voting_extended` notification event — email to league members with notifications on, stating the new deadline.
* Frontend: a "+4h" action on the round page during voting, visible to the organizer/co-organizer.

## Out of scope

* Extending the submission deadline (not requested).
* Arbitrary/custom extension amounts (fixed 4h increments only, per the request).

title: Spotify playlists via shared account: public per-round playlist link for all members
description:
**Urgent — decided 2026-07-03.** Spotify's extended quota now requires 250k MAU, so the app stays in Development Mode indefinitely: max ~25 allowlisted Spotify accounts, platform-wide. Per-user OAuth playlist generation ([MYS-83](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-83/playlist-spotify-per-user-oauth-create-saved-playlist-for-a-round)) is therefore dead as a general feature — a beta tester (Slamlumni league) looped through connect six times against a silent 403 because his account isn't allowlisted. Replace it with the shared-account pattern: **one designated Spotify account creates each round's playlist as PUBLIC; every member just gets the link** (no API access needed to open a public playlist — same reach as the YouTube link).

## Ops prerequisites (owner actions, before/alongside the build)

* Create a dedicated **MysteryMixClub Spotify account** (not a personal one — the public playlists live on its profile)
* Allowlist it in the Spotify Developer Dashboard (User Management)
* Connect it once through the existing connect flow on staging; set the env config below

## Backend

* Config: `SPOTIFY_PLAYLIST_ACCOUNT_USER_ID` (UUID of the app user whose `spotify_connections` row is the shared token). Add to `.env.example` + staging env + both DO app specs per the secrets procedure in CLAUDE.md.
* `POST /rounds/:id/spotify-playlist`: any league member may trigger. Uses the SHARED account's refresh token (not the caller's). Creates the playlist **public** (verify the create call in `spotify_playlist.py` sets `public: true` — confirm what [MYS-83](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-83/playlist-spotify-per-user-oauth-create-saved-playlist-for-a-round) does today) and reuses-by-id on subsequent calls exactly as now, refreshing items. Store in `spotify_round_playlists` keyed by (round, shared-account user) so one playlist per round.
* Response = playlist URL; all members get the same one.
* Keep the per-user OAuth code paths **dormant, not deleted** (connect/callback/status endpoints stay; if we ever reach extended quota, flip back). Remove nothing from the DB.
* **Callback observability fix rides along** (from the incident): log the swallowed exceptions at `spotify.py:167-168` with the Spotify error body, and use distinct redirect flags (`denied` / `exchange_failed` / `api_error`).

## Frontend

* Round page: replace the connect-gated Spotify block with a plain "Spotify playlist →" affordance available to every member (parallel to the existing YouTube link; same generate-on-first-click behavior).
* Remove the "Connect Spotify" entry point from the round page (profile-level connect UI can stay hidden/dormant).

## Risks / accepted trade-offs (approved by product 2026-07-03)

* Playlists are public and appear on the shared account's profile — hence the dedicated account.
* Single point of failure: revoked grant breaks playlist gen platform-wide until reconnected; the round page should show the calm error state, and logs must say why.
* Dev-mode terms nominally target personal/small-scale use; accepted at invite-only beta scale.

## Done when

Any league member (no Spotify connection of their own) clicks the Spotify affordance on a voting round and gets a working public playlist link; the same link is returned to every member; regeneration refreshes tracks; failures are logged and visibly surfaced; per-user OAuth UI is gone from the round page.

title: Auth/Spotify: OAuth connect return lands authenticated user on /login (root route hard-redirects to /login)
description:
**Found on staging (HAR-confirmed).** After connecting Spotify, the user lands on the **login page** even though they're fully authenticated.

## Root cause (definitive, from the HAR)

On return from Spotify the app's silent refresh is **200** and `GET /users/me` is **200** — the session is fine. The bug is **routing**:

* The Spotify callback redirects to `APP_BASE_URL/?spotify=connected` → path `/`.
* `App.tsx:33`: `<Route path="/" element={<Navigate to="/login" replace />} />` — `/` **unconditionally** redirects to `/login`, ignoring auth.
* `/login` (`LoginRoute`) doesn't bounce authenticated users away, so they're stuck on the login form.

This was **not** a cookie/SameSite problem ([MYS-91](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-91/auth-session-lost-after-returning-from-spotify-oauth-switch-refresh)'s Lax change was a related hardening but not the fix — the refresh was always succeeding).

## Fix

1. Backend (`app/api/routes/spotify.py`): callback redirects to `/home` (an authenticated route), not `/`.
2. Frontend (`LoginRoute`): redirect already-authenticated users to `/home` (defense-in-depth; also fixes the latent `/`→`/login` trap for any authenticated user hitting `/`).

## Possible enhancement

Return the user to the **round** they connected from (pass it through the OAuth `state` / a param) instead of `/home`. The popup flow ([MYS-85](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-85/spotify-playlist-login-should-be-a-popupmodal-not-a-full-page-redirect)) would preserve context naturally.

title: Auth: session lost after returning from Spotify OAuth — switch refresh cookie to SameSite=Lax
description:
**Found on staging.** After connecting Spotify (full-page redirect to consent and back), the user lands on the **MMC login page** — the session is silently lost on return.

## Root cause

The connect flow does a full-page redirect (`window.location.assign`), wiping the in-memory access token. On return the app does one silent refresh against the refresh cookie — but the cookie is `SameSite=Strict`, which the browser withholds on the **cross-site-initiated navigation** back from `accounts.spotify.com`, so the refresh fails → `ProtectedRoute` → /login. (Normal reloads keep the session; only the OAuth round-trip breaks it — the signature of the Strict-cookie issue.)

## Fix

Change the refresh cookie to `SameSite=Lax` (`backend/app/api/routes/auth.py`, set + delete).

**Security:** safe. Lax still withholds the cookie on all cross-site POST/XHR, and every sensitive endpoint under the cookie path (`/auth/refresh`, `/auth/logout`, `/auth/logout-all`) is **POST**, so it can't be CSRF-forged. `/auth/verify` is GET but acts on a token query param, not the cookie. Deviates from technical-design §5/§9 (Strict) — doc updated with the rationale.

The robust alternative is the popup connect flow ([MYS-85](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-85/spotify-playlist-login-should-be-a-popupmodal-not-a-full-page-redirect)), which avoids the redirect entirely; Lax is the lighter fix and benefits all OAuth/cross-site returns.

## Note

Pure cookie-attribute change; existing sessions get the new attribute on their next `/auth/verify` or refresh.

title: Spotify playlist: generate 502s — missing playlist-read-private scope (reuse lookup 403s)
description:
**Found on staging (manual testing).** Generating a Spotify playlist fails with `spotify couldn't create the playlist — try again` (502).

## Root cause (reproduced locally with a real token)

`find_playlist_id_by_name` calls `GET /me/playlists`, which returns **403** `{"status":403,"message":"Insufficient client scope"}`. Our requested scopes are only `playlist-modify-public` + `playlist-modify-private`; **listing the user's playlists needs** `playlist-read-private`, which we never request.

Compounded by a regression from the PR #54 review fixes: `find_playlist_id_by_name` now **raises** `SpotifyApiError` on any non-200, so that 403 blows up the whole generate as a 502. (Pre-#54 it returned `None` and fell through to create.)

**Implication:** because `/me/playlists` always 403s with the current scopes, [MYS-87](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-87/spotify-playlist-reuse-same-named-playlist-instead-of-creating) **reuse never actually worked** — the lookup could never see an existing playlist.

## Fix

1. Add `playlist-read-private` to `PLAYLIST_SCOPES` (`backend/app/services/spotify_client.py`).
2. Make the reuse lookup **non-fatal** again: `find_playlist_id_by_name` degrades to `None` on any non-401 failure (401 → `SpotifyAuthError` for reconnect), so a lookup hiccup never blocks generation — at worst a duplicate. (Robust reuse-by-id is [MYS-89](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-89/spotify-playlist-persist-playlist-id-per-round-user-instead-of-name).)
3. **Migration caveat:** existing connections were authorized without the new scope, so **all users must disconnect + reconnect** once to re-consent.

title: Frontend auth flow (magic link UI)
description: Build the frontend auth flow\\n\\n- Email entry screen (request magic link)\\n- "Check your email" confirmation screen\\n- Magic link landing page (verify token, store access token in memory, redirect)\\n- Silent refresh wired up on all authenticated requests\\n- Logout button in profile/nav\\n- "Log out of all devices" option in profile settings\\n- PWA-friendly: works correctly when opened from home screen

title: Logout and logout-all-devices endpoints
description: Implement POST /api/v1/auth/logout and POST /api/v1/auth/logout-all\\n\\n- logout: set invalidated_at on current session, clear refresh token cookie\\n- logout-all: set invalidated_at on ALL active sessions for the user, clear cookie\\n- Both return 200 on success\\n- This is the "log out of all devices" privacy feature

title: Silent token refresh flow
description: Implement POST /api/v1/auth/refresh\\n\\n- Read refresh token from HttpOnly cookie\\n- Validate against sessions table (exists, not invalidated, not expired)\\n- Update last_used_at on the session record\\n- Issue new JWT access token (60-minute expiry)\\n- Return new access token in response body\\n- Return 401 if refresh token invalid or expired

title: Magic link verification and session issuance
description: Implement GET /api/v1/auth/verify\\n\\n- Validate token against magic_link_tokens table (exists, unexpired, unused)\\n- Hard-delete token immediately on use (single-use enforcement)\\n- Create user if first login\\n- Issue JWT access token (60-minute expiry)\\n- Issue refresh token (cryptographically random, 30-day expiry)\\n- Store refresh token hash in sessions table\\n- Return access token in response body\\n- Set refresh token as HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict cookie

title: Magic link request endpoint
description: Implement POST /api/v1/auth/request\\n\\n- Accept email in request body\\n- Generate cryptographically random token (min 32 bytes, URL-safe)\\n- Store token hash in magic_link_tokens table with 15-minute expiry\\n- Send magic link email via Resend\\n- Rate limit: max 5 requests per email per hour\\n- Never reveal whether email exists in the system

title: Sprint 1: Authentication
description: Parent issue for all auth work. Implement the full magic link authentication system before any other features.\\n\\nSee: `docs/technical/technical-design.md` Section 5 (Authentication)

title: Admin dashboard: view registered users + activity
description: Pivot 2 (2026-07-27, same conversation as ADR 0007/MysteryMixClub-ali8): admin-facing dashboard to see which users are in the system and their activity. Deliberately not yet scoped in detail -- Dawn asked to scope this after the Google/password auth epic (MysteryMixClub-ali8) ships. Needs a follow-up scoping conversation (data to show, activity definition, access control) before breaking into child issues.

title: Frontend: login screen — add Google and password options alongside magic link
description: Login screen shows all three methods. Google's official Sign-In button (their logo/colors/type) is a documented style-guide exception (ADR 0007) — do not reskin it. Password fields follow the existing underline-input + Rust invalid-state pattern (ADR 0004). Magic link's existing entry point is unchanged, just no longer the only option.

title: Backend: Google OAuth sign-in
description: Add google_id (nullable, unique) to users. New endpoints for the OAuth redirect/callback flow (standard authorization-code exchange), creating a new account or linking to an existing one on first sign-in. Refresh cookie is already SameSite=Lax (MYS-91) specifically for this case, so no cookie change needed. Depends on the Google Cloud OAuth client existing (see the provisioning task) to test against real credentials.
notes: Endpoint contract locked in by the staging-setup.md runbook (ali8.3): GET /api/v1/auth/google/login (redirects to Google's consent screen, 404 when unconfigured) and GET /api/v1/auth/google/callback (authorization-code exchange). Keep these paths — the runbook and prod-setup.md's GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI already reference them.

title: Provision Google Cloud OAuth client + wire secrets (staging + prod)
description: Create the Google Cloud project/OAuth client and consent screen, add GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET to .env.example and both staging.env/prod.env per the standard secret-onboarding process (docs/ci-cd.md). Start the Google verification review for the email/profile scopes early — the app already has live users, so a production OAuth client at this user count needs that review, which can add lead time outside our control. Track that review's status here.
close_reason: Staging OAuth client provisioned and credentials wired into /etc/mysterymixclub/staging.env (2026-07-27, confirmed by Dawn). Prod uses the identical documented steps (docs/prod-setup.md, docs/staging-setup.md 'Enabling Google Sign-In') whenever prod deploy is being prepared -- not a blocker for ali8.2's backend implementation.

title: Backend: password-based auth (register, login, reset)
description: Add password_hash (nullable) to users. New endpoints: password login, password set/register for an account, and a forgot/reset-password flow via Resend email (mirrors magic link's token pattern: single-use, expiring, hashed token). Login endpoint needs its own brute-force rate limiting — today only /auth/request is rate-limited. Use argon2 for hashing.
close_reason: Merged via PR #212 (squash), 2026-07-28. Full dev/review/fix/re-review cycle: 1 HIGH (register enumeration oracle) + 2 MEDIUM (blocking argon2, unbounded login_attempts) caught and fixed pre-merge. Manually smoke-tested against a live local stack (register/login/magic-link-still-works/forgot-reset/lockout/enumeration-fix all confirmed) plus green CI before merge. Deploying to staging now for Dawn's own test pass.

title: Auth: add Google Sign-In and password login alongside magic link
description: Magic link is the #1 user complaint (login friction/deliverability). ADR 0007 (docs/adr/0007-google-and-password-auth-alongside-magic-link.md) decides to add Google OAuth and email+password as two new sign-in methods that coexist with magic link, which stays fully supported and unchanged. Existing accounts are unaffected unless they opt in (set a password / link Google from settings). New signups via any of the three methods still go through the existing invite/waitlist gate.

title: Bug: deleting a club fails if any mix has a generated Spotify/Apple playlist
description:
Discovered incidentally during MysteryMixClub-y49x0v (MYS-258) implementation, 2026-07-26 - this is a PRE-EXISTING bug, not introduced by that work, but playlist_jobs (the new table added in MYS-258) now shares the identical latent gap, so it was surfaced while reviewing the pattern.

DELETE /clubs/:id manually cascades votes/notes/submissions/mixes/invites/members/club in application code, but never touches spotify_mix_playlists or apple_mix_playlists - neither has ondelete=CASCADE on their FK to mixes, and the manual cascade in the delete route does not delete them either.

## Impact

If any mix in a club ever had a Spotify playlist generated (auto-generated on mix close, shipped since MYS-83) or an Apple Music playlist generated (per-player, shipped since MYS-104-108), deleting that club today fails with a foreign-key constraint violation - organizer-initiated club deletion (MYS-124) is broken for any club with real usage history.

## Scope

- Add ondelete=CASCADE to spotify_mix_playlists.mix_id and apple_mix_playlists.mix_id FKs (Alembic migration), OR add explicit delete statements to the club-delete route's manual cascade, matching whichever pattern the rest of that cascade already uses.
- playlist_jobs.mix_id (new table, MYS-258) has the identical gap - fix it in the same pass, do not ship a third table with this bug already present.
- Add a regression test: create a club with a mix that has a generated playlist (of each type), delete the club, confirm it succeeds and the playlist rows are gone.
- Check whether this already caused any real failed deletions in prod/staging (log/error monitoring) before assuming it has been silently latent.
notes: Found via MysteryMixClub-y49x0v (MYS-258) review. Fix playlist_jobs's FK in the same pass, not as a separate follow-up.

title: Instrument Claude Code token usage for MMC agent workflow
description:
## Why

No measurement exists for what the five-subagent workflow costs in tokens, or
how that cost is distributed across developer / tester / reviewer / ui-agent /
product-manager. Model assignment has been tuned by intuition. Telemetry is
forward-only — nothing is captured for any period before this lands.

## Scope

1. Enable OpenTelemetry export.
   CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1
   OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER=prometheus     # scrapes at localhost:9464/metrics
   Set in shell profile, not per-session, so coverage is unbroken.
   Default metric export interval is 60s.

2. Stand up local scrape + retention. Prometheus + Grafana via docker-compose is
   sufficient; no cloud dependency. This is agent-workflow observability and is
   deliberately separate from MMC's own runtime observability.

3. Define the core metric:
      sum(claude_code.token.usage) / sum(claude_code.pull_request.count)
   sliced by agent.name for per-subagent attribution. Also break token.usage
   down by `type` (input / output / cacheRead / cacheCreation) — cache hit ratio
   is the lever most likely to move cost, and it is invisible in aggregate totals.

4. Secondary series worth panelling:
      claude_code.cost.usage          (USD, by model and agent.name)
      claude_code.commit.count
      claude_code.lines_of_code.count (by type added/removed, by model)
      claude_code.active_time.total   (by type user/cli)

5. Backfill the pre-instrumentation period from ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl,
   which carries per-request usage going back weeks. ONE-TIME extraction only:
   the transcript format is internal to Claude Code and changes between
   releases. Do not build a standing pipeline against it.
acceptance_criteria:
- claude_code.session.count visible in the backend, confirming the pipe works
- Dashboard shows tokens-per-PR broken out by agent.name
- At least one full week of continuous data before any conclusions are drawn
- Backfilled history loaded and clearly labelled as reconstructed, not measured
notes:
- Cost metrics are approximations; treat /cost and provider billing as ground truth
- Claude Code OTel support is in beta, details subject to change
- Reference: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/monitoring-usage

title: Production runtime: gunicorn workers, graceful reload, swap, CI-built frontend
description:
## Problem

The prod droplet (`mysterymixclub-prod`) runs uvicorn single-process with no
`--workers` flag, has no swap, and the deploy script builds the frontend
(`npm ci && npm run build`) on the droplet itself during every deploy —
none of these are a real production posture, and the frontend build in
particular risks OOMing a 2GB box under load.

## Rescoped 2026-07-26 — see notes

This ticket originally also proposed moving prod Postgres to a managed
instance and a backup/restore acceptance criterion. Both removed from this
ticket's scope after investigation — see Notes below for where each went.
This ticket now covers only the low-risk, independently-shippable runtime
track.

## Scope

**API runtime**

- Run uvicorn under gunicorn with a worker count tied to available cores
  (prod droplet is 2 vCPU — start at 2 workers, measure).
- SQLAlchemy is already fully async (`create_async_engine`/`AsyncSession`,
  confirmed) — the "sync session blocking the event loop" risk the original
  ticket flagged does not apply; no threadpool sizing work needed here.
- Real graceful reload on deploy: today's `deploy-prod.sh` does a hard
  `systemctl restart` regardless of worker count — change to a proper
  `SIGHUP`-based gunicorn reload (`ExecReload=` in the systemd unit,
  deploy script calls `reload` not `restart`) so requests aren't dropped
  mid-deploy.

**Deploy hygiene**

- Build the frontend in GitHub Actions and ship the built artifact to the
  droplet, instead of running `npm ci && npm run build` on the droplet
  during deploy. Needs the workflow split into a build job (hosted runner)
  and the existing deploy job (self-hosted runner, for firewall reasons)
  with an artifact hand-off, and Vite build-time env vars (e.g.
  `VITE_API_BASE_URL`) supplied to the CI build job rather than baked in
  via the droplet's env file.
- Add swap on the droplet as a safety net regardless (pure addition, no
  existing behavior touched).

## Acceptance criteria

- Prod API serves from multiple gunicorn workers with documented, measured
  throughput.
- A deploy reloads gracefully (no dropped requests) rather than hard-restarting.
- The frontend build happens in CI, not on the droplet; a deploy cannot
  OOM the application host from the build step.
- Swap is provisioned and active on the prod droplet.

## Notes

- **Managed Postgres migration — deferred, not part of this ticket.**
  Investigation (2026-07-26) found this proposal directly contradicts an
  existing documented decision: `infra/terraform/README.md`'s own "what
  breaks first at 10x users" section says to split Postgres onto its own
  plain droplet *before ever reaching for managed Postgres, which would
  reintroduce the lock-in [ADR 0002] just left*. MMC is at 5-10 users, has
  never resized the droplet — that trigger hasn't fired. Tracked separately
  as a deferred decision, not cancelled outright: see the new ticket this
  was split into.
- **Backup/restore acceptance criterion — dropped from this ticket,
  belongs to `MysteryMixClub-aqz0tt`** ("Automated offsite Postgres backup
  + restore drill"), which already owns this deliverable end to end. Not
  duplicating it under two ticket numbers.
- Prod's Postgres is confirmed co-resident with the app on the same
  droplet today (verified via `scripts/bootstrap-droplet-prod.sh`,
  `scripts/prod.env.example`, and a read-only `doctl compute droplet list`
  check) — the original ticket's framing assumed this might still need
  confirming; it's now a settled fact for future reference.

title: Move playlist generation to a background job queue
description:
## Problem

Playlist generation currently runs inside the request cycle. Each generation makes sequential outbound calls to Spotify / YouTube / Apple Music / Bandcamp / Deezer / Tidal, each taking seconds of network wait. On a single uvicorn worker, a handful of concurrent generations can starve every other request on the box.

This is the primary scaling ceiling in the current architecture, and it is not fixable by resizing the droplet. It gets acutely worse at round close, when generation fan-out coincides with a voting spike.

## Scope

* Introduce a job queue + worker process (evaluate Celery vs. RQ vs. arq vs. FastAPI `BackgroundTasks` — the last is likely insufficient since it still runs in the API process)
* Move playlist generation out of the request path; endpoint returns a job ID immediately
* Job status endpoint + frontend polling or SSE so the UI can show progress rather than hanging
* Per-provider retry with backoff; a failure on one platform should not fail the whole generation
* Respect per-provider rate limits at the worker level. Note Spotify's limit is **per-app on a rolling 30s window, shared across all users** — this needs a global throttle, not a per-request one
* Idempotency: re-running a job for the same round must not create duplicate playlists
* Dead-letter handling and visibility into failed jobs

## Acceptance criteria

* No outbound music-platform API call happens inside a request handler
* A round with N leagues closing simultaneously does not degrade p95 latency on unrelated endpoints
* Failed generations are retryable without manual DB intervention
* Job state is observable (queued / running / partial / complete / failed)

## Notes

Decide whether the queue broker is Redis on the same droplet or managed. This choice interacts with the infra ticket on multi-worker + managed Postgres.

title: Limit each player to one note per song (currently unlimited)
description:
**Bug/behavior change** (from user testing, applies to every mode — casual and competitive alike)

**Current state:** `backend/app/models/note.py` explicitly allows multiple notes per (author, submission) today — its own comment says "No unique constraint: a player may leave multiple notes on a submission (free-form appreciation)." The frontend's "leave a note" button (`SongNotes` in `frontend/src/pages/MixDetailRoute.tsx`, ~line 1942) stays available after posting, so nothing stops repeat notes on the same song by the same person.

**Ask:** exactly one note per song per author, everywhere.

**Scope**

* DB: unique constraint on `(author_id, submission_id)` + migration
* API (`backend/app/api/routes/notes.py`): change from insert-only to upsert/edit-in-place once a note exists
* Frontend: `SongNotes` becomes "edit my note" once the current user already has one, instead of always offering "leave a note"

title: Restrict club invite creation/sharing to club admin only
description:
**Feature**

Only the club admin (organizer) should be able to invite people or access/share the club's invite link. Regular players/members should not see the invite option at all.

**Scope**

* Hide invite link / "invite people" UI entirely for non-admin members
* Backend: ensure invite-related endpoints (generate/view link, send invite) are admin-gated, not just hidden client-side
* Applies to both the copyable invite link and the email-invite flow ([MYS-244](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-244/invite-via-email-club-admin-enters-an-email-invite-link-is-sent-there)) once built

title: Set up inbound email forwarding for mysterymixclub.com via Resend Inbound (→ mysterymixclubspotify@gmail.com)
description:
## Problem

Email sent to any address at `mysterymixclub.com` (e.g. an `inbox@` or similar) currently has nowhere to go and bounces. Confirmed via DNS lookup (2026-07-23): the apex domain has **no MX record at all**. The only MX record on the domain is on the `send.` subdomain (`send.mysterymixclub.com -> feedback-smtp.us-east-1.amazonses.com`), which is Resend's *outbound* bounce/feedback tracking record — unrelated to receiving mail. Resend isn't "swallowing" anything; there's simply no inbound mail exchanger configured.

## Goal

Every email sent to any address `@mysterymixclub.com` reliably reaches `mysterymixclubspotify@gmail.com` (the existing shared ops inbox already used for the Spotify integration, [MYS-234](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-234/admin-add-ops-only-connect-spotify-button-for-the-shared-playlist)).

## Decided approach: Resend Inbound (2026-07-23)

We already run Resend for outbound transactional mail — Resend also offers an **Inbound** product, so this stays on our existing vendor instead of adding ImprovMX/Cloudflare/Workspace. How it actually works, confirmed against Resend's docs:

* Inbound is **domain-wide, delivered via webhook**, not native forwarding. Add an MX record for `mysterymixclub.com` pointing to Resend; any mail to `anything@mysterymixclub.com` triggers a `POST` to an endpoint we host.
* The webhook payload is **metadata only** (sender, recipient, subject, attachment info) — the body/attachments/full MIME must be fetched via a separate Resend API call.
* To land the mail in Gmail, our endpoint has to: verify the webhook signature → fetch full content via Resend's API → call Resend's *send* API to relay it to `mysterymixclubspotify@gmail.com`.

**Scope guardrail: keep the endpoint thin.** Resend's inbound pipeline already provides its own retry/idempotency handling on delivery to our webhook — do **not** build custom dedupe, retry, or queueing infrastructure on our side for this. One handler: verify → fetch → relay. No debounce logic, no persistence, no job queue.

## Work

1. Confirm the exact MX record Resend requires for `mysterymixclub.com` (value/priority) and whether it should live on the apex or a subdomain, to avoid any conflict with the existing `send.` outbound record.
2. Add that MX record (+ any verification record) via Terraform (`infra/terraform/`), matching the existing `digitalocean_record` pattern — not clicked into the DO dashboard by hand.
3. Add a single FastAPI route for the Resend inbound webhook: verify signature, fetch the message via Resend's API, relay via Resend's send API to `mysterymixclubspotify@gmail.com`. No retry/dedupe/queue infra — Resend already handles reliable delivery to the webhook.
4. Register the webhook endpoint URL in the Resend dashboard.
5. Test end-to-end: send to a random address at the domain, confirm it lands in the Gmail inbox.

## Alternatives considered (and dropped)

* **ImprovMX** — zero-code catch-all forwarder, no app code needed, but adds a new third-party vendor for something Resend (already in use) now covers natively.
* **Cloudflare Email Routing** — free and simple, but requires migrating the domain's nameservers off DigitalOcean onto Cloudflare, a much bigger change just to get email forwarding.
* **Google Workspace** — real mailboxes, not just forwarding; heavier and paid, overkill for "just forward everything to one existing inbox."

## Done when

Sending to any address at `mysterymixclub.com` reliably arrives in `mysterymixclubspotify@gmail.com` via the Resend Inbound webhook relay, the MX record is captured in Terraform, and the webhook handler stays limited to verify→fetch→relay with no added retry/dedupe machinery.

title: Automated offsite Postgres backup (pg_dump → Spaces) + restore drill
description: Neither staging nor the proposed prod design has automated Postgres backups today — staging's droplet-level `backups` feature is off, and there's no dump/export process at all. Prod design assumes weekly droplet backups (fast full-box recovery) plus nightly `pg_dump` to a DO Spaces bucket as the portable, offsite primary — but this needs to actually be built: a cron/systemd timer running `pg_dump`, upload to Spaces, a retention policy, and a documented + tested restore procedure (a backup nobody has restored from isn't verified). See `infra/terraform/README.md` for the cost/design rationale.
notes: 2026-07-26: confirmed this ticket owns the backup/restore acceptance criterion exclusively - MysteryMixClub-s7bv2t's duplicate criterion was dropped in favor of this ticket. If MysteryMixClub-prr7 (deferred managed-Postgres decision) ever ships, this ticket's pg_dump-to-Spaces design would need rescoping to a PITR-restore drill instead - not duplicated under a new number.

title: Prod: move off DO App Platform onto self-managed droplet (Terraform + CI/CD)
description:
Decision recorded in **ADR 0002** (`docs/adr/0002-prod-platform-self-managed-droplet.md`): production moves off DO App Platform onto a self-managed droplet — same shape as staging (Nginx + systemd + local Postgres) — for portability (`digitalocean_app` has no equivalent on another cloud; Terraform can't paper over that). Claude Code is building this out, including the CI/CD migration — confirmed 2026-07-22, superseding the narrower "hand-provisioned only" framing on the original [MYS-213](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-213/devops-and-maintenance-schedule-playbook) decision.

## Scope

**Infra (Terraform):** `infra/terraform/envs/prod/` already has a proposed droplet-shaped design — `s-2vcpu-2gb`, dedicated VPC (10.120.0.0/20), cloud firewall with SSH locked to an admin CIDR (placeholder, must be replaced with a real IP before apply), reserved IP + apex/`www` DNS (ties to [MYS-174](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-174/domain-migration-move-the-app-to-wwwmysterymixclubcom)), weekly droplet backups + nightly `pg_dump` to Spaces, CPU/mem/disk monitor alerts. See `infra/terraform/README.md` for full design/cost rationale. Needs a write-scoped DO token to apply.

**CI/CD:** `deploy-prod.yml` currently deploys via `app_action/deploy` to App Platform — this needs to become an SSH-based deploy mirroring `deploy-staging.yml`:

* New `scripts/deploy-prod.sh` (mirrors `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`).
* New secrets `PROD_HOST` / `PROD_SSH_USER` / `PROD_SSH_KEY` replace `DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN` as the deploy-time credential.
* `production` environment approval gate stays; only the job's internals change.
* `advance_mixes` deadline job moves onto a systemd timer (mirrors staging's `mysterymixclub-advance-mixes.timer`) instead of needing a DO App Platform Job component — closes the gap flagged in `docs/ci-cd.md`.
* Prod secret onboarding moves from the App Platform `envs:`/dashboard route to the Droplet's `/etc/mysterymixclub/*.env` + `systemctl restart` route (same as staging).

**Docs:** `docs/ci-cd.md` and `docs/technical/technical-design.md` (§3 "Hosting: DigitalOcean App Platform") need updating once this ships to describe the droplet as prod's actual target. `.do/app.prod.yaml` and the App Platform deploy path should be deleted outright once cut over, not left as reference.

## Blocked on

Write-scoped DO token for the Terraform apply; real admin CIDR for `ssh_allowed_cidrs`; PROD_HOST/PROD_SSH_USER/PROD_SSH_KEY once the droplet exists (chicken-and-egg with the Terraform apply — droplet must exist first to get its IP for the SSH secrets).

title: Add DO cloud firewall to staging — SSH open to 0.0.0.0/0
description:
Read-only `doctl` inspection (2026-07-21) found the staging droplet (577618725) has no DO cloud firewall attached — `doctl compute firewall list` returned empty. SSH (port 22) is reachable from the entire internet at the edge, relying on host-level hardening only.

The Terraform module (`infra/terraform/modules/droplet-app`) already supports a `create_firewall` toggle with `ssh_allowed_cidrs`/`web_allowed_cidrs` variables. Fix is to set `create_firewall = true` and a real admin CIDR in `infra/terraform/envs/staging/terraform.tfvars`, then apply (needs write-scoped token).

title: ISRC-less submissions: Bandcamp/YouTube-only tracks + playlist-gap visibility
description:
Beta testers want to submit tracks that exist on Bandcamp or YouTube but NOT on the major streaming catalogs. Today every resolve path funnels through Deezer for an ISRC (`submissions.isrc NOT NULL`), so those tracks hard-fail with "no matching track found" — or worse, fuzzy-match to the wrong song. Follow-on from [MYS-200](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-200/bandcamp-platform-link-out-paste-a-link-resolution).

## Requirements

1. **Accept ISRC-less submissions** from Bandcamp and YouTube links.
2. **Make it obvious which tracks are NOT on the auto-generated playlists** (Spotify/Apple, and YouTube where unmatchable) — in the mix playlist view and anywhere the generated playlist is surfaced.

## Design sketch (from 2026-07-19 scoping)

* **Schema:** make `submissions.isrc` nullable — single `DROP NOT NULL`, additive, safe for live staging users.
* **Identity:** ISRC-less submissions get a source-anchored identity from the pasted URL — `youtube:<video_id>` / `bandcamp:<artist>/<track-slug>` (both already parsed). Dedupe on that. Audit current dedupe/equality uses of `isrc` first.
* **Resolve UX:** when the Deezer funnel misses, offer "submit as a Bandcamp/YouTube-only track" using metadata already extracted (og:title split, oEmbed title/artist), with user confirmation — instead of the hard 404. This also reduces wrong-song fuzzy accepts.
* **Playback:** the source platform is always exactly playable — YouTube-only tracks carry their exact video id (slots natively into the generated YouTube voting playlist); Bandcamp pages stream in-browser.
* **Playlist generation:** skip unmatched tracks, never guess — a wrong song in the anonymous voting playlist is worse than a gap. Surface the gap explicitly: "N tracks are Bandcamp-only — listen here" with direct source links, plus per-track marking in the playlist/tracklist UI (design-system-compliant badge, e.g. Sage Pale `bandcamp only` / `youtube only`).

## Touches

Schema migration · submission validation (`POST /mixes/:id/submissions`) · resolver miss-path + response shape · SongSearchCard confirm flow · Spotify/Apple/YouTube playlist generators (skip + report) · playlist/tracklist UI marking.

## Out of scope

Bandcamp playlist generation (no API); custom Bandcamp artist domains.

title: Rename R6: living docs, terminology notes, final audit, closeout
description:
Final rename phase — docs and process. Done **last** deliberately so docs never describe identifiers that don't exist yet.

## Scope

* Rename living docs: `CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `docs/technical/technical-design.md`, `docs/design/style-guide.md`, `docs/security/authorization-audit.md`, `docs/security/input-sanitization.md`, `docs/staging-setup.md`, `docs/ci-cd.md`, `docs/feature-flags.md`, `docs/qa/e2e-test-plan.md`.
* Historical docs (`docs/discovery/*`, `docs/prd/*`, `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`, `docs/idea-scratch.md`) get a one-line top note: *"Terminology: this document predates the July 2026 rename — 'league' is now 'club', 'round' is now 'mystery mix' (internal: mix)."* No content rename.
* **Never touch "Music League"** ([README.md:13](<http://README.md:13>), [CLAUDE.md:35](<http://CLAUDE.md:35>), discovery docs) — the competitor's proper noun.
* Final audit: `rg -in '\bleagues?\b|\brounds?\b'` excluding historical docs, frozen migrations, node_modules; whitelist: "Music League", `Math.round` ×2, SVG `strokeLine*="round"` (~36), "round-trip" prose. Zero unexplained hits.
* Update session memory files (vocabulary in beta-triage, playlist-rollout, branch-topology; remove [MYS-177](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-177/epic-cohort-bout-round-restructure-post-beta) deferral note); close the epic.

## Done when

Audit clean, docs merged, epic closed, full end-to-end staging lifecycle passed (create club → mixes → invite → submit → vote → close → wrap email → old-URL redirect → PWA refresh → timer job).

title: Rename R5: cutover — API surface + DB rename (one breaking deploy)
description:
Fifth rename phase — **the only breaking deploy**. API paths, JSON field names, and DB schema flip together in one PR, executed inside an announced maintenance window on staging.

Fusing rationale: JSON field renames change response *shapes*, so API alias routes can't save stale clients anyway; splitting API and DB would need two shims and two announced windows. The Droplet deploy is atomic (one script), so FE+BE+DB land together.

## Scope

* Backend: `/api/v1/leagues → /api/v1/clubs`; all `/rounds/… → /mixes/…` endpoints (9 route files); pydantic fields `league_id→club_id`, `round_id→mix_id`, `round_number→mix_number`, `total_rounds→total_mixes`, `current_round→current_mix`, `league_name→club_name`; delete R4's pinned-old-name column mappings.
* Alembic: ONE revision, tested `downgrade()`: `rename_table` ×5 (leagues→clubs, league_members→club_members, rounds→mixes, spotify_round_playlists→spotify_mix_playlists, apple_round_playlists→apple_mix_playlists); `alter_column(new_column_name=…)` ×11; rename the 9 named uq/ix **plus default-named PKs/FKs** (`leagues_pkey→clubs_pkey`, `submissions_round_id_fkey→…`) — Postgres does not auto-rename constraints; enumerate exact names on staging first (`SELECT conrelid::regclass, conname FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname ~ '(league|round)'` + pg_indexes). All metadata-only, single transaction.
* Frontend: `api.ts` wire property names + URL paths; service-worker `CACHE_VERSION → "mmc-shell-v2"`.

## Runbook (execute in order)

1. Night before + 15 min before: email beta users — briefly unavailable ~10 min; refresh afterwards.
2. Droplet backup: `pg_dump "$DATABASE_URL" -Fc -f ~/backups/mmc-pre-club-rename-<ts>.dump`; record row counts of all 9 affected tables.
3. Merge inside the window → auto-deploy. Known mismatch windows: alembic→restart (~seconds), restart→frontend publish (~1–4 min Vite build). Accepted.
4. Verify: `alembic current` at new head; row counts match exactly; orphan-FK LEFT-JOIN checks all 0; smoke login → club → mystery mix → playlist; journalctl clean; advance-mixes timer live.
5. Rollback (decide ≤30 min): any count mismatch / orphans / persistent 5xx after refresh → `alembic downgrade -1` on Droplet + `git revert` on develop + push. pg_dump restore is last-resort only — renames cannot corrupt row data.

## Done when

Rollback rehearsal done locally BEFORE merge (upgrade → app runs → downgrade -1 → previous commit runs); cutover executed and verified per runbook.

title: Rename R4: backend internal identifiers + advance-mixes job/systemd
description:
Fourth rename phase — Python identifier rename with the DB and wire pinned to old names (the shim R5 deletes).

## Scope

* Models: `models/league.py→club.py` (`League→Club`), `models/round.py→mix.py` (`Round→Mix`), playlist models `SpotifyRoundPlaylist→SpotifyMixPlaylist` / `AppleRoundPlaylist→AppleMixPlaylist`. Attributes renamed **with explicit old DB names pinned**: `__tablename__ = "leagues"` kept; `club_id: Mapped[…] = mapped_column("league_id", …)`; same for `mix_number`, `total_mixes`, `current_mix`, all FKs.
* Route modules renamed (`routes/leagues.py→clubs.py`, `rounds.py→mixes.py`) — router prefixes and pydantic **field** names unchanged; response *classes* may rename (`RoundResponse→MixResponse`).
* ~34 function names (`_load_league_as_organizer→_load_club_as_organizer`, `advance_round_state→advance_mix_state`, `queue_round_event→queue_mix_event`, `_round_label→_mix_label`, …); `ROUND_STATES→MIX_STATES` (state *values* untouched); event literals `round_closed→mix_closed`, `league_complete→club_complete` (verified: nothing persists event names). ~1,170 app + ~3,068 test line-matches, ~123 test names.
* Job + infra: `app/jobs/advance_rounds.py → advance_mixes.py`; new units `scripts/mysterymixclub-advance-mixes.{service,timer}`; `deploy-staging.sh` disables/removes the old advance-rounds units then installs the new ones (idempotent — no manual Droplet step).

## Done when

Full pytest + mypy green; staging smoke; `systemctl list-timers | grep advance` shows only advance-mixes; one timer run observed in journalctl.

title: Rename R3: frontend internal identifiers (wire frozen)
description:
Third rename phase — mechanical TS identifier rename, ~49 files (33 product + 16 test). No user-visible or wire changes.

## Scope

* Types: `League→Club`, `Round→Mix`, `RoundState→MixState`, `LeagueMember→ClubMember`, etc.
* ~20 function names in `services/api.ts` (`createLeague→createClub`, `getRound→getMix`, …).
* Component + file renames: `RoundDetailRoute→MixDetailRoute`, `LeagueHomeScreen→ClubHomeScreen`, `MyLeaguesScreen→MyClubsScreen`, and the rest; 16 test files follow.
* Heaviest files: `api.ts` (194 hits), `LeagueHomeScreen` (225), `RoundDetailRoute` (183).

## Hard rule — the wire is frozen until R5

JSON property names (`league_id`, `round_id`, `round_number`, `total_rounds`, `current_round`, `league_name`) and every `/api/v1/leagues…` / `/rounds/…` path string in `api.ts` stay byte-identical. Guard before merge: grep `api.ts` for `club_id|mix_id` — only *type* names may appear, never wire strings.

Excluded from any replace: SVG `strokeLinecap/Linejoin="round"` (~36), Tailwind `rounded-*`, `Math.round` (2).

## Done when

Typecheck + full frontend suite green; manual smoke against the live staging backend (proves wire compatibility unchanged).

title: Rename R2: backend user-visible copy — emails, playlists, error details
description:
Second rename phase — every string the backend puts in front of a human. Depends on R1 being deployed (emails will link `/clubs/{id}`).

## Scope

* `app/services/notifications.py`: `_round_label` → `Mystery Mix {n}: {theme}` / `Mystery Mix {n}`; all 5 event subject/body pairs; deadline warnings; empty-mix notice; welcome email; unsubscribe footer → "You're receiving this because you're in this club on MysteryMixClub." (avoids "MysteryMixClub club"); league URLs → `/clubs/{id}`.
* Key copy: club-complete event → subject `{club} — that's a wrap`, body "…has wrapped after its final mystery mix." ("the club is complete" reads like a roster statement.)
* `app/services/spotify_playlist.py` (shared by the Apple path): name fallback `MysteryMixClub: {club}, Mix {n}` — full "Mystery Mix" would double the brand in the title; description → "Every song from Mystery Mix {n} ({theme}) of {club} on MysteryMixClub." ("The full mix from Mystery Mix 3" reads badly).
* **Fix the stale docstring** in `spotify_playlist.py` claiming name-keyed playlist reuse — reuse has been stored-ID (`spotify_playlist_generation.py:169`, [MYS-89](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-89/spotify-playlist-persist-playlist-id-per-round-user-instead-of-name)) and is rename-proof. Verified during planning; the rename does not break reuse.
* ~47 HTTPException `detail=` strings across `rounds.py` (~17), `leagues.py` (~20), `votes.py` (4), `submissions.py` (5), `users.py` (1): "mystery mix not found", "club not found", "the club has wrapped", "another mix is already active", … lowercase, short, calm.

## Done when

Pinned copy tests updated to exact new strings; full pytest green; manual: trigger a real staging email and generate a playlist, read both.

title: Rename R1: frontend display copy, SPA routes + redirects, legal pages
description:
First rename phase — everything a user *reads or bookmarks* in the SPA. No identifier or wire changes.

## Scope

* `App.tsx`: new routes `/clubs/:id`, `/mixes/:id`, `/clubs/new`; **permanent** redirect routes `/leagues/:id → /clubs/:id`, `/rounds/:id → /mixes/:id`, `/leagues/new → /clubs/new`. Old notification emails embed `/leagues/{id}` forever, so the redirects never get removed.
* 9 `navigate()` template call sites across 6 files → new paths.
* ~40 display strings across 9 screen files (CreateLeagueScreen, LeagueHomeScreen, MyLeaguesScreen, JoinLeagueScreen/Route, ProfileScreen, RoundDetailRoute, HomeRoute, LeagueHomeRoute): "club" / "mystery mix" in headings and prose, "mix 3 of 6" in dense chips.
* Legal + metadata: `TermsRoute.tsx` ("invite-only music club"), `PrivacyRoute.tsx` (3 mentions), `public/manifest.json` description ("…music club for close-knit friend groups").

## Explicitly out of scope

Component/type/variable names, JSON field names, `/api/v1/...` strings — all frozen until R3/R5.

## Done when

Typecheck + full frontend suite green (string assertions updated); manual staging pass: full click-through, plus pasting an old `/leagues/{id}` email URL redirects to `/clubs/{id}`.

title: Epic: Rename league → club, round → mystery mix
description:
Pre-prod naming change to make the app distinct from Music League (decided 2026-07-18). **Deep rename**: user copy, code identifiers, API routes, DB schema, living docs.

## Terms

* **league → club** everywhere: `clubs`, `club_members`, `club_id`, `/api/v1/clubs`, `/clubs/:id`.
* **round → mystery mix** in user-visible copy; internal short form is `mix`: table `mixes`, `mix_id`, `mix_number`, `/api/v1/mixes`, `/mixes/:id`. UI says "mystery mix" in headings/prose; "mix" shorthand allowed in dense chips ("mix 3 of 6").

## Shape

Six phased child tickets (R1–R6), strict order, one branch at a time, each individually non-breaking **except R5** — the fused API+DB cutover, which runs as an announced brief maintenance window on staging (live beta users) with pre-deploy backup, post-deploy verification, and a tested downgrade path.

1. R1 — frontend display copy + SPA routes/redirects + legal pages
2. R2 — backend user-visible copy (emails, playlists, error details)
3. R3 — frontend internal identifiers (wire frozen)
4. R4 — backend internal identifiers + job/systemd rename (DB names pinned)
5. R5 — cutover: API surface + DB rename, one breaking deploy + runbook
6. R6 — living docs, historical-doc terminology notes, final audit, memory/Linear closeout

Supersedes and cancels [MYS-177](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-177/epic-cohort-bout-round-restructure-post-beta) (cohort → bout restructure) — its "run it back" concept can be re-filed later under club vocabulary.

Full plan of record (naming table, copy table, runbook): session plan file 2026-07-18; key excerpts recorded on each child ticket.

title: Apple playlist link shows "Item Not Available" on mobile
description:
Found in staging testing of [MYS-108](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-108/apple-music-musickit-connect-create-round-playlist-phase-b) on 2026-07-18.

## Symptom

Tapping "open playlist in Apple Music" on mobile redirects into the Music app, which then shows **"Item Not Available"** — despite the playlist existing and being visible under Library → Playlists. Desktop works correctly.

## Cause — an Apple platform limit, not our bug

The iOS Music app **does not support deep links to library playlists**. A `/library/...` URL can open Apple Music to the Library, but no deeper: the app receives the link, can't resolve a library item from it, and reports "Item Not Available". Desktop works only because the **web player** resolves `/library/` paths.

Reshaping the URL doesn't help — `music://` instead of `https://` changes which app handles the link, not whether the app can resolve it. There is no working deep link to a library playlist. (Same root constraint as [MYS-107](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-107/apple-music-spike-can-a-library-playlist-yield-a-shareable-link): library playlists are second-class in Apple's linking model.)

The broken link is worse than no link — it reads as "we failed to create the playlist" when the playlist is fine.

## Fix (agreed with @dgabriel)

One behavior on every platform, no user-agent detection:

* Link to `https://music.apple.com/library` — opens the Library in both the mobile app and the desktop web player.
* Name the playlist in the UI so the member knows what to look for: *in your library as "<name>"*.

Requires persisting the playlist name: `apple_round_playlists` stores only `playlist_id`, and the `[revised on HH:MM]` suffix ([MYS-108](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-108/apple-music-musickit-connect-create-round-playlist-phase-b)) is a wall-clock time that cannot be recomputed later. Additive nullable column; pre-existing rows fall back to an unnamed confirmation.

## Done when

Mobile and desktop both reach the playlist without a dead end, the playlist name is shown, and no user-agent sniffing is involved.

title: Publish Terms of Service & Privacy Policy, capture consent at signup
description:
No Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, or Cookie Policy exist anywhere in the repo, and real beta users are already live on staging — we're collecting personal data (email, submissions, votes) with no posted policy and no consent record.

**Scope**

* Draft and publish a Terms of Service page and a Privacy Policy page (public routes, linked from footer/nav — see `docs/design/style-guide.md` for the about-page pattern used in [MYS-155](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-155/about-page-placeholder-scope-tbd)).
* Add a required "I agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy" checkbox to signup/invite-acceptance flows.
* Persist a timestamped consent record (policy version + timestamp) per user — needed to demonstrate consent under GDPR, not just collect it.
* Privacy Policy should disclose current data practices already implemented: aggregate-only metrics, no third-party analytics, `DELETE /users/me` cascade/right-to-be-forgotten (`docs/technical/technical-design.md` §10).

Not in scope: cookie-consent banner — our only cookies are strictly-necessary auth cookies (HttpOnly refresh token), which are generally exempt from ePrivacy consent requirements, just need disclosure in the policy text.

Filed from a 2026-07-16 compliance gap review; not previously scoped in Linear.

title: Spotify playlist improvements (placeholder — scope TBD)
description:
Placeholder ticket (same pattern as [MYS-155](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-155/about-page-placeholder-scope-tbd)): "better Spotify playlists" is named as a beta must-have, but the specific pain points still need to be confirmed with Dawn before implementation.

## Candidate scope (confirm/strike each)

- [ ] **Update-in-place** — regenerating a round's playlist should update the existing playlist rather than creating a duplicate each time
- [ ] **Naming / description / cover art** — derive playlist title + description from league name and round theme; consider generated cover art
- [ ] **Track ordering** — deliberate (or deliberately shuffled/anonymized) order instead of insertion order

- [ ] Anything else from alpha feedback

## Context

* Builds on the shipped per-user OAuth playlist flow ([MYS-83](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-83/playlist-spotify-per-user-oauth-create-saved-playlist-for-a-round))

**Next step: scope this with Dawn, then break into concrete tasks.**

title: Search relevance: wrong/irrelevant matches and wrong versions in song search
description:
Beta blocker: the Deezer-backed song search returns bad matches — wrong versions (live, karaoke, covers, re-recordings), irrelevant results, and poor ranking of the obviously-intended track.

## Symptoms (from alpha)

* Searching a well-known song surfaces covers/karaoke/live versions above or instead of the original
* Intended track ranks below noise, or doesn't appear at all despite being in the catalog

## First steps

1. Collect concrete repro queries from alpha users (query → expected track → what actually came back) and record them here
2. Audit how we call the Deezer search endpoint (query construction, params, result count) and how results are ranked/filtered before display
3. Evaluate cheap wins: penalize/flag titles containing "karaoke", "live", "cover", "tribute", "originally performed by"; prefer exact artist+title matches; surface album/artist context in the results UI so users can disambiguate

## Boundaries

* Distinct from [MYS-166](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-166/allow-submission-without-isrc-for-songs-not-in-deezer-catalog) (tracks missing from Deezer's catalog entirely — a coverage problem; this ticket is about relevance/ranking of tracks that ARE findable)
* The strategic provider question lives in [MYS-82](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-82/spike-music-metadata-provider-caching-strategy-for-progressive-scaling) (metadata-provider + caching spike); this ticket is the tactical pre-beta fix on the current stack

## Acceptance

* The collected repro queries return the intended original recording as the top result (or clearly disambiguated)
* No regression in link-paste resolution

title: Domain migration: move the app to www.mysterymixclub.com
description:
Move **production** to the real domain. Scope narrowed 2026-07-12: the domain is already owned and **staging already runs on** `staging.mysterymixclub.com` (beta testers have been using it), so DNS/registrar setup, the staging Nginx/certbot work, and likely Resend domain verification are already done. What remains is the prod cutover.

## Remaining scope (prod)

**DNS**

* Add apex + `www` records pointing at the `mysterymixclub-prod` App Platform app

**DO App Platform**

* Add custom domain(s) to the prod app; DO-managed SSL
* Decide canonical form (`www` vs apex) and redirect the other

**App config (prod env)**

* `APP_BASE_URL` — magic-link emails must point at the new domain
* `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (CORS), `VITE_API_BASE_URL`
* PWA `manifest.json` `start_url`/scope if affected
* `.do/app.prod.yaml` updated so config-as-code matches

**Third parties**

* Resend: confirm the sending domain (SPF/DKIM) is verified — likely already done for staging emails; verify prod uses it too
* Spotify developer dashboard: add the prod redirect URI (keep existing ones until cutover verified)

## Rollout notes

* Additive cutover: keep the DO-provided prod URL working until the new domain is verified end-to-end (magic-link login, Spotify connect, PWA install)

## Acceptance

* Magic-link login, Spotify OAuth, and PWA install all work on `www.mysterymixclub.com`
* Prod emails send from the verified domain and pass SPF/DKIM

title: Results: show which member voted for each song after a round closes
description:
**New top priority (2026-07-10).**

## What

On the round results view (after a round closes), show which member cast each vote for each song — i.e. attach voter identity to individual votes in the closed-round results, not just the aggregate vote count.

## Scope decision (2026-07-10)

Voting stays **fully anonymous throughout** `open_voting` — no change to the live voting experience. Voter identity is revealed **only after the round closes**, attached per song in the results view, visible to all league members (not organizer-only).

## Relationship to prior decisions — this is a deliberate reversal for closed rounds only

* [[[MYS-110](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-110/round-progress-visibility-submittedvoted-counts-no-names)]] (round progress visibility) decided **counts only, no names** — that decision stands for the *in-progress* round (`open_submission`/`open_voting`). This ticket only changes what's shown **after** the round is closed.
* [[[MYS-131](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-131/vibing-rules-votable-vibers-anonymous-voting-viewer-gated-reveal)]] / [[[MYS-68](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-68/voting-playlist-mark-the-callers-own-submission-enabler)]] established the voting playlist and vote-casting as anonymous by design (`PlaylistEntry` carries no owner field, entries shuffled). That anonymity is preserved during voting. This ticket adds a post-close reveal layer on top — it does not touch the live voting mechanics.

## Needed

* **Backend:** round results endpoint needs to return, per submission, the list of voters (user id/display name) once the round's state is `closed`. Confirm `votes` table already has voter `user_id` per vote (it should, since votes are per-voter — just not surfaced in the results response today).
* **Frontend:** results/reveal UI (`RoundDetailRoute.tsx`) surfaces voter names per song in the closed-round view.
* Consider: does this apply retroactively to already-closed rounds, or only rounds closing after this ships? (Existing vote rows have voter_id already, so retroactive should be free — confirm no anonymization/deletion of that data has happened.)

Source: user request, 2026-07-10 session.

title: Allow members who didn't submit to vote (and leave notes)
description:
Product decision (2026-07-02, found during [MYS-159](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-159/deadline-schema-submissionvoting-deadline-days-on-leagues-deadline) manual testing): a league member who has NOT submitted a song must still be able to vote and leave notes during `open_voting`. This reverses the [MYS-20](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-20/voting-system-and-just-vibing-mode) decision ("only players who are themselves Playing may vote — a member with no submission cannot vote").

## Current behavior

* **Votes**: `POST /rounds/:id/votes` 409s "submit a song before voting" (`app/api/routes/votes.py` ~line 81). The frontend already shows the voting UI to non-submitters, so they hit the 409.
* **Notes**: already allowed for any league member — no change needed.

## Fix

* Remove the no-submission 409 in `cast_votes`.
* **Vibing stays vote-less**: a submitter's stance comes from their submission's `participation_mode` (unchanged); a non-submitter's stance comes from their `league_members.vibe_mode` — vibe-mode non-submitters still can't vote (they leave notes instead).
* Frontend: `RoundDetailRoute` passes `isVibingParticipant` from the first submission's mode; for non-submitters derive it from the member's vibe flag so vibe-mode non-submitters see the sit-out message instead of a doomed ballot.
* Quorum/auto-close (`voting_quorum_met`) stays keyed on playing **submitters** — non-submitting voters are welcome but never block or force advancement. Same for the [MYS-102](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-102/show-voting-progress-x-of-y-votednoted-z-just-vibing-on-the-voting) voted-progress counts and the [MYS-162](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-162/12h-deadline-warning-email-for-approaching-round-close) voting warning email (playing submitters only).

Shipping inside PR #111 ([MYS-159](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-159/deadline-schema-submissionvoting-deadline-days-on-leagues-deadline) branch) per product request so manual testing can complete.

title: Link tab: service selector + auto-detect for Spotify, YouTube, Apple Music
description:
Beta tester request. Redesign the "paste a link" tab in `SongSearchCard` to make it clear that Spotify, YouTube, and Apple Music links are all accepted, and to default to the user's preferred streaming service.

## What

### Service selector

* Add an underline-style `<select>` (matching the TextField input spec — no box border, underline only) above the URL input, labelled `SERVICE` in label style (DM Mono, 9px, ALL CAPS, letter-spacing 0.15em, Muted).
* Options: **Spotify**, **YouTube**, **Apple Music** (no Deezer — dropped).
* Default: user's `preferred_service` from their profile, mapped to the nearest option. Fall back to Spotify if `preferred_service` is null, "deezer", or an unrecognised value.

### Placeholder adapts to selected service

| Service | Placeholder |
| -- | -- |
| Spotify | `https://open.spotify.com/track/…` |
| YouTube | `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=…` |
| Apple Music | `https://music.apple.com/…?i=…` |

Input label changes to `paste a link` (replacing the current "paste a spotify or youtube link").

### Auto-detect on paste/input

When the URL field changes, parse the hostname and snap the selector to the matching service:

* `open.spotify.com` → Spotify
* `music.apple.com` → Apple Music
* `youtube.com`, `m.youtube.com`, `music.youtube.com`, `youtu.be` → YouTube
* Unrecognised host → leave selector unchanged (backend will reject it cleanly with the existing error message)

### Helper text

Below the URL input, in Muted DM Mono 11px light weight:

> paste any link — we'll detect the service automatically

### Backend

No changes. `link_resolver.py` already dispatches all three services correctly. The selector is purely a UX affordance.

## Scope

* `SongSearchCard` only — "search by title" tab is unchanged.
* `preferred_service` is available on the auth user object; pass it as a prop `preferredService?: string | null` so the card stays decoupled from auth context.

## Style notes

* Select uses underline-only border (same spec as TextField): `border-bottom: 1px solid #D6D2CA`, transparent background, DM Mono 13px. Focus state: underline shifts to Sage.
* No Rust used in this card (existing constraint — home screen spends its Rust budget elsewhere).
* Helper text: `font-mono text-[11px] font-light text-muted`.

title: 12h deadline warning email for approaching round close
description:
Send a reminder email to players who haven't yet completed their action when a round deadline is ~12 hours away ([MYS-158](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-158>)). Runs inside the [MYS-145](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-145>) job's scan.

## Recipients (decided 2026-07-01)

* **Submission warning** (round in `open_submission`): members who haven't fully submitted — no submission at all, or submission count < `songs_per_submission`. Members who finished get nothing.
* **Voting warning** (round in `open_voting`): **playing submitters who haven't voted**. Vibers can't vote and non-submitters don't block quorum, so neither is nagged (non-submitters may vote — [MYS-167](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-167/allow-members-who-didnt-submit-to-vote-and-leave-notes) — but are never required to).
* Both respect the existing `email_notifications` preference + unsubscribe (reuse `gather_recipients` filtering / the [MYS-109](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-109/email-notifications-for-round-lifecycle-events) pipeline in `app/services/notifications.py`).

## Send rule + idempotency (updated 2026-07-02 for hour-granular windows)

* **Only when the phase window itself exceeds 12h** (`league.*_window_hours > 12`): with windows as short as 4h now allowed, a "12 hours left" email at round open is nonsense — for short windows the round-open email (which carries the deadline) is the only signal.
* Send when `0 < deadline − now ≤ 12h` **and** the per-phase stamp is unset; then set the stamp (`rounds.submission_warning_sent_at` / `voting_warning_sent_at`, added in [MYS-159](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-159>)). Stamp-based = idempotent at any cron cadence (15 min).
* Skip (don't send late) if less than ~1h remains — e.g. an organizer edited the deadline to be imminent.

## Email content

* **Submission warning:** "You have about 12 hours to submit to [Round label] in [League Name]. [Submit now →]"
* **Voting warning:** "About 12 hours left to vote in [Round label] in [League Name]. [Vote now →]"
* Note that whatever is submitted/voted by the deadline counts.

## Also in scope: deadline in the existing lifecycle emails

`_subject_and_body` in `app/services/notifications.py`: add the concrete deadline date to the "open for submissions" email (which currently says "before the deadline" with no deadline) and the "voting is open" email.

## Acceptance

* Warning sent once per phase per round to exactly the incomplete players, ~12h before deadline — and only for windows > 12h
* Not sent twice (stamp-based); not sent when <1h remains; never sent for a ≤12h window
* Lifecycle open emails include the stamped deadline
* Console sender fallback works in dev; tests cover recipient selection, idempotency, and the short-window skip

title: Round view: show submission/voting deadline as static date + live countdown
description:
Surface the round deadline to players ([MYS-158](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-158>)).

## Scope update (2026-07-02)

The **static deadline display ships early inside PR #111** (product request during [MYS-159](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-159/deadline-schema-submissionvoting-deadline-days-on-leagues-deadline) testing), in two places:

1. **Round page, top** — below the round theme/title, above the submission/vote UI: "closes Jul 5 at 9:00 PM" for the current phase (submission_deadline while open_submission, voting_deadline while open_voting), formatted in the player's browser-local time. Muted DM Mono per style guide.
2. **League page** — the active round's row/card shows the same date/time for its current phase.

No display when the deadline is NULL (legacy rounds).

## Remaining in this ticket (build after PR #111)

* **Live countdown:** "2d 14h remaining" — updates every minute client-side, next to the static date on the round page. Ticks via interval (1-min resolution), stopped on unmount.
* **"Closing soon…"** state when the deadline has passed but the cron hasn't force-advanced yet.
* The existing 60s polling ([MYS-111](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-111/auto-refresh-roundleague-state-via-60s-polling)) picks up the state change after a force-advance — no extra work.
* If an urgency treatment (<12h) is wanted, remember the Rust rule — one use per screen; check what the round view already uses before reaching for it.

## Acceptance (this ticket)

* Countdown updates without page refresh; correct across hour-granular windows (e.g. a 4h window shows "3h 12m remaining", not "0d 0h")
* No deadline = no display (no regression on legacy rounds)
* "Closing soon…" shown if deadline passed but round still open

title: League creation UI: configurable submission + voting deadline days
description:
Expose `submission_window_hours` and `voting_window_hours` in the league creation form ([MYS-158](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-158>)).

## What (updated 2026-07-02 — hour-granular windows)

Two window settings on the league creation screen (and league settings if editable post-creation), each entered as a **days + hours pair** (the API stores total hours):

* "Submission window" — how long players have to submit after a round opens. Default **3 days 0 hours** (72h).
* "Voting window" — how long players have to vote after voting opens. Default **3 days 0 hours** (72h).

## Validation

* Total window: **minimum 4 hours, maximum 168 hours (1 week)** — matches the API (`ge=4, le=168`)
* Days input 0–7, hours input 0–23; validate the combined total client-side before submit (e.g. 0d 2h → "windows need at least 4 hours"; 7d 1h → over the max)
* Any combination within bounds is fine (4 days 6 hours = 102h)

## Design

* Underline-style number inputs (design system — no border boxes), DM Mono values
* Labels ALL CAPS DM Mono 9px per label spec
* Helper text: "rounds also close early if everyone finishes" to communicate the quorum-or-deadline behaviour

## Acceptance

* League creation POST sends total hours for both windows
* Defaults pre-fill as 3d 0h; conversion days+hours → hours is correct at the boundaries (4h min, 168h max)
* Out-of-range totals blocked client-side with a calm inline message; server 422 handled gracefully anyway
* Created league stores correct values; visible in any league settings screen

title: Deadline schema: submission/voting deadline days on leagues + deadline timestamps on rounds
description:
Add the data model that underpins datetime-based round closing ([MYS-158](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-158>)).

## Rework (2026-07-02, before first deploy)

Product decision: windows are **hour-granular durations**, not whole days — min 4h, max 168h (1 week), any combination (4 days 6 hours = 102h). The days-based columns from the first pass never reached staging (PR #111 unmerged), so the migration is reworked **in place**. Local DBs that applied `c7d2e9f1a4b8` must `alembic downgrade -1 && alembic upgrade head` after pulling.

## Scope change (2026-07-01)

`rounds.submission_deadline` and `rounds.voting_deadline` **already exist** (nullable TIMESTAMPTZ) and already flow through the API and frontend types — already datetime-native, no change needed for hour granularity.

## Migrations (additive — live beta users on staging)

**leagues**

* `submission_window_hours` INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 72
* `voting_window_hours` INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 72
* Validated **4–168** at the API layer

**rounds** — notification bookkeeping so [MYS-162](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-162/12h-deadline-warning-email-for-approaching-round-close)/[MYS-145](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-145/deadline-force-advance-fallback-for-stalled-rounds) are pure logic:

* `submission_warning_sent_at` TIMESTAMPTZ NULL
* `voting_warning_sent_at` TIMESTAMPTZ NULL
* `empty_round_notice_sent_at` TIMESTAMPTZ NULL

## Logic

In `advance_round_state` (`app/api/routes/rounds.py`):

* entering `open_submission` → `submission_deadline = now + timedelta(hours=league.submission_window_hours)` (including auto-opened next rounds)
* entering `open_voting` → `voting_deadline = now + timedelta(hours=league.voting_window_hours)`
* Never clobber a non-NULL (organizer-set) deadline.

Rounds already open at migration time keep NULL deadlines — the [MYS-145](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-145/deadline-force-advance-fallback-for-stalled-rounds) job stamps them with a fresh full window on its first pass (rollout decision, see epic). A NULL deadline never force-advances.

## Acceptance

* Migration applies cleanly; existing rows get NULL stamps and 72/72 defaults
* Deadlines stamped on both transitions, including the auto-open-next-round path
* League create/read/PATCH APIs carry both window-hours fields (default 72, validated 4–168, explicit null rejected)

title: Datetime-based round closing (epic)
description:
Rounds close when quorum is reached **or** a configurable deadline passes — whichever comes first. Organizers set default deadline windows (hour-granular durations) at league creation; deadlines are stamped onto rounds when they open. Players see a static deadline and a live countdown. A 12h warning email goes to players who haven't acted. Partial submissions and votes count at deadline time.

## Child tickets — build order

1. [MYS-159](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-159>) — schema: window-hours config on leagues + warning/notice stamps on rounds (round deadline columns already exist)
2. [MYS-145](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-145>) — force-advance job + cron wiring
3. [MYS-162](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-162>) — 12h warning emails + add deadline dates to existing lifecycle emails
4. [MYS-161](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-161>) — round view: static deadline + live countdown
5. [MYS-160](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-160>) — league creation UI: deadline window fields

## Design decisions (updated 2026-07-02)

* **Windows are hour-granular durations, not whole days** (product decision 2026-07-02): min **4 hours**, max **168 hours (1 week)**, any combination (e.g. 4 days 6 hours = 102h). Stored as integer hours on leagues (`submission_window_hours` / `voting_window_hours`), default **72** (3 days). UI presents days + hours inputs.
* Deadlines are stamped when the round **enters** the state: `submission_deadline = now + submission window` at open_submission, `voting_deadline = now + voting window` at open_voting (computed from that moment, not round creation). Round deadline columns are TIMESTAMPTZ — already datetime-native.
* Stored UTC; **displayed in the player's browser-local time** — *revises the earlier "display UTC as-is" decision*
* Partial submissions/votes at deadline time count — already persisted incrementally, no freeze needed
* One cron job handles both the 12h warning scan and the force-advance scan: `app/jobs/advance_rounds.py`, systemd timer every 15 min on the staging Droplet. Prod wiring is a follow-up noted in [MYS-145](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-145/deadline-force-advance-fallback-for-stalled-rounds) (App Platform has no native cron; prod isn't live yet)
* **Rounds in flight at rollout get a fresh window.** The job stamps any open round with a NULL deadline at `now + configured window` instead of advancing it. Nobody is closed early, stalled rounds un-stick after one full window, and the job is self-healing — every open round always ends up with a deadline. A NULL deadline never force-advances.
* **Empty round at submission deadline (zero submissions): hold, don't advance.** Email the organizer once suggesting they extend the deadline or advance manually.
* 12h **submission** warning → members who haven't (fully) submitted. 12h **voting** warning → **playing submitters who haven't voted** (see also [MYS-167](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-167/allow-members-who-didnt-submit-to-vote-and-leave-notes): non-submitters may vote but never block quorum, so they aren't nagged). **Warnings only fire when the phase window itself exceeds 12h** — a "12 hours left" email makes no sense for a 4-hour round; the round-open email already carries the deadline.
* Existing "open for submissions" / "voting is open" emails get the concrete deadline date added to their copy.

## Already in place (audited 2026-07-01)

* `rounds.submission_deadline` / `voting_deadline` columns exist (nullable TIMESTAMPTZ), flow through the API and frontend types — nothing stamped or enforced them before [MYS-159](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-159/deadline-schema-submissionvoting-deadline-days-on-leagues-deadline)
* `advance_round_state` + `queue_round_event` ([MYS-69](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-69/auto-advance-round-lifecycle-when-everyone-has-acted) / [MYS-109](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-109/email-notifications-for-round-lifecycle-events)) are the single transition + notification path to plug into
* 60s polling ([MYS-111](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-111/auto-refresh-roundleague-state-via-60s-polling)) means players see a force-advance within a minute without refreshing
* Organizer manual advance override and deadline edits on open rounds already work

title: About page (placeholder — scope TBD)

Placeholder ticket for an About page. Content and scope to be defined.

Likely candidates: what MysteryMixClub is, how rounds work, supported streaming services, contact/feedback info.

title: Block duplicate ISRC within a round; warn on league repeat
description:
Prevent the same song being submitted twice in one round; surface a soft warning when a song reappears that was used in a prior round of the same league.

## Rules

**Hard block — same round (any player):**
`POST /rounds/:id/submissions` and `PATCH /rounds/:id/submissions/:sid` — if the submitted ISRC is already present in this round (by any player, including the submitter themselves in a multi-song round), return 409 with a friendly message:

> "oops, someone else has great taste too — this track is already in this round"

For the edit path, the check excludes the submission being replaced (so editing a song to itself doesn't self-block).

**Soft warning — same league, prior rounds:**
