If the ISRC has appeared in any *other* round of this league, the submission still succeeds (201/200) but `SubmissionResponse` carries `league_previously_submitted: true`. The UI surfaces a calm inline notice like "this song was submitted in a previous round — submitted anyway."

## Build

**Backend (**`submissions.py`**):**

* Add `league_previously_submitted: bool` to `SubmissionResponse` (default `false`)
* In `submit_song`: before committing, query `submissions` for the ISRC in this round → 409 if found. Then query for ISRC in any other round of this league → set flag.
* In `edit_song`: same checks, excluding the current `submission_id` from the round-level query.

**Frontend (**`RoundDetailRoute.tsx`**,** `api.ts`**):**

* Add `league_previously_submitted: boolean` to `SubmissionResult`
* After a successful submit/edit, if the flag is set, show a calm inline notice below the submission list

## Done when

Both hard block (409) and soft warning (league repeat) work end-to-end with tests.

title: Results UI: per-player grouping + tests
description:
`frontend/src/pages/RoundDetailRoute.tsx` results section. The leaderboard arrives already aggregated per player (from the voting+results child); each reveal tile still shows its song's own vote count. Optionally group a player's songs visually so a multi-song player reads as one entrant.

Tests: results rendering with a multi-song player (one leaderboard row, multiple reveal tiles). Blocked by the voting+results child.

title: Submit screen: multi-song add/edit/remove manager
description:
`frontend/src/pages/RoundDetailRoute.tsx` submit section → a small list manager: show your songs, add up to the cap (hide "add" at cap), edit and remove each. At cap 1 it collapses to today's single edit-in-place (parity).

`frontend/src/services/api.ts` — `getMySubmission` → list; add `deleteSubmission` / `editSubmission`.

Tests: `RoundDetailRoute.test.tsx` — add/edit/remove, cap enforcement (no add at cap), cap==1 parity. Blocked by the submission-API child.

title: League setup UI: songs-per-submission stepper (1–5)
description:
`frontend/src/pages/CreateLeagueScreen.tsx` — add a songs-per-submission stepper (1–5, default 1), beside the existing `votes_per_player`/`total_rounds` controls. Design-system compliant (DM Mono, underline input, no extra Rust).

`frontend/src/services/api.ts` — add `songs_per_submission` to league create payload + response types.

Tests: `CreateLeagueScreen` / `CreateLeagueRoute.test.tsx` cover the new field + default. Blocked by the schema child (response shape).

title: Voting + results: per-player-total leaderboard + distinct-submitter counts
description:
`backend/app/api/routes/rounds.py` + `votes.py`.

* **Leaderboard** (`get_round_results`): aggregate by `user_id`, summing `vote_count` across a user's submissions → one `LeaderboardEntry` per player. The `submissions` list keeps per-song `vote_count`.
* **Vibing-viewer** `winners`: recompute from per-player totals (not per-song) to match the leaderboard. `picks` stays the full per-song tracklist.
* `_submission_count` (and the grouped count in `list_rounds`): count distinct `user_id`, not rows — fixes [MYS-101](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-101/show-submission-progress-x-of-y-players-submitted-on-the-round-league) "X of Y submitted".
* [**votes.py**](<http://votes.py>): `own_submission` lookup now matches multiple rows → existence/`limit(1)` check. Self-vote prevention already covers all of the voter's songs. `votes_per_player` unchanged.
* Playlist: no structural change (user-id sets already).

Blocked by the schema + submission-API children. Done when: per-player sum, distinct-count, and self-vote tests pass.

title: Submission API: multi-song CRUD + cap enforcement + uniform vibe mode
description:
`backend/app/api/routes/submissions.py` — move from single replace-in-place to a per-song collection. Capture the league from `_load_league_as_member` (currently discarded) to read the cap.

* `POST /rounds/:id/submissions` — add a song. 201 on create; 409 "you've submitted the maximum of N songs" when already at `songs_per_submission`. Drops the old replace branch.
* `PATCH /rounds/:id/submissions/:sid` — edit one of your songs (track + note); re-assemble `platform_links`/`youtube_video_id`. Ownership + `open_submission` checks.
* `DELETE /rounds/:id/submissions/:sid` — remove one (ownership + open). Allowed down to zero.
* `GET /rounds/:id/submissions/mine` — returns `list[SubmissionResponse]` (was single + 404); empty list when none.
* `participation_mode` uniform per player per round: resolve as today (payload override → member `vibe_mode`) and apply to all of the player's rows on every add/edit.

Blocked by the schema child. Done when: cap 409, multi-song mine list, delete, and uniform-mode tests pass.

title: Multi-song schema: leagues.songs_per_submission + drop submission unique constraint
description:
Foundation for [MYS-116](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-116/songs-per-submission-admin-configurable-per-league-cap-default-1-max-5).

* `backend/app/models/league.py` — add `songs_per_submission: int` (NOT NULL, default 1, `server_default text("1")`), mirroring the existing `votes_per_player` column. Not denormalized onto `rounds` (fixed league-wide value; the submit path already loads the league).
* `backend/app/models/submission.py` — remove `UniqueConstraint("round_id", "user_id", name="uq_submissions_round_user")`. Per-column indexes on `round_id`/`user_id` already cover lookups.
* New Alembic migration: add the league column; drop the submissions unique constraint.

Done when: migration applies on local Postgres, existing single-song rounds still read (cap defaults to 1), `mypy app` + `pytest` green.

title: Join league page is missing the top nav
description:
**Manual test finding (P1).** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

`/invite/:token` and `/join/:token` (`JoinLeagueRoute`) are registered **outside** the `AuthedLayout` group in `App.tsx` (it's a public route so logged-out visitors can preview), so the screen has **no** `TopNav`. An authenticated user following an invite lands on a nav-less page.

## Fix

Show the shared `TopNav` on the join screen **when the viewer is authenticated** (keep it absent for logged-out previews, where there's no session to drive it). Either render `TopNav` conditionally within `JoinLeagueScreen`/`JoinLeagueRoute` on `isAuthenticated`, or wrap the authed case. Keep the logged-out preview unchanged.

title: Closed round: vibers should see the submitted songs (no scores)
description:
**Manual test finding (P1).** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`. Refines the [MYS-112](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-112/define-andquotjust-vibingandquot-behavior-decision-unblock-vibing-ui) reveal gating.

Today a vibing viewer's closed reveal is trimmed to winner(s) + Most Noted + their own song (`submissions` comes back empty from `get_round_results`). [MYS-133](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-133/closed-round-the-playlist-listen-affordance-disappears) added a "listen back" whole-mix link, so a viber can hear the mix but still can't **see the tracklist**.

**Decision (2026-06-26):** a vibing viewer should see the **full song list** on the closed reveal — title, artist, submitter, and notes — **but no vote counts and no leaderboard** ("notes, not votes / no rankings" still holds).

## Implementation

* Backend `get_round_results`: for a vibing viewer, return the picks as a **vibe-safe shape without** `vote_count` (e.g. a new `picks: list[RevealPick]` field: submission_id, submitter_display_name, title, artist, submitter_note, notes), ordered neutrally (e.g. title asc). Keep `leaderboard` empty and `submissions` empty; keep `winners` + `most_noted`. (This can replace the `own_submission` field added in [MYS-131](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-131/vibing-rules-votable-vibers-anonymous-voting-viewer-gated-reveal) — the viber's own song is in the picks.)
* Frontend `VibingReveal`: render winner(s) + the picks list (no scores) + Most Noted.
* Update the [MYS-112](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-112/define-andquotjust-vibingandquot-behavior-decision-unblock-vibing-ui) decision text in `docs/prd/prd.md` + `docs/technical/technical-design.md` (viber reveal now includes the unscored song list).

Server-side gating still applies: vote counts/leaderboard must not be sent to a viber.

title: Closed round: the playlist / listen affordance disappears
description:
**Manual test finding (P1).** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

Once a round closes, there's **no way to listen to the mix**. The whole-mix YouTube/Spotify playlist links and the per-song platform links only render inside `VotingSection` (open_voting). The closed-round reveal (`ResultsSection` in `frontend/src/pages/RoundDetailRoute.tsx`) shows titles / artists / notes / scores but **no listen affordance** — no playlist and no per-song platform links.

## Steps

1. Open a round that's `closed`.
2. The reveal lists the songs but offers no way to play them.

## Expected

The reveal keeps a listen path: the whole-mix playlist (YouTube + Spotify, as on the voting screen) and/or per-song platform links on each pick card, so members can replay the round.

## Actual

No playlist, no platform links on the closed view.

## Notes

`GET /rounds/:id/playlist` is gated to non-`open_submission` states, so it already serves closed rounds — the closed view can reuse it (or surface per-song `platforms` on the results payload). Decide whether to fetch the playlist on the closed view or add platform links to the results response.

title: Vibing viewer can't leave notes on the open-voting playlist
description:
**Manual test finding (P1).** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

A player who is **just vibing** for a round sits voting out, but per the [MYS-112](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-112/define-andquotjust-vibingandquot-behavior-decision-unblock-vibing-ui) decision they can still **listen and optionally leave notes**. On the open-voting screen they currently can't: the vibing-viewer branch of `VotingSection` (`frontend/src/pages/RoundDetailRoute.tsx`) renders each song as a plain `Card` (title / artist / platform links) with **no** `SongNotes` **affordance**. The playing-voter branch has it; the vibing branch doesn't.

## Steps

1. Be a vibing participant in a round that's in `open_voting`.
2. Open the round → you see the playlist but no "leave a note" control on any song.

## Expected

Each song in the vibing viewer's playlist exposes the same notes affordance (read notes + leave-a-note composer) the playing voters get — leaving notes is a viber's main way to participate.

## Actual

No notes affordance at all for a vibing viewer.

## Fix sketch

Add `<SongNotes …>` to each card in the `isVibingParticipant` branch of `VotingSection`, mirroring the playing branch. Confirm the notes API allows a vibing member to post (it should — notes are participation-mode-agnostic).

title: Global top navigation bar (home / profile / logout + contextual league link)
description:
A persistent top nav bar on all authenticated screens.

* Left: concentric-ring logo mark → home (My Leagues). Right: HOME, PROFILE, LOGOUT (logout calls existing logout()).
* On a round screen, show a "← LEAGUE" contextual link back to that round's league home.
* If the user is a platform admin (is_platform_admin), keep the ADMIN entry in the bar (absorb the existing MyLeaguesScreen admin nav entry into the shared bar).
* Authenticated screens only (not login/verify/onboarding/invite-preview).
* Strict design system: DM Mono ALL CAPS, Sage/Ink, line icons, NO Rust (nav must not consume the screen's single Rust signal). Slim/quiet/compact.

Shared <TopNav> component. Frontend-only. Tests: links render + route correctly; ← LEAGUE only on round screens; admin entry gated; logout works; no Rust introduced.

title: Bare-bones profile screen (edit display name + archived leagues)
description:
A minimal profile screen at /profile.

* Edit display name (PATCH /users/me — already supported via updateDisplayName). Underline input, calm save, inline confirm.
* "Archived leagues" section: the user's COMPLETED leagues (state === "complete"), shown as a linkable list → league home. Sourced from the existing getLeagues() (no backend change); filter complete vs active.
* Design-system compliant; one Rust signal max.

Frontend-only. Tests: rename happy path + validation; archived list renders completed leagues and links through.

title: Platform-admin hard-delete user + organizer kick UI
description:
Let a platform-admin eject bad actors globally; surface the existing organizer league-kick in the UI.

* Refactor app/jobs/purge_accounts.py: extract hard_delete_users(db, user_ids, emails) (FK-safe cascade); purge job + admin endpoint both reuse it.
* auth/deps.py: get_platform_admin — current user whose email is in SEED_ADMIN_EMAILS, else 403. (seed_admin_emails repurposed from a login gate to platform-admin identity.)
* app/api/routes/admin.py: GET /admin/users?email=<substr> (find target); DELETE /admin/users/{id} → hard-delete (404 missing, 409 self-delete), 204.
* /users/me: add is_platform_admin so the UI can gate the admin nav.
* Frontend: thin platform-admin-only /admin page (email search → hard-delete with confirm; single Rust signal). Ensure organizer "remove from league" (existing remove_member) is wired in the members list.

Tests: get_platform_admin authz; hard-delete cascade zero-orphans + sessions killed; 404/409; non-admin 403; is_platform_admin correct.

No email re-signup blocklist for now (re-delete if a banned user returns via a fresh link).

title: Invite-gated sign-up + global user cap (1500)
description:
New accounts can only be created by someone arriving through a valid invite link; existing users always log in. Cap total users at 1500.

* config: MAX_USERS (default 1500; 0 = unlimited) + .env.example.
* /auth/request: optional invite_token. Send a magic link only if the email is an existing non-deleted user OR a valid unexpired invite_token is presented; otherwise neutral no-send (anti-bot + anti-enumeration). When sending with an invite, append &invite=<token> to the verify link.
* /auth/verify: optional invite query param. Existing user → log in (and join the invite's league if present). New user → require a valid unexpired invite (else 403 "you need an invite to create an account") AND enforce cap: 403 "at capacity" if count(non-deleted users) >= MAX_USERS; otherwise create + join.
* Shared _join_via_invite helper reused by accept_invite and verify.
* Frontend: pass invite token through request + verify; calm 403 capacity / 403 invite-required / 410 expired states.

Tests: send-gating matrix; new-user-only-with-invite; cap blocks new but not existing; auto-join; idempotent re-login.

(Supersedes the email-allowlist approach from canceled [MYS-125](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-125/player-admin-email-invites-invite-only-login-allowlist).)

title: Invite links expire after 48h
description:
Shareable invite links become invalid 48h after creation.

* create_invite sets expires_at = now + 48h (no schema change; invites.expires_at already exists, legacy NULL = non-expiring).
* preview_invite + accept_invite return 410 "this invite link has expired" when expires_at is in the past.
* Frontend JoinLeague flow renders the expired state calmly ("ask the organizer for a new one").

Tests: ~48h expiry on create; 410 on expired preview/accept; valid + legacy-NULL links still work.

(Supersedes part of canceled [MYS-125](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-125/player-admin-email-invites-invite-only-login-allowlist); part of the shareable-link access-control rework.)

title: Player admin: email invites + invite-only login allowlist
description:
Pivot invites from anonymous shareable links to email-addressed invites, add an organizer admin tool, and gate login on an allowlist.

**Data model** (`invites` + migration): add `email TEXT NULL` (null = legacy link) and `accepted_at TIMESTAMP NULL`; partial unique index on `(league_id, email) WHERE email IS NOT NULL`. Make `token` nullable; keep generating one for backward-compat with the accept route.

**Config:** `SEED_ADMIN_EMAILS` (comma-separated) + `.env.example` entry.

**Email:** add `send_invite(email, league_name, accept_url)` to EmailSender + all impls.

**Routes (**`/leagues/{id}/invites`**):**

* `POST` accepts `{"emails": [...]}` (1..N); normalize/validate, dedupe vs existing invites + active members, create rows, send invite emails; return per-email result (created | already_invited | already_member).
* `GET` organizer-only guest list: email, has_account, display_name|null, is_member, invited_at, accepted_at.
* `DELETE /{invite_id}` organizer-only: revoke invite + soft-remove matching membership. Never deletes the global account.

**Login allowlist (**`/auth/request`**):** allow if email is a seed-admin OR an existing non-deleted user OR holds any invite. Otherwise return the same neutral response with no token created and no email sent (no enumeration leak).

**Auto-join on first login (**`/auth/verify`**):** after resolving/creating the user, join every league with an unaccepted invite for their email and stamp `accepted_at`. Idempotent.

**Frontend:** organizer admin panel on league home — single/bulk email add + guest table (email · account? · username · status · revoke). Strict design-system compliance.

**Tests:** bulk create + dedupe + per-email result shape; guest-list shape; revoke removes membership but not account; allowlist (invited/existing/seed allowed, stranger neutral-no-send); auto-join on verify (idempotent, accepted_at stamped).

Decision log: login gate = invited OR existing user OR seed-admin; auto-join on first login; admin "delete user" scoped to remove-from-league + revoke-invite (not global); delete-league blocks in-flight.

title: Delete a league (organizer-only, cascade)
description:
Add the ability for a league organizer to delete a league.

**Endpoint:** `DELETE /api/v1/leagues/{league_id}` → 204

**Authorization:** organizer-only (reuse `_load_league_as_organizer`).

**Guardrail:** return 409 if the league is in-flight — `state == "active" and current_round > 0` ("can't delete a league that's in progress"). Allowed when not-yet-started (`current_round == 0`) or `state == "complete"`.

**Cascade** (FKs have no ON DELETE CASCADE) in dependency order within one transaction:
votes → notes → submissions → rounds → invites → league_members → league.

**Frontend:** organizer-only "delete league" action on the league home with a confirm step (calm copy per style guide; destructive confirm is the screen's single Rust signal). On success, navigate to My Leagues.

**Tests:** 401 unauth, 403 non-organizer, 404 missing, 409 in-flight, 204 + no orphan rows for both a not-started and a complete league.

title: Email deliverability: verify SPF/DKIM/DMARC + per-env Resend config before relying on prod email
description:
**Deployment/DNS checklist — gates whether** [MYS-109](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-109/email-notifications-for-round-lifecycle-events) **emails actually land** (vs. spam/undelivered). Mostly dashboard + DNS work, not code. The `List-Unsubscribe` header is already handled in code ([MYS-109](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-109/email-notifications-for-round-lifecycle-events), PR #65).

## Confirm / set up

**Domain authentication (the core "not spam" signals) on** `mysterymixclub.com`**:**

- [ ] **SPF** TXT present and covers Resend's sending (custom MAIL FROM subdomain). Likely already set since magic links send.
- [ ] **DKIM** record present (Resend-provided CNAME/TXT) and verified.
- [ ] **DMARC** record at `_dmarc.mysterymixclub.com` (this is the one most likely missing — SPF/DKIM are required to verify a domain in Resend, DMARC is added separately). Start at `p=none` with a `rua=` reporting address, tighten later.

**Sender identity:**

- [ ] Confirm Resend domain verification covers the new `notifications@mysterymixclub.com` from-address (same domain as the working `login@`, so likely fine — verify).

**Per-environment config:**

- [ ] `RESEND_API_KEY` set in **staging** and **prod** (App Platform spec + DO dashboard). Without it the app falls back to `ConsoleEmailSender` (logs only, no real send).
- [ ] `API_BASE_URL` set in staging + prod specs so the unsubscribe link/header points at the API host (falls back to `APP_BASE_URL` — the frontend host — otherwise).

## Context

Google/Yahoo bulk-sender rules (Feb 2024) require SPF + DKIM + DMARC + one-click `List-Unsubscribe` + low complaint rate. We're low-volume, but meeting the bar is the right call. One-click unsubscribe (`List-Unsubscribe` / `List-Unsubscribe-Post`) ships with [MYS-109](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-109/email-notifications-for-round-lifecycle-events).

## Done when

A test round transition delivers a real email to an external inbox (Gmail) that passes SPF/DKIM/DMARC (check "show original") and shows Gmail's native unsubscribe affordance.

title: 3-step help overlays per page (+ info-icon replay)
description:
3-step help overlay per key page, dismissable, replayable via an info icon in TopNav. **Design decided 2026-07-12** (interactive mockup attached; all decisions product-owner approved). Beta ships phases 1+2 with static vignettes; the animation pass is a follow-up ticket.

## Decided design

**Scope: four overlays** — `home` (MyLeagues), `league` (LeagueHomeScreen), `round-submit`, `round-vote` (RoundDetail keyed by phase). Create/join/profile and pending/closed round states get none; the reveal is never interrupted.

**Pattern: centered modal, 3 steps paged inside one dialog** — reuses the app's existing modal surface (leave-blocker in RoundDetailRoute: Ink/40 scrim + bordered Cream panel).

**Anatomy** (per the mockup):

* Panel: bg-cream, 1px Border, radius 3px, padding 24px, max-w-sm
* Eyebrow "how this page works" (Label 9px caps Muted) + ✕ (16px line icon, Muted→Ink, 44px hit area)
* Vignette area 96px (static inline SVGs for beta; Sage/Ink/Border line style)
* Title: DM Serif Display 22px Ink; body: DM Mono 13px/300 **Ink** (not Muted — Muted on Cream fails AA at 13px)
* Step indicator: single 20px concentric-ring glyph, rings fill Sage inward per step, paired with "N of 3" Label + aria-live — the overlay's one motif use
* Buttons: primary Sage `next` → `got it`; muted underline `back` on steps 2–3; ✕/ESC/scrim-click all dismiss and all count as seen
* **Rust: none in overlay chrome. One approved exception:** the round-vote step-2 vignette teaches the rust "voted" card state (product-owner signed off 2026-07-12)

**Behavior**: auto-open once per overlay id ~400ms after screen data resolves; round overlays fire on first round seen in that phase; ⓘ in TopNav (rightmost, renders only when the screen registers an overlay — reuse the AuthedLayout outlet-context pattern) replays anytime. Focus trap, initial focus on primary button, focus returns to invoker, body scroll locked, prefers-reduced-motion honored (static frames).

**Persistence**: localStorage `mmc.help.<userId>.<overlayId>` = content version string; bump version to re-show after material copy changes. No backend change.

**Copy**: final drafts live in the mockup (all 4 overlays × 3 steps) — use verbatim.

## Build phases

1. `HelpOverlay` component + persistence util + `useHelpOverlay` hook + TopNav ⓘ + `home`/`league` overlays (static vignettes)
2. `round-submit`/`round-vote` overlays + phase-keyed auto-show
3. Animation pass — **split to follow-up ticket, post-beta**

## Done when (beta scope)

All four overlays show once per user/page, replay from the ⓘ, pass the accessibility checklist (dialog semantics, focus trap, ESC, reduced-motion, ≥44px targets), and frontend tests cover persistence + step navigation.

title: Songs per submission: admin-configurable per-league cap (default 1, max 5)
description:
**Epic.** Let an admin allow more than one song per player per round. The cap is chosen **once at league setup** (`leagues.songs_per_submission`, default 1, min 1, max 5) and applies to every round in that league.

Supersedes the original "needs a mini-PRD" framing — PRD is below. [MYS-122](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-122/andquotsetandquot-submission-two-related-songs-back-to-back-on-the) (ordered 2-song "sets") is a later layer that stays blocked on this.

## Locked product decisions

1. **Cap location:** per-league, fixed at creation. No per-round override.
2. **Scoring:** per-player total — sum a player's votes across their songs → one leaderboard row per player. The reveal still shows each song's own vote count.
3. **Vote budget:** `votes_per_player` is untouched and independent of the cap.
4. **Cap = a maximum, not a quota:** a player must submit ≥1 and may submit up to the cap. At cap 1 everything behaves exactly like today (backward-compatible).

## Structural heart

Drop the `uq_submissions_round_user` unique constraint; submissions become a small per-player collection (add/edit/delete up to the cap); leaderboard aggregates by player. `participation_mode` (vibing) stays uniform across a player's songs.

## Children

1. Multi-song schema: `leagues.songs_per_submission` + drop submission unique constraint
2. Submission API: multi-song CRUD + cap enforcement + uniform vibe mode
3. Voting + results: per-player-total leaderboard + distinct-submitter counts
4. League setup UI: songs-per-submission stepper (1–5)
5. Submit screen: multi-song add/edit/remove manager
6. Results UI: per-player grouping + tests

## Watch-outs

* [MYS-101](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-101/show-submission-progress-x-of-y-players-submitted-on-the-round-league) "X of Y submitted" must switch from counting submission *rows* to distinct *players*, or it reads wrong.
* [MYS-69](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-69/auto-advance-round-lifecycle-when-everyone-has-acted) (auto-advance, not yet built): "has submitted" = distinct players with ≥1 song.

Full implementation plan lives with the author (plan: eager-booping-crane).

title: Email notifications for round lifecycle events
description:
From the ideas list (`docs/idea-scratch.md`). **Priority raised per product (2026-06-22).** Email-only here; SMS is split into its own ticket (heavier — new vendor/opt-in).

## Why now / what exists

Technical-design §3 already lists Resend for "round notifications," and the infra is partly built: `app/services/email.py` has a `ResendEmailSender` + `ConsoleEmailSender` dev fallback, but the `EmailSender` protocol only exposes `send_magic_link`. So sending works; we need to generalize it and hook it to events.

## Build

* **Generalize the sender** beyond `send_magic_link` (e.g. a `send(to, subject, html)` + per-notification templates), keeping the console fallback for dev.
* **Event hooks** on round/league transitions (`rounds.py` lifecycle, see technical-design §6): round opens for submission, voting opens, round closes / results ready, league complete. Fire to the right members (respect membership; skip removed members).
* **User preference + unsubscribe** — a per-user notifications toggle (account/settings; relates to [MYS-61](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-61/no-profilesettings-screen-preferred-service-account-deletion) settings screen) and an unsubscribe link. Don't email without consent.
* **Idempotency / no dupes** — a state transition fires its email once even if the transition is retried/auto-advanced (interplays with [MYS-69](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-69/auto-advance-round-lifecycle-when-everyone-has-acted) auto-advance).

## Out of scope

SMS notifications (separate ticket); inbound email/SMS submissions (separate); digesting/batching beyond per-event.

## Done when

Members receive a clean templated email on each lifecycle event, gated by their preference, with working unsubscribe, plus tests for the event→email mapping and the console fallback.

title: Apple Music: MusicKit connect + create round playlist (Phase B)
description:
**Phase B — the Apple playlist feature** (spike: [MYS-79](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-79/spike-apple-music-integration-links-playlist-generation), `docs/discovery/spike-apple-music.md` §3.2, §4, §7). Mirrors the Spotify flow ([MYS-83](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-83/playlist-spotify-per-user-oauth-create-saved-playlist-for-a-round)) but with Apple's two-token auth.

## What to build

A "Connect Apple Music" → "create this round's playlist" flow.

* **Client-side auth (the key difference from Spotify):** integrate **MusicKit JS**, configure it with our developer token ([MYS-105](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-105/apple-music-developer-token-service-es256-jwt-signing)), and call `authorize()` (Apple sign-in **popup**) to mint the **Music User Token (MUT)**. Relay the MUT to the backend.
* **Backend create-then-add:** with `Authorization: Bearer <developer_token>` + `Music-User-Token: <MUT>`:
  * `POST /v1/me/library/playlists` (name = round/league title, like the Spotify naming from [MYS-86](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-86/spotify-playlist-include-league-name-in-the-playlist-title)).
  * `POST /v1/me/library/playlists/{id}/tracks` (append-only; no reorder). Track ids from the ISRC catalog lookup ([MYS-106](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-106/apple-music-isrc-catalog-matching-upgrade-in-song-linkspy-phase-a)).
* **Surface the result link per** [MYS-107](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-107/apple-music-spike-can-a-library-playlist-yield-a-shareable-link)**'s finding** — a shared link if available, otherwise "playlist created in your library."
* Reuse the round→track-resolution + "unmatched tracks" handling from the broader playlist work ([MYS-76](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-76/spike-auto-generate-streaming-playlists-youtube-deezer-spotify-as) §9).
* Token handling server-side where possible; handle MUT expiry/revocation → re-auth.

## Done when

A subscribed user can connect Apple Music and generate the round's playlist into their library end-to-end, with backend + frontend tests and graceful handling of unmatched tracks and auth failures.

title: Apple Music: spike — can a library playlist yield a shareable link?
description:
**Spike — decides the shape of the Apple playlist build (**[MYS-108](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-108/apple-music-musickit-connect-create-round-playlist-phase-b)**)** ([MYS-79](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-79/spike-apple-music-integration-links-playlist-generation), `docs/discovery/spike-apple-music.md` §4, §6). Small; do before the UI.

## The open question

Spotify/Deezer return a **public, shareable** playlist URL. Apple **library** playlists live in the user's own library and historically do **not** reliably expose a public `share`/`url` in the API response — possibly only a `music.apple.com/library/...` link that opens just for that signed-in user.

## Investigate

* Create a test library playlist (needs developer token [MYS-105](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-105/apple-music-developer-token-service-es256-jwt-signing) + a Music User Token) and inspect the response/relationships for any **public/shareable URL**.
* Determine what link, if any, we can surface to *other* players vs. only the owner.

## Outcome decides [MYS-108](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-108/apple-music-musickit-connect-create-round-playlist-phase-b)'s scope

* **If shareable:** "one shared mix link," like Spotify/Deezer.
* **If owner-only:** scope [MYS-108](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-108/apple-music-musickit-connect-create-round-playlist-phase-b) as **"each player generates the playlist in their own library"** (still useful) — not a single shared link. Do **not** promise a shareable mix link until this is confirmed.

## Done when

We have a definitive answer (with evidence) on the shareable-link question, recorded back on [MYS-79](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-79/spike-apple-music-integration-links-playlist-generation)'s findings doc or here.

title: Apple Music: developer-token service (ES256 JWT signing)
description:
**Foundation for all Apple Music API calls** (spike: [MYS-79](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-79/spike-apple-music-integration-links-playlist-generation), `docs/discovery/spike-apple-music.md` §3.1, §8). Server-side only.

## What to build

A service that mints and caches the Apple Music **developer token** — an **ES256 JWT** signed with the MusicKit `.p8` private key.

* Claims: `iss` = Team ID, `kid` = Key ID (JWT header), `iat`, `exp` ≤ 180 days, `alg: ES256`.
* Read credentials from env (`APPLE_MUSIC_TEAM_ID`, `APPLE_MUSIC_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_MUSIC_PRIVATE_KEY`) per [MYS-104](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-104/apple-music-approve-apple-developer-program-dollar99yr-provision).
* Cache the token in-process; refresh before expiry (rotate well under the 180-day cap).
* Used as `Authorization: Bearer <developer_token>` on Apple Music API calls. **The** `.p8` **never leaves the server.**
* Follow the single-file-boundary pattern of `app/services/odesli.py` / `song_links.py`.

## Done when

The service returns a valid developer token (verifiable against an authenticated Apple Music API catalog read), with unit tests for the JWT claims/signing and cache/refresh behavior.

title: Apple Music: approve Apple Developer Program (~$99/yr) + provision MusicKit credentials
description:
**Blocks all Apple Music API work** (spike: [MYS-79](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-79/spike-apple-music-integration-links-playlist-generation), `docs/discovery/spike-apple-music.md` §3, §6, §8). This is a product/budget decision plus a manual provisioning step — not a code task.

## Decision

Approve the **Apple Developer Program membership (\~$99/yr)**. It is the prerequisite for *any* Apple Music API capability, including the developer-token-only matching upgrade.

## Provisioning (manual, in the Apple Developer portal)

* Enroll in the Apple Developer Program.
* Note the **Team ID**.
* Certificates, IDs & Profiles → Keys → **+** → enable **Media Services (MusicKit)** → download the `.p8` **private key** (one-time download). The Key ID is the last 10 chars of the filename.
* Store the `.p8` as a **server secret** (per technical-design §11 env pattern). Add the contract keys to `.env.example` (no values): `APPLE_MUSIC_TEAM_ID`, `APPLE_MUSIC_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_MUSIC_PRIVATE_KEY` (the `.p8` contents). Set real values via the deploy secret stores (GitHub Actions + DO), never committed.

## Done when

Membership is active and the three credentials exist as deploy secrets, unblocking the developer-token service.

title: Song paste-link resolves to the wrong song
description:
**Manual test finding (P1) — correctness bug.** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

Pasting a **direct** track link resolved to a **different song**.

**Repro:** pasted `https://open.spotify.com/track/2v05RhwIQx3zbN8O72Ff69` → got **"Serpentskirt"** instead of **"Serpents"**.

Likely cause: the keyless resolver (post-Odesli, [MYS-81](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-81/migrate-off-odesli-public-api-before-it-is-retired-2026-07-31) — `backend/app/services/link_resolver.py` / `song_links.py`) isn't honoring the Spotify **track id** in the URL and instead falls back to a title/artist search that mis-hits. A pasted link with a specific track id should resolve to *that* track. Investigate the Spotify-link path of the resolver.

title: Spotify playlist: reuse same-named playlist instead of creating duplicates (idempotent generate)
description:
**Found in** [MYS-83](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-83/playlist-spotify-per-user-oauth-create-saved-playlist-for-a-round) **manual testing.** We don't record the playlists we create (no id stored), so every "make a spotify playlist" click spawns a **brand-new** playlist in the user's library — duplicates pile up.

**Want:** before creating, look up the user's playlists for one with the **same name**; if found, **reuse it** (replace its tracks) instead of creating a new one. Do this on every generate.

## Approach

* `find_playlist_id_by_name(access_token, name)` — paginate `GET /me/playlists`, return the id of an exact-name match (or None).
* If found → `PUT /playlists/{id}/items` to **replace** contents with the current matched URIs (idempotent: regenerate = current mix, no dupe tracks). Else → create + add as today.

## Correctness dependency — folds in [MYS-86](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-86/spotify-playlist-include-league-name-in-the-playlist-title)

Dedup keys on the playlist **name**, so the name must be **unique per round**. Today it's `MysteryMixClub — Round N: Theme` with **no league** → two leagues with the same round/theme would collide and overwrite each other. So this includes [MYS-86](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-86/spotify-playlist-include-league-name-in-the-playlist-title) (league name in title): `MysteryMixClub: {League}, {theme}` (fall back to `Round N` when no theme). Closes [MYS-86](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-86/spotify-playlist-include-league-name-in-the-playlist-title).

## Reference

`backend/app/services/spotify_client.py` (`create_playlist`/`add_tracks` + new `find_playlist_id_by_name`/`replace_tracks`), `app/services/spotify_playlist.py` (`playlist_name`), `app/api/routes/spotify.py` (`create_round_spotify_playlist`).

title: Migrate off Odesli public API before it is retired (2026-07-31)
description:
**Hard deadline: 2026-07-31.** Odesli is retiring its public SongLink API (`v1-alpha.1` on `api.song.link` / `api.odesli.co`). After that date all requests return **410 Gone**. Between now and then it runs under stricter per-IP daily rate limits (429 on excess). Announced 2026-05-21. (Source: Odesli/Linktree help — "Sunsetting the Songlink (Odesli) public API".)

## Impact on us

`POST /api/v1/songs/resolve` — the paste-a-link flow — calls keyless `OdesliClient.resolve()` for song identity (`app/routers/songs.py`). **On 2026-08-01 that flow breaks (410).**

Unaffected: the Deezer search flow (`GET /songs/search`) and cross-service link assembly (`song_links.py`, keyless Deezer + iTunes) — neither touches Odesli.

Also worth noting: keyless Odesli is *already* degraded — verified it returns only long-tail platforms (no youtube/spotify/apple) from a Deezer or Apple source, which is what blocked the original [MYS-78](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-78/playlist-one-click-youtube-playlist-link-for-a-round-watch-videos-no) approach.

## Replacement approach (keyless, sunset-proof)

Replace Odesli's identity-resolution role with **iTunes Search + Deezer** — both keyless and already in the codebase:

* Deezer search → title / artist / **ISRC**.
* iTunes Search → Apple identity + `trackViewUrl` (no ISRC, so pair with Deezer for ISRC).
  Then drop the `OdesliClient` dependency from the resolve path.

## Alternative (keep Odesli)

Odesli offers a partner **allowlist** (application form) for continued, keyed API access. Higher risk: approval/timing uncertain and it's an ongoing dependency on a service that just retired its public tier. Only pursue if we specifically need Odesli's cross-matching.

## Out of scope

YouTube-playlist video-id resolution ([MYS-78](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-78/playlist-one-click-youtube-playlist-link-for-a-round-watch-videos-no)) — that needs the YouTube Data API; neither Odesli nor iTunes can supply YouTube video ids.

title: Auto-advance round lifecycle when everyone has acted
description:
Advance a round's state automatically instead of relying on the organizer:

1. Open voting once every player has submitted a song.
2. Close the round and advance the league once every player has voted.

**Resolved design (2026-06-21):**

* **Quorum = members active when the round opened.** Late joiners do not block advancement. Vibing players don't vote, so they don't count toward the voting quorum (but do count toward the submission quorum).
* The **organizer keeps a manual override** to advance early.
* **Deadlines still force-advance** on time even if the quorum isn't met (stalled-round fallback).

Combines two manual-test findings (auto-open voting + auto-close/advance). Build-ready.

Source: manual testing (`docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`), 2026-06-21.

title: Voting: action buttons show a bare "…" busy label
description:
On the round voting screen, action buttons swap their label to a bare ellipsis (`…`) while a request is in flight, which reads as a meaningless button.

Seen on `cast votes`, `leave note`, and the round-advance button (`frontend/src/pages/RoundDetailRoute.tsx:326, :658, :830`).

**Expected:** a clear busy state — keep the verb with a spinner/disabled style or use explicit text ("casting…", "saving…") rather than a lone `…`.

Source: manual testing (`docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`), 2026-06-21.

title: Set Secure flag on auth cookies in all HTTPS environments (incl. staging)
description:
Repo-side hardening split out from [MYS-40](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-40/staging-replace-self-signed-cert-with-lets-encrypt)'s optional note.

The refresh-token cookie's `Secure` flag is currently gated on `settings.environment == "production"` (`backend/app/api/routes/auth.py:162` set, and `:214` clear). Staging runs `ENVIRONMENT=staging` and is served over HTTPS (self-signed today, Let's Encrypt via [MYS-40](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-40/staging-replace-self-signed-cert-with-lets-encrypt) soon) with edge HSTS ([MYS-58](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-58/hsts-at-the-nginx-edge-staging-droplet)) — but its auth cookies are sent **without** `Secure`. That means the refresh cookie could be transmitted over a plain-HTTP request to the staging host.

## Change

Treat every non-development environment as a secure (HTTPS) context. Add a property to `Settings` (`backend/app/config.py`), e.g.:

```python
@property
def secure_cookies(self) -> bool:
    """Set the Secure flag on auth cookies in every HTTPS environment.
    Local development is the only environment served over plain HTTP."""
    return self.environment != "development"
```

Fail-closed: any environment value other than `development` (staging, production, or an unrecognized value) gets `Secure`. Use it in **both** `set_cookie` and `delete_cookie` in `auth.py` — they must stay identical or the cookie won't clear on logout (see the existing matching-attributes comment at `_clear_refresh_cookie`).

## Out of scope

* HSTS gating in `SecurityHeadersMiddleware` stays production-only (staging already gets edge HSTS from nginx; API-level HSTS on staging would be redundant).
* No change to the dev magic-link console behavior (`environment != "production"` branch).

## Acceptance

* Refresh cookie carries `Secure` when environment is `staging` or `production`, and does NOT when `development`.
* Set and clear paths use the same gating (logout still clears the cookie).
* Tests cover staging/production = Secure, development = not Secure.

title: Security response headers middleware (API)
description:
Add a Starlette/ASGI middleware to the FastAPI app that emits standard security response headers on every response. App-layer placement so it covers **both** staging (Droplet) and prod (App Platform), where no shared edge exists.

Derives from technical-design §9 checklist item 1 (HTTPS enforced) — the http→https redirect exists but downgrade/clickjacking/MIME hardening do not. The API currently runs only CORSMiddleware (`app/main.py`).

**Headers to set**

* `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains` — production only (gate on `settings.environment == "production"`, same pattern as the refresh-cookie `secure` flag)
* `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`
* `X-Frame-Options: DENY`
* `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`
* `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`

**Acceptance**

* Middleware registered in `create_app()` alongside CORS
* Tests assert each header present on a sample response; HSTS present only when environment=production, absent in development
* No interference with existing CORS behavior

Note: frontend Content-Security-Policy is intentionally scoped to a separate issue (more involved — needs API origin + Deezer/Odesli album-art hosts).

title: Frontend: round UI (create, submit, playlist/vote, reveal)
description:
Sprint 3 frontend — make the round loop usable in the browser (backend is done: [MYS-18](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-18/round-creation-state-machine-and-playlist-generation) rounds + [MYS-51](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-51/song-submission-endpoint-post-roundsidsubmissions) submissions + [MYS-52](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-52/cross-service-link-assembler-keyless-replace-odesli-only-resolution) links). Screens:

* **League Home**: a Rounds section listing the league's rounds with state; organizer can **create a round** (theme + optional votes-per-player).
* **Round detail** (`/rounds/:id`), state-aware:
  * `open_submission` — submit/replace your song via the existing SongSearchCard search/resolve flow (note + playing/vibing); organizer can **open voting**.
  * `open_voting` — the anonymous, shuffled **playlist** with per-platform open-on-service links (preferred service first); organizer can **close**.
  * `closed` — revealed submissions.

Follows docs/design/style-guide.md (named tokens, DM Serif headings / DM Mono, underline inputs, one Rust max, ring loaders). Reuses Button/Badge/Card/TextField/ConcentricRings and the api client patterns.

Also tidies the submission endpoint: `url` is no longer used ([MYS-52](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-52/cross-service-link-assembler-keyless-replace-odesli-only-resolution) assembles links from title/artist/isrc), so drop it from the request.

title: Cross-service link assembler (keyless) — replace Odesli-only resolution
description:
Keyless Odesli won't cross-match Spotify/YouTube/Apple from a Deezer-sourced track (proven: search results came back deezer-only), and an Odesli API key isn't available. Pivot: stop resolving cross-platform links *through* Odesli and assemble them ourselves from keyless sources.

Approach (anchored on title+artist, ISRC where it maps cleanly — ISRC is per-recording so it's a tiebreaker, not the master key):

* **Deezer** (keyless): exact track link via `/track/isrc:{isrc}`, else search; + ISRC + art.
* **Apple Music** via the **iTunes Search API** (keyless): exact track link (`trackViewUrl`).
* **Spotify / YouTube**: universal open-on-service deep links (keyless) built from title+artist.
* Every platform always gets at least a deep link; exact where a keyless lookup succeeds.

Scope:

* New `app/services/song_links.py` assembler. Keep `odesli.py` only to identify a *pasted* URL → title/artist (keyless identity).
* `POST /api/v1/songs/resolve` accepts a song identity (title/artist/isrc) or a url; returns the assembled `platforms`.
* Submission stores the assembled links (rename `submissions.odesli_data` → `platform_links`); playlist reads them directly.
* Frontend SongSearchCard: search-selected resolves by identity (no Odesli), paste resolves by url.
* Structured so adding free Spotify client creds later upgrades Spotify to an exact link with no rearchitecting.

title: Song submission endpoint (POST /rounds/:id/submissions)
description:
Sprint 3 gap: [MYS-16](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-16/sprint-3-round-flow-and-song-submission) (Round Flow & Song Submission) only had [MYS-17](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-17/odesli-integration-service-search-and-link-resolution) (song search/resolve) and [MYS-18](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-18/round-creation-state-machine-and-playlist-generation) (round creation + state machine + playlist) as children, but the actual **submission** endpoint — the thing that puts a song into a round — was never ticketed. [MYS-18](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-18/round-creation-state-machine-and-playlist-generation)'s playlist generation depends on submissions existing, so this is the bridge between the two.

Spec (technical-design §6 submissions, §7 Submissions):

* `POST /api/v1/rounds/:id/submissions` — submit a song to a round (members only, round must be in `open_submission`).
* Accepts the picked track (URL/ISRC from the search/resolve flow). Server re-resolves via Odesli and **persists the full** `odesli_data` **JSONB** plus isrc/title/artist/album/album_art_url (this is the [MYS-17](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-17/odesli-integration-service-search-and-link-resolution) "cache resolved track data in DB" line, descoped here).
* One submission per user per round (enforce uniqueness); allow replace/update while the round is open.
* `note` (max 280 chars), `participation_mode` (playing | vibing).
* `GET /api/v1/rounds/:id/submissions/mine`; full list only after voting closes (§7).

Depends on the rounds model/state machine from [MYS-18](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-18/round-creation-state-machine-and-playlist-generation).

title: Account deletion cascade + scheduled hard purge (DELETE /users/me)
description:
Technical-design §7/§9/§10 (right to be forgotten). `DELETE /api/v1/users/me` is specified but not yet built. Implement soft delete with a scheduled hard purge (within 30 days) that cascades to all personal data — submissions, votes, notes, sessions, league membership — leaving no orphaned records.

Note: this is partly a feature (the endpoint + purge job), not pure hardening — flag for scoping. Interacts with [[[MYS-25](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-25/handle-soft-deleted-user-re-login-unique-email-collision)]] (soft-deleted user re-login email collision).

title: Authorization audit: enforce per-league data isolation
description:
Technical-design §9: "Row-level security on PostgreSQL — players can only access their own league data." Audit every authenticated endpoint (leagues, members, invites, and the upcoming rounds/submissions/votes/notes) to confirm a user cannot read or mutate data for a league they aren't a member of.

* Verify membership/organizer checks on each route, including read endpoints.
* Add negative tests (non-member → 403/404) where missing.
* Decide whether to enforce at the app layer (current pattern) and/or DB RLS, and document the decision.

Should be revisited as Sprint 3–5 endpoints land, then signed off here before launch.

title: Frontend: SongSearchCard component + home screen integration
description:
## What to build

A `SongSearchCard` component that lives on the authenticated home screen, below the league list. This is a permanent fixture — not just a PoC throwaway.

## Layout and behavior

The card has two tabs or modes, switchable by the user:

**Mode 1: Paste a Link**

* Single underline-style text input: "Paste a Spotify or YouTube link"
* On submit (Enter or button): calls `POST /api/songs/resolve`
* While loading: subtle spinner, input disabled
* On success: displays the song result card (see below)
* On error: inline message ("We couldn't find that song. Check the link and try again.")

**Mode 2: Search by Title**

* Underline-style text input: "Song title" (required)
* Underline-style text input: "Artist" (optional, renders below)
* On submit: calls `GET /api/songs/search`
* While loading: subtle spinner
* On success with ≤10 results: displays a list of result rows for user to select from
* On success with `tooManyResults: true`: shows results plus a soft prompt: "Too many matches — try adding the artist name"
* On selection: calls resolve, transitions to song result card

**Song Result Card**
After resolution, display:

* Album art (thumbnail)
* Song title + artist + album
* Platform link row: icons/buttons for Spotify, YouTube, Deezer, Apple Music — only show platforms that exist for this song
* A "Search again" affordance to clear and restart

## Design constraints (from style guide)

* Follow `docs/design/style-guide.md` exactly
* Palette: Cream, Sage, Ink, Muted — Rust used once max as a signal element
* DM Serif Display for the card heading; DM Mono for everything else
* Underline-style inputs (no box borders)
* Concentric ring motif can be used as a subtle loader or decorative element
* Component goes in `frontend/src/components/songs/SongSearchCard.tsx`
* Use existing API client patterns from Sprint 1 auth work

## Accessibility

* Inputs have proper labels (visually hidden if needed)
* Platform links open in new tab with `aria-label`
* Loading states announced to screen readers

title: Backend: Odesli API service + song search endpoint
description:
## What to build

A backend service layer and API endpoints that power both song search modes.

## Endpoints

### `POST /api/songs/resolve`

Accepts a Spotify or YouTube URL. Calls Odesli `GET https://api.song.link/v1-alpha.1/links?url={url}` and returns:

* Song title, artist, album, thumbnail URL
* ISRC (canonical identity, from `entitiesByUniqueId`)
* Platform links object: `{ spotify, youtube, deezer, appleMusic }` — only include platforms with available links

### `GET /api/songs/search?q={title}&artist={artist}`

* Uses Spotify search API (client credentials flow — no user login required) to find matching tracks
* Returns up to 10 results: `{ id, title, artist, album, thumbnailUrl, spotifyUrl }`
* If `artist` param is omitted and results exceed 10, include a flag `{ tooManyResults: true }` to prompt the user to refine
* For each result the user selects, call Odesli resolve to get full platform links

## Implementation notes

* Create `backend/app/services/odesli.py` — thin async wrapper around the Odesli API
* Create `backend/app/services/spotify_search.py` — client credentials auth + search
* Create `backend/app/routers/songs.py` — mounts the two endpoints above
* Odesli API key from `ODESLI_API_KEY` env var; Spotify client ID/secret from `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID` / `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET`
* Add all three to `staging.env.example` and `.env.example`
* Add error handling: invalid URL, song not found, API timeout
* Add unit tests for both service modules with mocked HTTP calls

title: Song Search PoC — Odesli integration + home screen search card
description:
## Overview

Implement a Song Search proof-of-concept on the authenticated home screen. This is the most critical mechanic in MysteryMixClub — the ability to find a song across platforms and resolve it to a canonical identity (ISRC) with links to Spotify, YouTube, Deezer, and Apple Music.

This card lives permanently on the home screen as a quick utility and onboarding tutorial, not just during the PoC phase.

## Goals

* Validate the Odesli/Songlink API integration
* Validate the song search UX before it's embedded in round submission flows
* Give users a way to share songs across platforms from anywhere in the app

## Two modes

1. **Paste a link** — user pastes a Spotify or YouTube URL; app resolves it via Odesli and displays canonical song info + platform links
2. **Search by title/artist** — user types a song title (+ optional artist); app returns up to 10 results to choose from

## Acceptance criteria

* Search card appears below league list on the home screen for authenticated users
* Both input modes work and display results correctly
* Results show: song title, artist, album art, and links to all available platforms
* If search returns too many ambiguous results (title only, common name), user is prompted to add artist name
* UX is polished and responsive — this is a showpiece feature
* Odesli API key is read from environment, never hardcoded

title: Staging: HTTP Basic Auth on /api breaks authenticated calls (Authorization header clash)
description:
Clicking the magic/sign-in link on staging returned "401 Authorization Required".

## Root cause

HTTP Basic Auth (added for anti-crawl) and the app's JWT both use the `Authorization` HTTP header. Once the SPA is signed in, every API call sends `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`, so the browser can't *also* attach `Authorization: Basic <creds>` — nginx sees Bearer, not Basic, and 401s every authenticated API request. Confirmed in nginx logs: `GET /api/v1/users/me 401 188` with no basic-auth user (nginx challenge), while unauthenticated calls like `/auth/request` carried Basic fine.

## Fix

Disable basic auth on the `location /api/` block — the API authenticates itself (JWT + one-time magic-link tokens + refresh cookie). Basic auth stays on the SPA/HTML (top-level navigations carry no Authorization header, so anti-crawl still works).

Applied to the live Droplet (nginx reload) and committed to `scripts/nginx-mysterymixclub-staging.conf`. Verified: `/` still 401s without creds; `/api/v1/users/me` with Bearer (no basic auth) → 200.

## Note

The deploy pipeline does not manage nginx config, so this nginx change was applied to the box by hand in addition to the repo commit.

title: Staging environment on a DigitalOcean Droplet
description:
Stand up a staging environment for MysteryMixClub on a self-managed $6/mo Ubuntu 24.04 DigitalOcean Droplet (IaaS), serving the React build via Nginx and the FastAPI backend via systemd, with local Postgres.

## Why this diverges from [MYS-29](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-29/devops-cicd-pipeline-husky-hooks-github-actions-digitalocean-app-specs)

[MYS-29](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-29/devops-cicd-pipeline-husky-hooks-github-actions-digitalocean-app-specs) delivered the CI/CD pipeline as config-as-code targeting **DigitalOcean App Platform** (`.do/app.staging.yaml` + `app.prod.yaml`). Per decision in this work, **staging moves to a Droplet** while **production stays on App Platform**. `.do/app.staging.yaml` is retained for reference but no longer drives the staging deploy.

## Deliverables (in the PR)

* `scripts/bootstrap-droplet.sh` — idempotent one-time provision (packages, `mysterymixclub` user, staging Postgres role+DB, repo checkout, venv, ufw 22/80/443)
* `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` — pull develop → `pip install -e .` → `alembic upgrade head` → restart service → `npm ci && build` → publish to web root
* `scripts/mysterymixclub-api.service` — systemd unit (uvicorn 127.0.0.1:8000, env from `/etc/mysterymixclub/staging.env`, restart-on-failure)
* `scripts/nginx-mysterymixclub-staging.conf` — SPA + `/api/` proxy + `/health`→`/api/v1/healthz`, HTTP Basic Auth, SSL placeholder
* `scripts/staging.env.example` — runtime env template
* `.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml` — replaced App Platform deploy with SSH → `deploy-staging.sh` (secrets `STAGING_HOST`, `STAGING_SSH_USER`, `STAGING_SSH_KEY`)
* `docs/staging-setup.md` — full runbook
* `backend/app/config.py` — add `"staging"` to the `environment` Literal (previously crashed on `ENVIRONMENT=staging`)
* `CLAUDE.md` + `docs/ci-cd.md` — reconciled to document the staging/prod infra split

## Corrections vs. the original spec (to match the actual app)

* `SECRET_KEY` (app reads this), not `JWT_SECRET`
* `pip install -e .` (pyproject), no `requirements.txt`
* nginx `/health` proxies to the real route `/api/v1/healthz`
* added `"staging"` to the env Literal so the app boots

## Remaining manual steps (tracked here)

* Droplet IP: 67.207.81.183 (root SSH confirmed; Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS)
* Point a subdomain (e.g. [staging.mysterymixclub.com](<http://staging.mysterymixclub.com>)) at the IP, then run the runbook with Let's Encrypt
* Add GitHub secrets `STAGING_HOST` / `STAGING_SSH_USER` / `STAGING_SSH_KEY`
* Provision the box (`bootstrap-droplet.sh`), populate `/etc/mysterymixclub/staging.env`, install systemd unit + nginx site, create basic-auth file
* Merge the PR only after the box + secrets exist (merging triggers the SSH deploy)

title: Normalize DATABASE_URL to the asyncpg driver
description:
Discovered during [MYS-37](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-37/run-db-migrations-on-deploy-pre-deploy-alembic-upgrade) review. The app builds its engine with `create_async_engine(settings.database_url)` (backend/app/db/session.py) and Alembic's migrations/env.py uses `async_engine_from_config` off the same URL. Both REQUIRE a `postgresql+asyncpg://` scheme. Nothing normalizes the scheme: backend/app/config.py stores DATABASE_URL as a raw string.

DigitalOcean managed-Postgres bindings (`${db.DATABASE_URL}`) emit a bare `postgresql://...` (often with `?sslmode=require`). If so, the async engine raises on startup and the ENTIRE backend (auth included, not just leagues) fails to boot on DO. CI never catches this because ci.yml hardcodes the `postgresql+asyncpg://` URL itself.

Fix: normalize the scheme in [config.py](<http://config.py>) so a bare `postgresql://` or `postgres://` is coerced to `postgresql+asyncpg://` (idempotent: leave an already-correct `postgresql+asyncpg://` untouched). A Pydantic field validator on the settings is the natural place. Preserve query params (e.g. sslmode). asyncpg note: asyncpg does not accept `sslmode` as a libpq query param the same way - confirm whether the DO URL's query string needs handling (asyncpg uses `ssl=`), and document/handle if required.

Acceptance: given DATABASE_URL in any of `postgresql://`, `postgres://`, or `postgresql+asyncpg://` forms, settings.database_url is a valid asyncpg URL; covered by unit tests. This unblocks the develop -> main promotion (prod must boot).

title: Run DB migrations on deploy (PRE_DEPLOY alembic upgrade)
description:
Discovered during [MYS-15](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-15/frontend-league-and-invite-screens) browser smoke test. The deploy pipeline never runs database migrations: neither .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml / deploy-prod.yml nor .do/app.staging.yaml / app.prod.yaml run `alembic upgrade head`. The backend service only runs uvicorn.

Impact: the Sprint 2 tables (leagues, league_members, invites) do not exist in staging (which auto-deployed on every develop merge today) or prod, so all league/invite endpoints will 500 in those environments. The dev DB only worked locally because migrations were run by hand. This blocks the develop -> main promotion.

Fix (config as code):

* Add a PRE_DEPLOY job to BOTH .do/app.staging.yaml and .do/app.prod.yaml that runs `alembic upgrade head` against the managed Postgres, using the same backend source/build and the DATABASE_URL secret as the api service. (DigitalOcean App Platform: `jobs:` entry with `kind: PRE_DEPLOY`.)
* Add a migration apply step to CI (ci.yml backend job) so every PR proves `alembic upgrade head` succeeds against the CI Postgres - a lasting guard against "model added but migration/deploy missing."

Acceptance: a fresh database reaches the full current schema purely via the deploy pipeline (no manual alembic run), and CI fails if migrations do not apply cleanly. Verify the auth-era tables were not relying on a one-time manual migration either.

title: Expose user id on GET /users/me
description:
Enabler for [MYS-15](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-15/frontend-league-and-invite-screens). The frontend has no way to learn the current user's id, but the league home screen needs it to compute `isOrganizer` (`league.organizer_id === me.id`) and to identify the viewer's own member row (so the "remove" control is never shown on yourself).

`GET /api/v1/users/me` currently returns `{display_name, email, preferred_service, default_vibe_mode}`. The `users` table already has `id` (UUID pk); it is simply not surfaced.

Change: add `id` (UUID serialized as string) to the `UserProfileResponse` and `_to_profile` mapper in backend/app/api/routes/users.py, and add `id: string` to the frontend `UserProfile` type in frontend/src/services/api.ts. Keep the field read-only (PATCH must not accept it). Update the backend users-me test to assert the new key, and the frontend api.test.ts getMe fixtures.

Small, low-risk, read-only addition.

title: League read endpoints (list, detail, members)
description:
Read endpoints needed to build the [MYS-15](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-15/frontend-league-and-invite-screens) frontend (my-leagues list, league home, organizer controls). All three are specified in technical-design section 7 but were not included in the Sprint 2 backend build order ([MYS-12](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-12/create-league-endpoint)/13/14). Splitting them out so the frontend has a real API to call and backend stays green-before-frontend.

All authenticated. All league-scoped access is gated on ACTIVE membership (`league_members.removed_at IS NULL`); removed members and non-members are denied. Missing league -> 404; exists-but-not-an-active-member -> 403.

### GET /api/v1/leagues

* Returns the full league objects (same shape as POST /leagues) for every league where the caller is an ACTIVE member (this includes leagues they organize, since the organizer is an active member).
* Excludes leagues where the caller's membership has been removed.
* Order by created_at descending (most recent first).
* Returns a JSON array (possibly empty).

### GET /api/v1/leagues/:id

* 404 if not found; 403 if caller is not an active member; else 200 with the full league object.

### GET /api/v1/leagues/:id/members

* 404 if league not found; 403 if caller is not an active member.
* Returns the ACTIVE members only (removed_at IS NULL), each as `{user_id, display_name, joined_at, is_organizer}` where `is_organizer` is `user_id == league.organizer_id`. Do NOT expose member email addresses.
* Order by joined_at ascending (organizer, who joined at creation, naturally first).

Implementation notes: all three on the existing leagues router; reuse LeagueResponse / _to_response; add a `_load_league_as_member` helper paralleling the existing `_load_league_as_organizer`. No new model or migration. Members endpoint joins league_members -> users for display_name.

title: Backend CI is red: ruff-format drift + missing jose mypy stubs
description:
Backend CI (`ruff · mypy · pytest`) has been failing on `develop` from **two stacked pre-existing issues**, both surfaced while reviewing PR #1 / [MYS-27](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-27/frontend-onboarding-capture-display-name-on-first-login) (frontend-only, unrelated). The ruff failure ran first and masked the mypy one.

## 1\. ruff-format drift

`ruff format --check .` failed on 10 backend files that predate consistent formatting enforcement (`app/api/routes/auth.py`, the models, two migrations, four `tests/test_auth_*.py`). `ruff check` passed — purely formatting.

## 2\. mypy: missing jose stubs

Once formatting was fixed, `mypy app` failed: `app/auth/jwt.py:4: Library stubs not installed for "jose"`. python-jose ships no type stubs (came in with [MYS-26](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-26/user-profile-endpoints-getpatch-usersme)). Fixed with a scoped `[tool.mypy]` override (`ignore_missing_imports` for `jose.*`), matching the untyped-boundary intent documented in `jwt.py`.

## Fix (PR #2, branch `chore/backend-ruff-format`)

* `chore(MYS-31): apply ruff format to backend`
* `fix(MYS-31): ignore missing jose type stubs in mypy`

## Acceptance

* Backend CI fully green on develop: ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy, pytest.
* No behavior change (formatting + mypy config only).

## Follow-up (optional)

Add `ruff format --check` and `mypy` to the pre-push hook to catch this locally.

title: DevOps: CI/CD pipeline (husky hooks, GitHub Actions, DigitalOcean app specs)
description:
Stand up a professional CI/CD pipeline as configuration-as-code for the FastAPI + React monorepo deployed on DigitalOcean App Platform. Shipped in commit `bd236ae`.

## Delivered

**Local git hooks (Husky v9)**

* `pre-commit` → lint-staged: ESLint `--fix` + Prettier on staged `*.ts/tsx`; `ruff check --fix` + `ruff format` on staged `*.py`.
* `commit-msg` → commitlint (Conventional Commits, `.commitlintrc.json`).
* `pre-push` → frontend typecheck + backend pytest.

**GitHub Actions** (`.github/workflows/`)

* `ci.yml` — PRs to `main`/`develop`: frontend lint/typecheck/test + backend ruff/mypy/pytest+coverage.
* `deploy-staging.yml` — push to `develop` → `mysterymixclub-staging`.
* `deploy-prod.yml` — push to `main`, gated by `environment: production` → `mysterymixclub-prod`.

**DigitalOcean** — per-environment specs `.do/app.staging.yaml` and `.do/app.prod.yaml` (api service :8080, frontend static site, managed Postgres 15), `deploy_on_push: false` so Actions own deploys.

**Supporting** — frontend ESLint flat config + Prettier config + `lint` script, `pytest-cov` dev dep, `## CI/CD` section in CLAUDE.md, `docs/ci-cd.md` (pipeline diagram, branch-protection checklist, secret onboarding).

## Deviations from the original brief (intentional)

* `ruff format` instead of `black` — repo standardized on ruff (line-length 100); black would conflict.
* Health check path is the real route `/api/v1/healthz`, not `/health`.
* Frontend is a `static_sites` entry (Vite SPA → `dist/`), not a long-running service.
* `digitalocean/app_action/deploy@v2` (the monolithic action was split into subactions).

## Known follow-ups (not yet ticketed)

* Hooks assume backend tooling is on `PATH`, but it lives in `backend/.venv` — `pre-commit` (ruff) and `pre-push` (pytest) fail unless the venv is active. Worth making the hooks auto-resolve the venv.
* Manual setup still required: GitHub branch-protection rules, the `production`/`staging` environments, and the `DIGITALOCEAN_ACCESS_TOKEN` secret (all documented in docs/ci-cd.md).

title: Frontend onboarding: capture display_name on first login
description:
Deferred out of [MYS-10](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-10/frontend-auth-flow-magic-link-ui) (frontend auth flow). Resolves the sentinel created in [MYS-7](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-7/magic-link-verification-and-session-issuance).

## Context

[MYS-7](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-7/magic-link-verification-and-session-issuance) creates a first-login user with `display_name = ""` as the deliberate "not yet onboarded" sentinel. [MYS-10](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-10/frontend-auth-flow-magic-link-ui) shipped the core auth flow + a minimal authenticated home but did NOT build onboarding. We need a frontend step that forces a new user to set a real display name before entering the app.

## Scope

* After verify/login, if the user's `display_name` is empty, route them to an onboarding screen that captures a display name and saves it via `PATCH /users/me`, then proceeds to /home.
* Gate app entry on a non-empty display_name (the empty-string sentinel = needs onboarding).
* Build the screen in the design system (ui-agent): underline input, Rust once, DM fonts.

## Depends on

* [MYS-26](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-26/user-profile-endpoints-getpatch-usersme) (GET/PATCH /users/me) — needed to read the empty display_name and to save the chosen one.

## Acceptance

* New user with empty display_name is forced through onboarding before reaching /home.
* Returning user with a set display_name is unaffected.
* Covered by tests.

title: User profile endpoints: GET/PATCH /users/me
description:
Deferred out of [MYS-10](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-10/frontend-auth-flow-magic-link-ui) (frontend auth flow). Per technical-design §7 (Users):

* `GET /api/v1/users/me` — return the current user's profile (display_name, email, preferred_service, default_vibe_mode). Bearer-authenticated.
* `PATCH /api/v1/users/me` — update display_name, preferred_service, default_vibe_mode. Bearer-authenticated, input-validated/sanitized (§9).

## Dependency this unblocks

This is the first **Bearer-protected** resource, so it requires building the JWT-decode / `get_current_user` auth dependency that [MYS-7](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-7/magic-link-verification-and-session-issuance)/[MYS-8](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-8/silent-token-refresh-flow) deliberately deferred (decode the access token, 401 on missing/invalid/expired). The frontend already ships an `authenticatedRequest` wrapper (in `frontend/src/services/api.ts`) that attaches `Authorization: Bearer` and silently refreshes on 401 — it's ready to consume these endpoints.

## Acceptance

* `get_current_user` dependency decodes/validates the JWT and yields the user; covered by tests (valid, missing, malformed, expired).
* GET/PATCH /users/me implemented, validated, tested.
* Blocks the onboarding name-capture follow-up.

title: Notes system and Most Noted calculation
description: Notes system and Most Noted mechanic\\n\\n- POST /api/v1/submissions/:id/notes: leave a written note on any submission (max 280 chars)\\n- GET /api/v1/submissions/:id/notes: retrieve notes\\n- Most Noted: calculated at round close, awarded to submission with most notes\\n- Eligible to ALL submissions regardless of participation mode\\n- Tie: both songs recognized\\n- Notes on Most Noted song surfaced publicly at round reveal\\n- Most Noted displayed alongside (never instead of) scoring results

title: Voting system and Just Vibing mode
description: Voting endpoint and Just Vibing participation mode\\n\\n- POST /api/v1/rounds/:id/votes: cast votes (Playing players only, up to votes_per_player)\\n- Prevent voting on Just Vibing players' submissions\\n- Prevent self-voting\\n- Enforce unique constraint (one vote per submission per voter)\\n- Just Vibing mode: set per profile (default_vibe_mode) or per submission (participation_mode field)\\n- Just Vibing players' submissions visible in playlist but receive no votes\\n- When a Playing player would vote for a Vibing submission: prompt to leave a note instead\\n- Just Vibing status visible to group with warm language (not punitive)

title: Sprint 4: Voting, Notes, Just Vibing, and Most Noted
description: Parent issue for voting, notes, Just Vibing mode, and Most Noted mechanic.\\n\\nSee: `docs/prd/prd.md` Section 5.3 (Participation Modes), 5.4 (Most Noted), 5.5 (Voting)\\nSee: `docs/discovery/personas.md` Persona 4 (The Vibe Player)

title: Round creation, state machine, and playlist generation
description: Round creation, state machine, and playlist generation\\n\\n- POST /api/v1/leagues/:id/rounds (organizer only): create round with theme, submission_deadline, voting_deadline\\n- PATCH /api/v1/rounds/🆔 advance state, update deadlines\\n- Round states: open_submission -> open_voting -> closed\\n- GET /api/v1/rounds/:id/playlist: generate playlist using stored odesli_data, resolve to player's preferred_service\\n- Submissions anonymous and shuffled during voting\\n- YouTube always available as fallback for unavailable tracks

title: Odesli integration service (search and link resolution)
description: Implement Odesli service layer used by both submission paths\\n\\n- GET /api/v1/songs/search?q= -- native search via Odesli\\n- POST /api/v1/songs/resolve -- resolve any pasted platform link to canonical track\\n- Both return: ISRC, title, artist, album, album_art_url, full odesli_data JSONB\\n- Handle Odesli rate limits gracefully -- clear error to user on failure, never silent\\n- Cache resolved track data in DB to reduce repeat API calls\\n- Odesli API key stored server-side only, never exposed to client

title: Sprint 3: Round Flow and Song Submission
description: Parent issue for round flow: create round, song submission (paste + native search via Odesli), round state transitions, playlist generation.\\n\\nSee: `docs/technical/technical-design.md` Section 8 (Odesli Integration) and `docs/prd/prd.md` Section 5.1-5.2

title: Frontend league and invite screens
description: Build the frontend league and invite screens\\n\\n- Create league form (name, description, number of rounds, votes per player)\\n- League home screen (name, current round, member list, state)\\n- Invite link share UI (copy to clipboard, share sheet on mobile)\\n- Join league screen (shown when opening an invite link -- league preview + join button)\\n- Organizer controls (extend/shorten rounds, remove member)\\n- My leagues list screen

title: League management (extend, shorten, remove member)
description: PATCH /api/v1/leagues/:id (organizer only)\\n\\n- Allow organizer to update: name, description, total_rounds\\n- total_rounds can be extended or shortened\\n- Cannot shorten below current_round number\\n- Cannot modify a completed league\\n\\nDELETE /api/v1/leagues/:id/members/:userId (organizer only)\\n- Set removed_at on league_members record\\n- Removed members cannot access league data

title: Invite link generation and join flow
description: POST /api/v1/leagues/:id/invites and GET /api/v1/invites/:token and POST /api/v1/invites/:token/accept\\n\\n- Any league member can generate a shareable invite link\\n- Invite token is cryptographically random, no expiry in v1\\n- GET /invites/:token returns league name and member count (unauthenticated preview)\\n- POST /invites/:token/accept adds user to league_members\\n- Prevent duplicate membership

title: Create league endpoint
description: POST /api/v1/leagues\\n\\n- Authenticated users only\\n- Required fields: name, total_rounds, votes_per_player (default 3)\\n- Optional: description\\n- Creating user becomes the organizer\\n- Creates the league record and adds organizer as first league_member\\n- Returns full league object

title: Sprint 2: League and Member Management
description: Parent issue for all league and membership work.\\n\\nSee: `docs/technical/technical-design.md` Section 7 (API Design) and Section 6 (Data Model)

title: Define a consistent focus-visible treatment across form inputs and buttons
description: Surfaced during ali8.5's design review (login screen). TextField's only focus cue is its underline shifting Ink to Sage (a ~2.3:1 contrast shift on a 1px line, under the 3:1 WCAG non-text contrast floor), while buttons and links keep the browser's default focus ring (Tailwind preflight doesn't strip it) -- so the app currently has two inconsistent focus treatments: a nearly-invisible one on inputs and a UA-blue ring everywhere else that clashes with the Sage/Cream palette. Needs a single system-wide focus-visible style (e.g. a 2px Sage focus-visible ring with 2px offset) applied consistently to every interactive element, documented in docs/design/style-guide.md. Affects every form in the app, not just login -- broader than any single screen's ticket.

title: Waitlist IP rate limiter is silently broken under multi-worker gunicorn
description: Found incidentally during ali8.2 review (MysteryMixClub-ali8.2). waitlist.py:33's IP-keyed rate limiter is in-memory only, and its own comment says that only works because staging/prod run a single process (no --workers flag) — explicitly flagged as not a pattern to copy for anything durable. That precondition became false with MYS-259 (perf(prod): gunicorn multi-worker...): scripts/mysterymixclub-api-prod.service now runs gunicorn with --workers $GUNICORN_WORKERS. Each worker process has its own copy of the in-memory bucket, so the effective rate limit is N x the intended limit and resets on every deploy/worker restart. Currently low real-world exposure since WAITLIST_ENABLED=false everywhere (MYS-215, see project_waitlist-mys-215 memory) so the endpoint 404s, but the moment the waitlist flag is flipped on this is a live, silently-degraded control. Needs either a DB-backed limiter (same shape as login_attempts) or an explicit decision to accept the degraded behavior for this endpoint's threat model.

title: Wire systemd timers for purge_accounts and purge_login_attempts
