description: Neither backend/app/jobs/purge_accounts.py nor the new purge_login_attempts.py (MysteryMixClub-ali8.1) has an actual systemd .timer unit in scripts/ -- docs/ci-cd.md lists purge_accounts as timer-triggered but only advance-mixes actually has one. Both jobs are bounded in design (30-day soft-delete purge; 24h login_attempts retention) but not in practice until they're scheduled on staging and prod. Needs the same bootstrap-droplet.sh / systemd unit treatment as mysterymixclub-advance-mixes.timer, on both environments.

title: Frontend: account settings UI — set password / link Google
description: Surfaces the new opt-in actions from account settings for users who signed up via magic link: set a password, link a Google account. Follows the existing settings screen patterns.

title: Backend: account settings — set password / link Google on an existing account
description: Lets a user who signed up via magic link opt in to the new methods without a forced migration: PATCH-style endpoints to set a password on an account that doesn't have one, and to link a Google identity to an existing account. No behavior change for accounts that never call these.

title: Casual-mode clubs: rename "Open Voting" to "Reveal the Mystery Mix", confirm notes stay enabled
description:
**UX** (from user testing — testers used the word "collaborative" for what the app calls casual mode: no voting/ranking, just songs + notes)

For an all-casual club, the phase currently labeled/actioned as "open voting" doesn't fit — nobody actually votes, so the real event at that transition is revealing the anonymized, shuffled mix.

**Where:**

* `frontend/src/pages/MixDetailRoute.tsx` — `MIX_STATE_LABELS` (~line 65, `open_voting: "voting open"`) and the organizer's phase-transition button (~line 757, "open voting")

**Ask:** for a club with no competitive participants, rename this phase's label and the organizer's action button to "Reveal the Mystery Mix" instead of "Open Voting."

Also confirm notes stay available at this stage — they already render for an individual vibing member inside a mixed club (`SongNotes` in the `isVibingParticipant` branch, ~line 1634), but verify that holds for a fully-casual club too, not just one casual member inside an otherwise-competitive club.

title: Paste-a-link: replace the service dropdown with an auto-detected label
description:
**UX cleanup** (from user testing)

**Where:** `frontend/src/components/songs/SongSearchCard.tsx` (~line 344-389, the "paste a link" tab). A manual "service" `<select>` dropdown sits above the link field, but `handleUrlChange` already calls `detectService()` to auto-detect the source from the pasted URL — the dropdown is redundant, and the helper text right below it even says "paste any link — we'll detect the service automatically."

**Fix:** remove the dropdown. Once a link is pasted and the source is identified, show it as a read-only label/badge (reuse `SourceBadge`, already used elsewhere for this) instead of an input the user sets manually beforehand.

title: Add reassuring context before the Apple Music sign-in prompt
description:
**Bug/UX** (from user testing): a tester found the Apple Music login prompt "concerning."

**Where:** `frontend/src/components/AppleMusicPlaylist.tsx` — clicking "build this mystery mix in Apple Music" immediately calls `authorizeAppleMusic()` (`frontend/src/services/musickit.ts`), which pops Apple's own MusicKit sign-in/authorization dialog with zero lead-in from our UI.

We can't change Apple's own popup copy, only what appears before it. Add brief reassuring context near the button — e.g. explain this creates a private playlist copy in the user's own Apple Music account and MysteryMixClub never sees their password — so the sudden OS-level login prompt isn't a surprise.

title: Partial-submission leave warning doesn't convey time pressure
description:
**Bug** (from user testing)

The "leave anyway?" warning shown when navigating away mid-submission is misleading — it doesn't convey that there's a deadline, so a partial submitter may not realize they're at risk of missing it.

**Where:** `frontend/src/pages/MixDetailRoute.tsx` (the `partiallySubmitted` navigation blocker, ~line 152 and ~line 546-561). Current copy: `you've submitted {mySubmissions.length} of {submissionCap} songs. leave anyway?`

**Requested copy:** "You have X time to submit your final Y songs!" — where X is time remaining until the submission deadline (reuse the `formatCountdown`/`formatDeadline` helpers in `frontend/src/utils/deadline.ts`, already used by `DeadlineChip`) and Y is `submissionCap - mySubmissions.length`.

**Acceptance criteria**

* Leave-confirmation copy states remaining time and remaining song count instead of just "leave anyway?"
* Still only fires when partially (not fully, not zero) submitted, matching current `partiallySubmitted` gating

title: Improve Lighthouse/discoverability: render-blocking fonts, unused JS bundle, robots.txt, meta description, llms.txt
description:
## Baseline (measured 2026-07-23)

Ran a real Lighthouse audit (mobile, `lighthouse` CLI via headless Chrome) against the production build of the login/landing page — Dawn's own PageSpeed Insights link for [mysterymixclub.com](<http://mysterymixclub.com>) didn't render actual scores (client-side JS report, nothing extractable), so this is a fresh local measurement instead, run against `frontend`'s production build (`npm run build` + `vite preview`), not the dev server.

| Category | Score |
| -- | -- |
| Performance | 91 |
| Accessibility | 100 |
| Best Practices | 96 |
| SEO | 82 |

Core metrics: FCP 2.5s, LCP 2.9s, TBT 0ms, CLS 0, Speed Index 2.5s, TTI 2.9s.

Accessibility 100 is a good sign post-[MYS-121](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-121/wcag-accessibility-conformance), though this only exercised the public unauthenticated landing page, not the richer authenticated screens (mix detail, voting, etc.) that [MYS-121](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-121/wcag-accessibility-conformance)'s fixes mostly targeted — worth a follow-up audit against an authenticated page once there's an easy way to get Lighthouse past the magic-link login.

## Decided (2026-07-23): the public marketing surface should be discoverable

MysteryMixClub is invite-only for the *product* (join requires an invite or the waitlist), but Dawn wants the public marketing surface — landing page, about, help, waitlist signup — to be genuinely discoverable, both by search engines and by AI assistants/agents. That resolves the open question from this ticket's first draft: robots.txt and meta description are real fixes, not something to gate behind a product decision, and it's worth adding an `llms.txt` too.

## Scope

* **Render-blocking Google Fonts request — \~1,210ms estimated savings.** The `fonts.googleapis.com` request for DM Mono/DM Serif Display blocks first paint. Fix options: self-host the two font files instead of the Google Fonts CDN, or at minimum add `<link rel="preconnect">`/`rel="preload"` and confirm `&display=swap` is actually taking effect.
* **Reduce unused JavaScript — \~63 KiB estimated savings.** The whole app ships as a single 375 KB (104 KB gzipped) bundle with no code-splitting. Route-based lazy-loading (`React.lazy`/dynamic `import()`) for screens like Admin, Help, or the rarely-hit legal pages would cut what the landing page has to parse.
* **Add** `<meta name="description">` — currently missing entirely.
* **Add a** `robots.txt` that explicitly allows crawling of the public pages (landing, about, help, waitlist) — currently there is none at all, so crawlers get the SPA's `index.html` fallback instead of real directives.
* **Add** `llms.txt` at the site root (per the emerging [llmstxt.org](<http://llmstxt.org>) convention) — a short markdown file describing what MysteryMixClub is (platform-agnostic music club for close friend groups, Music League alternative, invite/waitlist-gated) with links to the landing page, about, help/FAQ, and the waitlist signup, so AI assistants asked about MysteryMixClub answer accurately and point people to the waitlist instead of guessing.

## Not real findings (test-environment artifacts, exclude from scope)

The audit also flagged CORS console errors — these are from testing the local `vite preview` build directly against `localhost:8000` with no reverse proxy, not a real issue. Staging/prod serve the API same-origin through nginx, so this won't reproduce there; skip re-checking it.

## Done when

Render-blocking font request resolved, JS bundle reduced via code-splitting on at least the largest non-critical routes, `robots.txt`/meta description/`llms.txt` all added and correct for a "discoverable marketing surface, gated product" posture.

title: Rename "vibe"/"vibing" terminology — reads as AI cliché, confusing to users
description:
"Vibe" / "vibing" / "just vibing" has spread across the product as the name for the non-competitive participation mode (profile setting, per-round toggle, UI copy, persona name). Flagged as too AI-cliché and confusing for users.

## Scope

* **User-facing copy** (highest priority): toggle labels, helper text ([MYS-199](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-199/explain-what-andquotjust-vibingandquot-means-on-the-create-club-form)), onboarding/create-club form, persona docs
* **Naming decision**: pick a replacement term for "just vibing" mode — needs to read clearly as "opt out of voting, still listen/comment" without sounding like AI-generated copy
* **Code/schema** (lower priority, can defer): `default_vibe_mode`, `participation_mode` values, `vibe_mode` fields, `MYS-*` branch/ticket language — decide whether to rename in code now or just at the copy layer first to avoid unnecessary migration churn

## Not in scope (unless decided otherwise)

* Full backend field/column renames — recommend shipping copy-layer rename first, then deciding if the schema rename is worth the migration

## Related

[MYS-112](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-112/define-andquotjust-vibingandquot-behavior-decision-unblock-vibing-ui) (behavior decision), [MYS-60](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-60/no-ui-to-set-just-vibing-participation-mode) (toggle UI), [MYS-199](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-199/explain-what-andquotjust-vibingandquot-means-on-the-create-club-form) (helper text), [MYS-20](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-20/voting-system-and-just-vibing-mode) (voting/vibe mode), [MYS-134](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-134/closed-round-vibers-should-see-the-submitted-songs-no-scores), [MYS-132](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-132/vibing-viewer-cant-leave-notes-on-the-open-voting-playlist) (vibing viewer notes/reveal)

## Next step

Pick the replacement term, then fan out to a copy-audit pass across screens listed above.

title: Voting tally screen drops playlist links once a player votes (should stay visible)
description:
## Bug

During `open_voting`, once a player casts their vote(s), the page swaps entirely from the voting view to a "you've locked in your votes" tally screen — and that screen drops the playlist links (YouTube/Spotify/Apple Music) entirely. A player who's done voting has no way to keep listening until the mix reaches `closed`.

This is distinct from (and not to be confused with) the already-working `closed`-state behavior (`ClosedListen`, [MYS-132](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-132/vibing-viewer-cant-leave-notes-on-the-open-voting-playlist)/[MYS-133](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-133/closed-round-the-playlist-listen-affordance-disappears)), which does keep playlists visible after a mix closes. The gap is specifically the *in-between* window: voted, but mix still open.

## Root cause

`frontend/src/pages/MixDetailRoute.tsx`:

* `VotingSection` (`:1477`) checks `isVotesLocked` first (`:1518-1521`) and, if true, returns `<VotingTally voteCounts={voteCounts} votesSaved={votesSaved} myVotes={myVotes} />` instead of the normal voting content.
* `isVotesLocked` is set once the current user has voted — `:191` on load (`loadedVotes.submission_ids.length > 0`), `:403` right after casting a vote. It's per-user, independent of overall mix state.
* `VotingTally` (`:1754-1840`) renders only the confirmation message + vote-count tally — no `YouTubePlaylistLink`, `SourceOnlyTracks`, `SpotifyPlaylist`, or `AppleMusicPlaylist`, unlike the non-locked voting/vibing branches (`:1541-1592`, `:1595-1605`) which render all of those before their own content.

## Fix direction (unconfirmed, needs design/scope check before implementing)

`VotingTally` should render the same playlist components the voting/vibing branches do, likely by accepting the same playlist props `VotingSection` already receives (`youtubePlaylistUrl`, etc.) and rendering them above or alongside the tally, matching the layout `ClosedListen` already establishes for the same components post-close.

## Repro

1. Join a club, get to a mix in `open_voting`.
2. Cast votes as a "playing" participant.
3. Observe: playlist links (present before voting) are gone from the page; only the tally + confirmation message remain.

title: Speed up backend test suite / CI wall-clock time
description:
## Why

Flagged by Dawn 2026-07-23 mid-session: pushing a small frontend-only PR took several minutes locally (pre-push hook: full backend pytest suite, 1037 tests, ~3.5min serial + frontend typecheck) before CI even started, and CI itself adds more on top. This is friction on every single push, not just large changes.

## Likely levers (unconfirmed, needs investigation before implementing)

* Backend suite runs serially (no `pytest-xdist`/`-n auto`) — parallelizing across cores is usually the single biggest win for a suite this size.
* Check whether `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs backend tests, frontend typecheck, and lint as a parallel job matrix or one sequential job — if sequential, splitting into parallel jobs cuts wall-clock without touching the tests themselves.
* Check for any obviously slow fixtures/setup (e.g. full DB reset per test vs. per-suite, unnecessary sleeps, network calls not mocked) — see [[reference_async-test-expire-all]] and [[project_serial-test-runs]] for known DB-related constraints already in play (shared test DB, no concurrent pytest runs allowed — any parallelization fix has to respect that).
* Pre-push hook itself running the *full* suite on every push (not just changed areas) is intentional per current process (`docs/git-hygiene.md`) — worth confirming whether that's still the right tradeoff once CI is faster, or whether pre-push should run a lighter subset and let CI catch the rest.

## Scope

Investigation first — profile where the time actually goes (test execution vs. fixture setup vs. CI job sequencing) before picking a fix. Don't guess-optimize.

title: Admin: add ops-only "connect spotify" button for the shared playlist account
description:
## Why

Follow-up from the 2026-07-23 prod playlist-secrets outage (see [[project_prod-playlist-secrets-outage]] internal notes): `SPOTIFY_PLAYLIST_ACCOUNT_USER_ID` still needs a one-time OAuth link against prod to connect `mysterymixclubspotify@gmail.com` ([MYS-169](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-169/spotify-playlists-via-shared-account-public-per-round-playlist-link) shared-account playlist generation). The connect flow (`GET /api/v1/spotify/connect`, `backend/app/api/routes/spotify.py:132`) has no UI caller — `connectSpotify()` in `frontend/src/services/api.ts:939` was dormant, callable only via manually copying a bearer token out of DevTools and hand-crafting a fetch call. Dawn asked to simplify this instead of repeating that dance.

## What

Adds a "spotify" section to the platform-admin page (`/admin`, `frontend/src/pages/AdminScreen.tsx` + `AdminRoute.tsx`):

* Shows current status via `GET /api/v1/spotify/status` (configured / connected) as a `Badge`.
* A "connect spotify" / "reconnect spotify" button that calls `connectSpotify("/admin")` and redirects the browser to Spotify's consent screen.
* Reads the `?spotify=connected|denied|...` flag the OAuth callback lands back with and shows a one-time result message, then clears it from the URL.

No backend changes — wires existing, already-shipped endpoints to a UI.

## Test plan

- [ ] Typecheck/lint clean (done locally)
- [ ] Manual verify on staging: badge renders correctly, button kicks off the real Spotify consent flow, lands back on `/admin` with the right result message
- [ ] Once confirmed working, do the actual prod OAuth link as a separate manual step (not part of this PR)

title: Backfill ADRs for previously uncaptured major decisions
description:
The ADR practice (`docs/adr/README.md`) was formalized 2026-07-22, but the project has made several major decisions before then with no ADR — the reasoning lives only in Linear comments, PR descriptions, or memory, not in `docs/adr/`. Go back through project history and write ADRs for the decisions that meet the "major decision" bar (tech/vendor/hosting choice, architectural pattern other work builds on, or a tradeoff overriding the obvious approach).

## Known candidates (non-exhaustive — check Linear history for more)

* Staging on a self-managed Droplet instead of DO App Platform ([MYS-39](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-39/staging-environment-on-a-digitalocean-droplet)).
* Magic-link + JWT + refresh-token auth model, and the `SameSite=Lax` refresh-cookie change ([MYS-91](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-91/auth-session-lost-after-returning-from-spotify-oauth-switch-refresh)) over the originally-specced `Strict`.
* Source-only (ISRC-less) track identity for Bandcamp/YouTube submissions ([MYS-201](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-201/isrc-less-submissions-bandcampyoutube-only-tracks-playlist-gap)).
* Tenant isolation enforced at the application layer rather than Postgres RLS (technical-design §9).
* league→club / round→mystery mix rename ([MYS-191](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-191/epic-rename-league-club-round-mystery-mix)) — why now, why this vocabulary split (wire vs. route-layer field names, [MYS-196](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-196/rename-r5-cutover-api-surface-db-rename-one-breaking-deploy)).
* Odesli/Songlink as the canonical song-identity dependency, and its eventual sunset implications.
* Any others surfaced while reviewing closed Linear issues and PR history.

Each should follow the `docs/adr/README.md` format (Context/Decision/Consequences/Revisit if) and get the next sequential number after whatever exists at the time this is picked up (currently up to `0002`).

title: Apex + www DNS records for prod (mysterymixclub.com)
description: Ties into [MYS-174](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-174/domain-migration-move-the-app-to-wwwmysterymixclubcom) (domain migration to [www.mysterymixclub.com](<http://www.mysterymixclub.com>)). `infra/terraform/envs/prod/terraform.tfvars` already declares `dns_a_names`/`dns_aaaa_names` for `@` (apex) and `www`, pointed at the prod droplet's reserved IP via the shared module. These records go live once the prod droplet is actually provisioned (see the "Build out prod droplet" ticket) and applied — this ticket tracks the DNS cutover itself, including verifying propagation and Resend/email record compatibility (the existing `mysterymixclub.com` zone already carries Resend DKIM/SES/DMARC records that must not be disturbed).

title: Provision DO Spaces bucket + wire Terraform remote state backend
description: Terraform state for staging + prod is local-only today (no backend configured in `infra/terraform/envs/*`). Recommended (see `infra/terraform/README.md`): a DO Spaces bucket as an S3-compatible backend with `use_lockfile = true` (native TF ≥1.10 locking, no DynamoDB needed) — reusing the same bucket planned for offsite `pg_dump` backups, ~$5/mo total. Runner-up considered: Terraform Cloud free tier (zero-ops, no portability cost since state format is standard). Avoid staying local long-term — no locking, laptop-only, loss risk. Needs a write-scoped DO token to create the bucket and access keys.

title: Move SPA build off the deploy box into CI
description: `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` currently runs `npm run build` for the React SPA directly on the staging droplet (`s-1vcpu-1gb`, 1GB RAM) alongside uvicorn and local Postgres — real OOM risk on a box that small, and the same pattern would be worse on prod under real traffic. Move the frontend build into GitHub Actions CI and ship the built `dist/` artifact to the droplet instead of building in place.

title: Configure DO monitor alert policies (CPU/mem/disk)
description: No `digitalocean_monitor_alert` policies exist for staging or prod today — confirmed via read-only inspection 2026-07-21. The Terraform module (`infra/terraform/modules/droplet-app`) already supports a `create_monitor_alerts` toggle wired to CPU/memory/disk thresholds (80% over 5m) and an `alert_emails` list. Needs: enable in staging tfvars (currently off) and prod tfvars (already on, pointed at [dgabriel@gmail.com](<mailto:dgabriel@gmail.com>)), then apply with a write-scoped token.

title: Import staging droplet + DNS record into Terraform state
description:
Terraform for staging was authored in `infra/terraform/envs/staging/` (feature/[MYS-213](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-213/devops-and-maintenance-schedule-playbook)-terraform-bootstrap) to match the live droplet exactly, so the first `plan` after import should report no changes. Not yet imported — needs a write-scoped DO token (session that wrote it only had read access).

Run from `infra/terraform/envs/staging/`:

```
tofu init
tofu import module.staging.digitalocean_droplet.this 577618725
tofu import 'module.staging.digitalocean_record.a["staging"]' mysterymixclub.com,1822275773
tofu plan   # must show No changes
```

SSH key, default VPC, and project are left unmanaged (data-only, no import needed).

title: Add BrowserStack cross-browser testing to PR CI pipeline
description:
Integrate BrowserStack (or similar) into the GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline so PRs trigger automated cross-browser/device tests before merge, catching rendering or compatibility issues early — especially for the Bandcamp embed player and PWA install flow.

**Acceptance criteria:**

* BrowserStack account/API key wired into GitHub Actions secrets
* Test suite runs against a defined browser/device matrix (e.g. Chrome, Safari, Firefox + mobile Safari/Chrome) on every PR
* CI fails the PR check if cross-browser tests fail
* Results visible in PR checks / linked report

**Notes:** Highest cross-browser risk area is the player panel work ([MYS-153](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-153/queue-ui-persistent-player-panel-with-manual-advance)/154).

title: Waitlist: replace "email for access" with a public waitlist + admin invite flow
description:
Temporary feature (flagged, per docs/feature-flags.md) — replaces the current "no invite yet? email us" copy on the login page with a real public waitlist.

## Scope

**Login page**: a small email-only form ("join the waitlist") replaces the current mailto "email us" copy in `EmailEntryScreen.tsx`. Basic validation: email format + duplicate-entry rejection. Gated behind a new `WAITLIST_ENABLED` flag (default off) so it can revert to today's copy without a code change.

**Backend**:

* New `waitlist_entries` table: `id`, `email` (unique, lowercased), `created_at`, `invited_at` (nullable), `invited_by` (nullable FK to users).
* `GET /waitlist/enabled` (public) — lets the frontend decide whether to render the form.
* `POST /waitlist` (public) — join; 404 if the flag is off, 409 on a duplicate email, otherwise 201.
* `GET /admin/waitlist` (platform-admin) — list entries.
* `POST /admin/waitlist/{id}/invite` (platform-admin) — mints a platform invite (same club-less, 48h-expiry invite `POST /admin/invites` already creates) and emails it to the waitlist entry's address, stamping `invited_at`/`invited_by`. Resendable (no block on re-inviting).

**Admin page**: new "waitlist" section below the existing invite-generation section, listing entries with an "invite" action per row.

**Explicitly unchanged**: the existing club-invite flow (`POST /clubs/:id/invites`, accept/preview) and the existing platform-invite generator (`POST /admin/invites`, manual copy-link) — both keep working exactly as today. The waitlist's admin-invite action reuses the same underlying invite-minting logic, it doesn't replace it.

**Email copy**: the "you're off the waitlist" email subject/body needs Dawn's sign-off before it's committed — hold that piece back from the PR until approved.

## Out of scope (not asked for)

* No coupling to the 1500-user cap (admin invites manually, same as today's platform-invite flow; the cap is still enforced lazily at signup as it already is).
* No rate limiting beyond basic format + duplicate-email validation.
* No change to `CheckEmailScreen`'s post-submit copy beyond keeping it consistent with the new waitlist entry point.

title: Apple Music playlist: direct link on desktop, app+prompt on mobile
description:
Follow-up to [MYS-190](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-190/apple-playlist-link-shows-andquotitem-not-availableandquot-on-mobile). Dawn's report: the Apple Music playlist link "breaks on desktop."

## Root cause

[MYS-190](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-190/apple-playlist-link-shows-andquotitem-not-availableandquot-on-mobile) (2026-07-18) fixed a real mobile bug — iOS can't resolve a `/library/playlist/{id}` deep link ("Item Not Available") — by collapsing the link to a generic `https://music.apple.com/library` for both platforms. That fix was deliberately platform-agnostic (no user-agent sniffing) but as a side effect, desktop lost the "go straight to the exact playlist" behavior it used to have (the desktop web player resolves `/library/playlist/{id}` even though Apple doesn't document that as supported) — now both platforms land on the generic Library root and the member has to find the playlist by name.

## Decided approach

Split by platform, explicitly reintroducing the per-platform branching [MYS-190](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-190/apple-playlist-link-shows-andquotitem-not-availableandquot-on-mobile) avoided, because desktop wants the sharper direct-link behavior back:

* **Desktop**: direct link to the exact playlist (`https://music.apple.com/library/playlist/{id}`)
* **Mobile**: today's behavior unchanged — generic `/library` link + "look for '{name}'" prompt

**Known risk, accepted**: desktop's direct-playlist URL relies on undocumented Apple web-player behavior that already regressed once (that's what [MYS-190](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-190/apple-playlist-link-shows-andquotitem-not-availableandquot-on-mobile) was). If it breaks again, desktop degrades back to the same generic-library link mobile already uses — not a regression, just back to today's baseline for desktop too.

## Scope

* Backend: un-deprecate `library_playlist_url()` in `apple_music_client.py`; add a `direct_playlist_url` field to `ApplePlaylistLinkResponse` and `GeneratedApplePlaylist`/`GeneratePlaylistResponse`, populated from the stored `playlist_id`.
* Frontend: first instance of platform detection in this app (no existing precedent) — `AppleMusicPlaylist.tsx` renders `direct_playlist_url` on desktop, falls back to `playlist_url` + the "look for it" prompt on mobile.

title: Canned skins designed by artists/designers (paid upgrade)
description:
## Problem

Rather than (or in addition to) user-built custom skins, offer pre-made, professionally designed skin packs as a paid upgrade — higher perceived quality, no design-system risk from user-generated combinations.

## Proposal

* Commission or partner with real artists/designers to create a curated set of skin packs.
* Sell/unlock as a paid upgrade (one-time purchase per skin, or bundled into a subscription tier).
* Skins should stay within brand guardrails (Duchamp Rotorelief-inspired system) while giving real visual variety.

## Open questions

* Sourcing: commission artists directly, or open a submission/marketplace model?
* Relationship to [MYS-207](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-207/custom-skins-for-paid-users) (custom skins for paid users) — complementary tracks or does one supersede the other?
* Revenue split if working with outside artists/designers?
* How many skins for MVP/launch?

title: Custom skins for paid users
description:
## Problem

No monetizable visual customization exists yet. Paid users have no way to personalize their app experience beyond default styling.

## Proposal

* Let paying users apply custom skins (colors/themes/visual treatments) to their profile, club, or player UI.
* Needs a definition of what's "skinnable" without breaking design system integrity (e.g. Rust #B5533C stays a signal color, not decorative — may constrain how far skins can go).
* Requires paywall/entitlement gating tied to a paid tier.

## Open questions

* What's the paid tier/pricing model this hooks into (not yet defined elsewhere)?
* Skin creation: user-defined (color pickers) vs. selecting from presets — relates to MYS-207 (canned skins by artists).
* Does this conflict with or complement the canned/artist-designed skins ticket?

title: Club image header upload
description:
## Problem

Clubs/leagues currently have no way to set a custom header image, making them feel generic and harder to visually distinguish.

## Proposal

* Allow club/league owners to upload a header image for their club.
* Define crop/aspect ratio and file size constraints.
* Fallback/default header for clubs that don't upload one (consistent with design system — Duchamp Rotorelief palette).

## Open questions

* Storage: where do uploaded images live (DigitalOcean Spaces vs droplet local storage)?
* Moderation: any review needed for user-uploaded images?
* Does this apply per-League or per-Club (naming/scope check needed)?

title: Shared Spotify playlist expiration: notify players + regeneration option
description:
## Problem

Shared Spotify playlists expire after 30 days. Once expired, players lose access to the collaborative artifact from that game/round.

## Proposed flow

* Track playlist creation date and compute a 30-day expiration.
* Before expiration, email all players in the game with a heads-up that the playlist is expiring soon and a prompt to copy it into their own Spotify account.
* Consider a regeneration mechanism: either auto-regenerate a fresh playlist from the same track set, or give a manual "regenerate" action so the game/League doesn't lose its music artifact permanently.

## Open questions

* How many days before expiration should the email fire (7 days? 3 days?)
* Does regeneration create a new playlist ID (breaking existing embeds/links) or refresh the existing one?
* Is this per-game or per-League (Collective league type has a persistent communal playlist artifact — expiration matters more there)
* Do we need a "last regenerated" or "expires on" indicator in the UI?

## Notes

Relevant to Collective league type's communal playlist artifact and any persistent player panel work ([MYS-153](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-153/queue-ui-persistent-player-panel-with-manual-advance)/154).

title: Bandcamp: platform link-out + paste-a-link resolution
description:
Add Bandcamp support at the two levels that are feasible without an API (Bandcamp's API is partner-only: no search, no track lookup, no oEmbed, no ISRCs).

## Scope

**A — platform link row.** Add `bandcamp` to the normalized platform keys with a search deep link (`https://bandcamp.com/search?q=<title artist>&item_type=t`), same pattern as the Spotify deep link. Backend `song_links.py` + frontend platform lists.

**B — accept pasted Bandcamp track links** in `POST /songs/resolve`. `*.bandcamp.com/track/<slug>` pages carry OpenGraph meta (`og:title` = "Track, by Artist", `og:image`); parse that and funnel through the existing Deezer search for canonical identity (ISRC). New host branch in `link_resolver.py`; existing paths untouched.

## Explicitly out of scope

* **Bandcamp-only tracks.** Submissions require an ISRC; Bandcamp doesn't expose them, so a pasted link only resolves when the track also exists on the major catalogs. Bandcamp-only releases fail with "no matching track found." Supporting them means making ISRC nullable — a schema/product change deferred past the first prod deploy.
* **Playlist generation** — impossible without an API.

## Notes

* OG-meta parsing is scraping (no API contract); acceptable for a user-pasted-link path, flagged here for the record.
* Custom artist domains (not `*.bandcamp.com`) are out of scope.

title: Explain what "just vibing" means on the create-club form
description:
The "just vibing by default" checkbox on `/clubs/new` says who starts vibing but not what vibing *is*. Requested by @dgabriel 2026-07-18: add helper text along the lines of "no voting or ranking, just songs and response notes."

Fold into the existing helper line under the checkbox (`CreateLeagueScreen`), keeping the switch-anytime reassurance. Voice: lowercase, short, no exclamation marks.

Note: the per-mix vibing toggle in the mix detail screen has its own copy — out of scope here unless requested.

title: Age verification for MMC
description:
MMC currently has no age verification/age-gating mechanism.

**Business context:** MMC does not share data with third parties and does not serve ads. This meaningfully narrows legal exposure — it avoids COPPA's heightened consent tier for third-party disclosures/targeted advertising, and sidesteps UK Children's Code Standards 12/13 (no profiling, no targeted ads by default). It does NOT eliminate the need for an age gate:

* **COPPA (US):** Collection of personal info from known under-13 users still requires notice + some form of verifiable parental consent, regardless of sharing practices. Actual knowledge is the trigger.
* **UK Children's Code + Online Safety Act:** Applies to any service "likely to be accessed by children" (everyone under 18 counts as a child under the Code). Requires age-appropriate design, data minimization, and a documented risk assessment — independent of ad/sharing model.
* **GDPR / UK GDPR:** Consent-based processing requires age-appropriate parental consent below local threshold (13-16 depending on member state); still need lawful basis, privacy notice, retention limits.

**Recommended MVP approach (given current small closed user group + no ads/no sharing):**

* Self-attested DOB field at signup (not just a checkbox) — regulators have flagged tick-boxes as insufficient
* Block/reject signups for under-13 users outright rather than building full COPPA parental-consent flows
* Keep data collection minimal and defaults private
* Revisit with a written risk assessment + possible age-assurance vendor if MMC scales into EU/UK markets meaningfully

**To figure out:**

* Where this fits in the signup/onboarding flow
* Copy/UX for the DOB gate and under-13 rejection flow
* Data retention policy for DOB field itself

Flagging now so it's not missed as MMC grows beyond a small closed user group.

title: Production release process: change notification + safer deploy pipeline
description:
Raised 2026-07-18 while shipping the Apple Music chain. Not needed now — the current flow is fine for non-breaking updates against a small beta cohort — but it should be settled **before the production launch**.

## Why

Today `develop` → staging deploys on merge, silently. That's acceptable while changes are additive and the audience is a handful of beta testers who know the app is in flux. It stops being acceptable when:

* users don't know a change happened, so a moved control reads as a bug;
* a migration is *not* purely additive and needs a real multi-step rollout;
* something ships broken and there's no announced way to tell people.

## To figure out

* **Change notification** — how users learn what changed. In-app changelog? Email on notable releases? A "what's new" note on the round page? Needs to distinguish "we moved a button" from "voting works differently now."
* **Breaking-change protocol** — the current rule (additive migrations only, flag before running) is a convention held in a person's head. Should be an enforced checklist or a CI gate.
* **Prod deploy gate** — `deploy-prod.yml` has a manual approval step; decide what the approver is actually verifying, and whether staging soak time is required first.
* **Rollback story** — currently undefined for a bad prod deploy. Cheapest useful version is probably a documented "redeploy the previous good spec" runbook.

## Not in scope

Rebuilding the branch model. `feature/* → develop → main` works; this is about what happens *around* a release, not how code reaches it.

title: Accessibility audit and remediation toward WCAG 2.1 AA
description:
Only 18 of 64 frontend `.tsx` components use any `aria-*` attribute, and there's no stated accessibility conformance target, keyboard-navigation audit, or color-contrast check against the design system palette (`docs/design/style-guide.md`).

**Scope**

* Audit against WCAG 2.1 AA: keyboard navigation/focus order, color contrast (particularly Rust/Gold signal colors against Cream background), form labeling, screen-reader landmarks.
* Remediate the gaps found; prioritize the invite/signup and round-voting flows since those are the most-used paths.
* Decide whether to add automated a11y linting (e.g. `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y`) to the pre-commit/CI chain (`docs/ci-cd.md`) to prevent regression.

Filed from a 2026-07-16 compliance gap review; not previously scoped in Linear.

title: Add data export / right-of-access endpoint (GDPR Art. 15/20)
description:
Right to erasure is implemented (`DELETE /users/me`, cascading hard purge within 30 days — `docs/technical/technical-design.md` §10) but there's no right of access / data portability path. PRD explicitly defers "Export / copy playlist" as a nice-to-have UX feature (`docs/prd/prd.md` line 245, technical-design.md §12) — this ticket is narrower and legally motivated, not the playlist-export feature.

**Scope**

* A `GET /users/me/export` (or similar) endpoint returning a JSON dump of the user's own data: profile, submissions, votes, notes, league memberships.
* Doesn't need a polished UI — a downloadable JSON file satisfies GDPR Art. 15 (access) and Art. 20 (portability). Can reuse the same data-gathering logic that powers the account-deletion cascade.

Filed from a 2026-07-16 compliance gap review; not previously scoped in Linear.

title: Disclose subprocessors and confirm DPAs (Resend, Spotify, YouTube, Deezer, Odesli, DO)
description:
GDPR Art. 28 requires disclosing subprocessors who touch EU users' personal data and having a Data Processing Agreement in place with each. We currently send user data (emails, listening submissions) through several third parties with no disclosure or DPA review:

* Resend (transactional email)
* Spotify Web API (playlist generation — see `reference_spotify-integration`)
* YouTube / Deezer / Odesli APIs (song resolution/playlist gen — Deezer already dropped per playlist-rollout status, Odesli sunsetting 2026-07-31)
* DigitalOcean (droplet host + managed Postgres)

**Scope**

* Enumerate every third party that receives user data (even indirectly, e.g. an email address hitting Resend's API).
* For each, check whether they offer a standard DPA and whether it's been accepted (most do, via their ToS/dashboard).
* Add a "Subprocessors" section to the Privacy Policy (depends on the ToS/Privacy Policy ticket) listing them.

Filed from a 2026-07-16 compliance gap review; not previously scoped in Linear.

title: Admin-generated, league-less signup invite
description:
Every invite today is tied to a specific league (`invites.league_id NOT NULL`) and only grants signup + membership in that one league. Add a second invite flavor a platform admin can generate that grants signup only — no league attachment — so the recipient can sign up and then create their own league (or later, join an open one).

## Design

* Migration: `invites.league_id` becomes nullable. A null `league_id` *is* the platform-invite marker — no new column/type field.
* `POST /admin/invites` (platform-admin only, `get_platform_admin`-gated) generates one: same shareable-link shape as league invites, 48h expiry (consistent with existing invite security posture — regenerating from the admin page is one click, so this stays low-friction).
* Admin page gets a "generate invite" action with a copy-link affordance, matching the existing per-league invite UI pattern.
* Reuse the existing `/invite/:token` link + `JoinLeagueScreen` rather than a second page: when `league_id` is null, show generic "you're invited to mysterymixclub" copy (no league name/member count), sign-in threads the token through to signup exactly like today, and an authenticated visitor lands on `/home` (no league to accept into).
* `accept_invite` rejects (404) a league-less token — "accept" only makes sense for a league invite; a platform invite's frontend flow never calls it.

Scoped down from [[[MYS-155](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-155/about-page-placeholder-scope-tbd)]]-adjacent invite conversation (2026-07-15) — keep blast radius minimal: nullable-column migration only, no new tables, reuse existing invite plumbing/UI wherever possible.

title: Expired invite links: redirect an already-member straight to their league
description:
Today `GET /invites/{token}` and `POST /invites/{token}/accept` both 410 on an expired token before checking membership, so an already-active member hitting a stale link they still have bookmarked/saved just sees "this link has expired" instead of landing in their league.

## Fix

* Check membership before applying the expiry gate on both the preview and accept routes. An already-active member passes through regardless of expiry.
* Preview: on an expired token, if the (optionally authenticated) caller is already an active member of that invite's league, the frontend redirects straight to `/leagues/{id}` instead of showing the expired screen.
* Accept: same idempotent bypass, consistent with the existing [MYS-135](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-135/join-league-an-existing-member-should-land-on-the-league-not-an-error) pattern.
* For everyone else on a genuinely expired link: keep the existing "ask the organizer for a new one" copy, plus a CTA — "go home" if signed in, "sign in" if not.

Requires a `get_current_user_optional` auth dependency (preview is a public route today; needs best-effort identity to check membership without requiring auth).

title: Epic: Cohort → Bout → Round restructure (post-beta)
description:
**Post-beta epic** (decided 2026-07-12): split today's fused "league" concept into a persistent group and repeatable competitions, enabling "run it back."

## Agreed hierarchy

```
Cohort — the people (persistent, never "finishes")
 ├─ name, organizer, members, invites
 └─ Bouts — one competition each (repeatable)
     ├─ settings + state: total_rounds, current_round, state,
     │  votes_per_player, songs_per_submission, deadline windows, completed_at
     └─ Rounds 1..N — unchanged (theme, submit → vote → reveal)
```

* **Cohort** = what "league" means socially today: the group, membership, invite links. Persists forever.
* **Bout** = what "league" means mechanically today: one run of the competition. A cohort has many bouts over time, **one active at a time**.
* **Round** = unchanged, parented to a bout instead of a league.
* **"Run it back"**: when a bout completes, the organizer starts a new bout in the same cohort — same members, same settings, fresh pending rounds, zero re-inviting.

## Design decisions (recorded 2026-07-12)

* Standings default **per-bout** (fresh race each run); cohort page may add all-time/bouts-won later
* `default_vibe_mode` lives at **cohort** level (it's a "how this group plays" setting); per-round playing/vibing unchanged
* Migration: every existing league becomes a cohort containing exactly one bout holding its existing rounds — nothing visible changes for existing users

## Recommended approach: structural-additive (sized 2026-07-12)

* **Additive migrations only** (live users on staging): new `bouts` table; the settings columns above move as a block off `leagues`; add `rounds.bout_id`; backfill one bout per existing league. **No table renames.**
* `leagues` table keeps identity/membership and takes the cohort role; internal `league` naming retained initially — **user-facing copy switches to cohort/bout** (UI strings + notification emails; no i18n layer exists, strings are inline)
* Full internal rename (league→cohort: ~3,000 occurrences across 50+ files + first-ever table-rename migrations) is **explicitly out of scope** for the first phase

## Implementation anchors (from codebase exploration)

* The only structural seam is `rounds.league_id` — submissions/votes/notes/playlists all key on `rounds.id` and are untouched
* Round auto-generation to reuse for new-bout: `backend/app/api/routes/leagues.py` `create_league` (~176–222) and `_reconcile_rounds` (~481–527)
* Leaderboard query (`leagues.py` ~331–390) must adopt bout scope; `most_noted` likewise
* Invites/join re-point to cohort (join = join the cohort; active bout picked up automatically)
* `app/services/notifications.py` hardcodes the `league_complete` event and `/leagues/{id}` URLs — becomes per-bout lifecycle
* Unique constraint `uq_rounds_league_number` → per-bout equivalent
* Permission helpers `_load_league_as_organizer/_member` gain the round → bout → cohort hop

## Phasing (carve child tickets when picked up)

1. Schema: `bouts` table + `rounds.bout_id` + backfill migration (additive, multi-step per live-user rules)
2. Backend: bout CRUD + "start new bout" endpoint + settings/permission reads via bout
3. Standings: per-bout leaderboard + reveal scope
4. Frontend: cohort page with bout history + "run it back" action; routing
5. Copy pass: UI strings + emails say cohort/bout

Related: [MYS-63](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-63/allow-appending-a-round-to-a-league-that-already-has-a-pre-created) (append a round to an existing slate) touches the same round-reconciliation code — consider folding it in.

title: League admin: broadcast message to all league members (in-app + email)
description:
New admin capability: let a league organizer/admin send a one-off message to every member of the league.

## Scope

* **Delivery**: in-app (announcement/banner or feed item on the league page) **and** email fan-out to each member's registered address.
* **Email infra**: reuse the existing Resend-based sender introduced for round lifecycle notifications ([MYS-109](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-109/email-notifications-for-round-lifecycle-events)) rather than standing up a new pipeline.
* **Sender**: any league admin (organizer or co-organizer, pending [[[MYS-99](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-99/league-allow-the-organizer-to-grant-another-member-admin-co-organizers)]] landing) can trigger a send.
* **Audience**: all current members of the league (need to decide: include members who've left/been removed? default no).

## Open questions (confirm before/at implementation)

* Message length/formatting limits (plain text vs light markdown)?
* Rate limiting — prevent spam/abuse of the broadcast (e.g. cooldown per league)?
* Does this need a persisted history (members can scroll past announcements) or is it fire-and-forget?
* In-app surface: dedicated announcements feed vs. toast/banner on next visit?

## Dependency

Admin-authorization surface overlaps with [[[MYS-99](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-99/league-allow-the-organizer-to-grant-another-member-admin-co-organizers)]] (co-organizer support) — both touch "who counts as a league admin" checks. Sequence after [MYS-99](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-99/league-allow-the-organizer-to-grant-another-member-admin-co-organizers) so authorization logic isn't duplicated.

title: Confirm before closing a round (organizer safety — prevents accidental close)
description:
**Born from a live incident (2026-07-03):** an organizer accidentally closed round 1 ("Off the wall") of Slamilluminati #1 while it was still `open_voting`. The round had a valid voting deadline still 3 days out, so this wasn't a deadline auto-close — a single click on "close round" did it. Closing a round is a one-click, no-confirm action (`OrganizerControls` in `frontend/src/pages/RoundDetailRoute.tsx:602-632`) and cascades: it auto-opens the next round (`open_submission`, deadline stamped) and advances `leagues.current_round`. There's no in-app undo (see [MYS-168](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-168/organizer-roll-a-round-back-from-voting-to-submission>)), so this incident required a hand-run SQL fix across three tables (the round, the next round, and the league) over SSH on staging.

## What

Add a confirm step to the "close round" action specifically — not "open round" / "open voting", which are lower-risk and easier to reason about. `OrganizerControls` currently fires `onAdvance("closed")` immediately on click with no intermediate state; gate that specific transition (`open_voting → closed`) behind an explicit confirm (e.g. a second "are you sure" click/button pair, in the same spirit as the admin screen's typed-confirm for account deletion, but lighter-weight — a round close isn't as destructive as a hard-delete). Exact treatment (modal vs. inline two-step) TBD at implementation; keep it in the Sage/Ink family per the style guide, no Rust unless it's genuinely the screen's one signal.

## Acceptance

* Clicking "close round" no longer closes immediately — it requires a second explicit confirm action.
* "open round" and "open voting" transitions are unaffected (still one click).
* Copy is calm and specific about what happens (round closes, next round opens, deadline starts) — not just "are you sure?".

title: Organizer: roll a round back from voting to submission
description:
Born from a live incident (2026-07-03): a beta round (Slamilluminati #1, r1) advanced to voting by accident and had to be rolled back by hand-run SQL over SSH. Organizers need this as a product capability — the round lifecycle is forward-only in code (`pending → open_submission → open_voting → closed`) with no sanctioned reverse step.

## What

`PATCH /rounds/:id` (or a dedicated endpoint) allowing the **organizer only** to move a round from `open_voting` back to `open_submission`. This is the single sanctioned backward transition; closed rounds stay closed.

## Semantics (proven in the incident, keep identical)

* `state → open_submission`
* `submission_opened_at = now()` — the quorum re-scopes to members active at rollback time, so a late joiner can hold the round open, and it legitimately re-advances once everyone's in
* `submission_deadline = now() + league.submission_window_hours` — fresh full window
* `voting_deadline = NULL` — re-stamped when voting genuinely reopens (the no-clobber guard in `advance_round_state` requires the NULL)
* `submission_warning_sent_at` / `voting_warning_sent_at` / `empty_round_notice_sent_at = NULL` — warnings re-arm
* **Votes cast during the accidental voting phase are deleted** (the ballot set may change; stale votes would poison results and could insta-satisfy the voting quorum). Surface a confirm in the UI when votes exist ("N votes will be discarded").
* **Notes are kept** — they're appreciation, remain state-gated, and resurface at close.
* `league.current_round` unchanged.

## UI

Organizer control on the round view (next to the existing manual-advance override). Confirm dialog; extra warning when votes exist. Calm copy per style guide.

## Notifications

Decide: silent (incident behavior — organizer tells the league) vs. a "submissions reopened" email. Lean silent-with-optional-email; needs product call.

## Watch out

* Concurrency with the [MYS-145](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-145/deadline-force-advance-fallback-for-stalled-rounds) job and the vote-cast auto-close: do the transition under the same `FOR UPDATE` lock discipline.
* The stale "voting is open" email from the accidental advance can't be unsent; a reopened round will send a second voting-open email later — acceptable.

title: Profile: uploadable profile photo (replaces cassette placeholder)
description:
Currently every user gets the same cassette tape SVG placeholder avatar (Vinyl color token). This ticket covers replacing it with real uploadable profile photos.

## Scope

* **Storage**: provision DO Spaces bucket for user-uploaded assets; add bucket + CDN config to both staging and prod environments
* **Backend**: `POST /users/me/avatar` — accept multipart image upload, validate type (jpeg/png/webp) and size (max 2MB), resize to 256×256, upload to Spaces, save `avatar_url` on the user row (new column + Alembic migration)
* **Frontend**: file input on profile screen with preview before upload; display avatar wherever `UserAvatar` is rendered; fall back to the cassette SVG when no photo is set

## Notes

* `UserAvatar` component is already wired in — just needs an `avatar_url` prop and a fallback branch
* The cassette SVG placeholder lives in `frontend/src/components/avatars/`
* DO Spaces is S3-compatible; use `boto3` or `httpx` on the backend

title: League home: member list becomes an all-time vote leaderboard
description:
The member list on the league home page should double as an all-time leaderboard showing total votes received per member across every completed round in the league.

## What

Replace (or augment) the current member list with a ranked leaderboard: each row shows the member's display name and their cumulative vote total from all songs they've submitted across all closed rounds in the league.

## Scope

* **Backend:** new endpoint (or extend an existing one) that aggregates `votes` by submitting user within a league, across all rounds. Only count votes from rounds in `closed` state so in-progress rounds don't pollute the totals.
* **Frontend:** render the member list as a ranked leaderboard on the league home screen — rank, display name, total votes. Members with no submissions (vibers, new joiners) appear at the bottom with 0.
* **Design system:** stay within Ink/Sage/Cream palette; DM Mono for figures. No Rust unless it's the single Rust use for the screen.

## Acceptance

* League home shows members ranked by total votes received (descending)
* Ties broken consistently (e.g. alphabetical by display name)
* Members with 0 votes are included, not hidden
* Only closed rounds contribute to the tally
* Current user is visually distinguished (e.g. bold or Sage accent) without breaking the rank order

title: Playlists: use a consistent seeded shuffle order across all platforms (Spotify, YouTube)
description:
The round playlist endpoint (`GET /rounds/{id}/playlist`) already shuffles submissions using `random.Random(round_id.int)`, which drives the YouTube watch-videos URL. The Spotify playlist generation route (`POST /rounds/{id}/spotify-playlist`) does not apply any shuffle, so Spotify and YouTube end up in different orders.

## Fix

* In both routes, sort submissions by `submission.id` before shuffling. Without a pre-sort, Postgres heap order (not guaranteed without `ORDER BY`) can vary between queries and produce different shuffle outputs for the same seed.
* In `spotify.py`: add `submissions.sort(key=lambda s: s.id)` then `random.Random(round_id.int).shuffle(submissions)` after fetching submissions, before building `matched_uris`.
* In `rounds.py` (`get_round_playlist`): add the same sort before the existing shuffle.

## Result

Every player who generates a playlist on any platform (Spotify, YouTube, and any future service) will see the submissions in the same randomized order. The order is stable per round — re-generating does not re-shuffle.

## Notes

This is grouped with [MYS-89](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-89/spotify-playlist-persist-playlist-id-per-round-user-instead-of-name) (persist playlist id) since it's part of the same playlist-generation refactor.

title: Voting: move leave-a-note / read-notes inside the song card and make it more prominent
description:
During voting (`open_voting`), the "leave a note" and "read notes" affordances are outside / detached from the song card, making them easy to miss. They should live inside the card itself and be visually prominent enough that players naturally notice and use them.

## What to fix

* Move the note input and note-read affordance into the song card component (same visual container as the song title, artist, and vote controls)
* Ensure the hierarchy makes the action feel primary, not a footnote
* Stay within the design system: underline-style input, Sage/Ink palette — no additional Rust unless it is the one Rust use for the screen

## Acceptance

* On a voting-state round, the note affordance is visually inside each song card
* First-time players can find it without hunting
* Design system rules respected (one Rust per screen max)

## Notes

Surfaced as a usability observation during a smoke test session (2026-06-28). No backend changes needed — the notes API is fully wired.

title: Completed league state: confetti burst + completion indicator on league home
description:
When `league.state === "complete"`, the league home screen should feel like a moment:

1. **CSS confetti burst** — fires once on mount, ~55 particles in design-system colors (sage, gold, sage-light, sage-pale, ink), falls and fades over ~3s. Re-fires each time the user navigates to the screen. Pure CSS `@keyframes`, no library. `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events-none`.
2. **Completion indicator** — a serif italic line `"the league is complete."` in muted, below the description/round-count block.

**Design constraints:**

* No Rust (screen's single Rust use stays on delete-league confirm)
* Gold in confetti only — not added to any other element (Gold is for winner moments on round cards)
* No infinite animation — confetti fires once and component unmounts itself after ~3.5s

**Implementation:**

* New component: `frontend/src/components/Confetti.tsx`
* Edit: `frontend/src/pages/LeagueHomeScreen.tsx` — import + render when complete

title: Welcome email on league join + league links in round notification emails
description:
Two related notification improvements:

## 1. Welcome email on league join

Send a transactional email when a user successfully joins a league, via either join path:

* `POST /invites/{token}/accept` (existing logged-in user accepts invite)
* `GET /auth/verify` with an `&invite=` token (join-on-signin flow, [MYS-127](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-127/invite-gated-sign-up-global-user-cap-1500))

**Subject:** `You've joined {league_name}`
**Body:** "You're in! You've joined **{League Name}**. [View {League Name} →](<%7Bleague_url%7D>)"
Includes standard unsubscribe footer.

Only fire when the user actually joined/rejoined — not when an already-active member clicks an old invite link (idempotent path).

## 2. League link in all round lifecycle emails

All 4 round notification emails (`submission_open`, `voting_open`, `round_closed`, `league_complete`) should include a CTA link to the league page: `{APP_BASE_URL}/leagues/{league_id}`.

## Implementation notes

* `_join_via_invite` in `invites.py` should return `bool` (True = actually joined/rejoined, False = already active no-op) so callers can conditionally send the welcome email
* Add `queue_league_joined(background_tasks, sender, settings, email, user_id, league_id, league_name)` to `notifications.py`
* Add `_league_url(settings, league_id)` helper
* `auth.py` needs `BackgroundTasks` + `EmailSender` deps added to `verify_magic_link`
* `invites.py` needs `BackgroundTasks` + `EmailSender` + `Settings` deps added to `accept_invite`

title: Warn on navigation with partial multi-song submission
description:
When a round has songs_per_submission > 1 and the player has submitted some (but not all) songs, navigating away silently drops their incomplete submission.

**Behaviour:** Block in-app navigation with an inline "leave anyway?" dialog (useBlocker), and trigger the browser's native beforeunload prompt on tab close / hard refresh.

**Condition:** round.state === open_submission AND submissions.length > 0 AND submissions.length < cap

Also fixed: the empty slot ordering bug — previously all empty slots were shown simultaneously, allowing out-of-order submission which confused the slot labels. Now only one empty slot is shown at a time (the next sequential one).

title: Deadline force-advance fallback for stalled rounds
description:
**Split from [MYS-69](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-69>) (auto-advance round lifecycle).** [MYS-69](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-69/auto-advance-round-lifecycle-when-everyone-has-acted) shipped the *quorum-based* auto-advance (open voting once everyone has submitted; close once every playing member has voted). This ticket is the **deadline fallback** half of the resolved design:

> Deadlines still force-advance on time even if the quorum isn't met (stalled-round fallback).

## What to build

`app/jobs/advance_rounds.py` — a standalone job (mirrors `purge_accounts.py`) that scans open rounds each run and, in order:

1. **Self-healing stamp:** any `open_submission`/`open_voting` round with a NULL deadline gets it stamped at `now + league window` — never force-advanced on NULL. This is also the rollout policy for rounds in flight at deploy time (decided 2026-07-01): every in-flight round gets a fresh full window; nobody is closed early; the invariant "every open round has a deadline" holds even if a future code path forgets to stamp.
2. **12h warnings** ([MYS-162](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-162>)) to players who haven't acted.
3. **Force-advance:** deadline passed without quorum → `open_submission → open_voting`, `open_voting → closed` (auto-opens the next round / completes the league). Reuse `advance_round_state` + `queue_round_event` — one transition path, one notification path, emails fire once.

### Empty-round guard (decided 2026-07-01)

If `submission_deadline` passes with **zero submissions**, do **not** advance — voting over nothing is meaningless. Hold the round in `open_submission` and email the organizer once (stamp `empty_round_notice_sent_at`, added in [MYS-159](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-159/deadline-schema-submissionvoting-deadline-days-on-leagues-deadline)) suggesting they extend the deadline or advance/close manually.

## Trigger mechanism — RESOLVED (2026-07-01)

**Standalone job + systemd timer on the staging Droplet, every 15 minutes** (matches the `purge_accounts.py` precedent; timer unit alongside the existing service files in `scripts/`, runbook update in `docs/staging-setup.md`).

**Prod follow-up (not in this ticket's acceptance):** App Platform has no native cron. Prod isn't live yet — when it is, pick between a GH Actions schedule hitting an authenticated admin endpoint or a small App Platform worker. Leave a note in `docs/ci-cd.md`.

## Notable edge already handled in [MYS-69](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-69/auto-advance-round-lifecycle-when-everyone-has-acted)

An **all-vibing round** (zero playing voters) chain-closes immediately on opening voting, so it does not rely on this fallback. This ticket covers the *partial-participation* stall (some members never submit/vote).

## Acceptance

* A round past deadline without quorum force-advances to the next state; NULL-deadline rounds get stamped, never advanced
* Zero-submission rounds hold + organizer notified once
* Notifications fire once via `queue_round_event`
* systemd timer wired on staging (15 min cadence), runbook updated

Grounding: [MYS-69](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-69/auto-advance-round-lifecycle-when-everyone-has-acted) resolved design (2026-06-21); deferred per session decision 2026-06-27; player-experience plan + decisions 2026-07-01.

title: Harden multi-song submission against concurrent at-cap race
description:
**Surfaced in the** [MYS-116](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-116/songs-per-submission-admin-configurable-per-league-cap-default-1-max-5) **(songs-per-submission) code review.** Same class of data-integrity gap as [MYS-32](<https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-32>) (concurrent first-join race).

## Problem

[MYS-116](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-116/songs-per-submission-admin-configurable-per-league-cap-default-1-max-5) introduced an admin-configurable per-league cap (`leagues.songs_per_submission`, 1–5) and, to allow more than one submission per (round, user), **dropped the** `uq_submissions_round_user` **unique constraint** (see migration `b7d4e2f09a13`).

The cap is now enforced **only** as an application-layer read-then-write in `backend/app/api/routes/submissions.py` (`add_song`):

```
existing = <player's submissions in this round>
if len(existing) >= cap: 409
... insert new submission
```

There is no row lock and no DB-level backstop. Two concurrent `POST /rounds/:id/submissions` from the same user can both pass the `len(existing) >= cap` check and both insert, exceeding the cap. **At cap == 1 this yields 2 songs for one player in a round** — which breaks invariants the rest of the code now assumes:

* uniform participation stance across a player's songs,
* `mySubmissions[0]` access on the frontend,
* the `votes.py` `.limit(1)` "any one submission answers the stance" gate.

Low probability at friend-group scale (≤20 players, deliberate manual submits), but the dropped constraint removed the guarantee the old schema used to provide for the cap-1 case.

## Options to consider

* A **partial/expression unique constraint** or a row-count check enforced in the DB (the cap is per-league/variable, so a plain unique constraint won't express it directly — may need a trigger or a guarded `INSERT ... WHERE (SELECT count ...) < cap`).
* `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` (or advisory lock) over the player's submissions in the round before the count-and-insert, mirroring the fix approach used for [MYS-32](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-32/harden-league-join-against-concurrent-first-join-race).

## Acceptance

* Two concurrent at-cap submits from the same user cannot both succeed; the second returns 409.
* Regression/concurrency test covering the cap-1 and cap-N at-cap race.

Grounding: review finding, 2026-06-27. Related: [MYS-32](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-32/harden-league-join-against-concurrent-first-join-race) (same read-then-write pattern), [MYS-116](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-116/songs-per-submission-admin-configurable-per-league-cap-default-1-max-5) (origin epic).

title: Organizer can delete a league in any state
description:
**Manual test finding (P2) — rule change.** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

Today `DELETE /leagues/:id` blocks deletion while a league is in progress: `delete_league` (`backend/app/api/routes/leagues.py`) raises **409 "cannot delete a league that is in progress"** when `state == "active" and current_round > 0`. New rule: **an organizer can delete their league at any time, no matter the state.**

## Fix

* Backend: drop the in-progress guard in `delete_league`; keep the organizer-only authorization. The cascade (votes → notes → submissions → rounds → invites → members → league) already handles a mid-round league.
* Frontend: no change needed — the two-step "this can't be undone" confirm already covers it; the 409 in-progress path just goes away.
* Update `test_leagues_delete` (the in-progress-409 test becomes "deletes in any state") and the frontend delete-league 409 test if present.

Note: this is genuinely destructive (deleting an active round wipes everyone's submissions/votes) — the confirm copy already says so.

title: Join league: an existing member should land on the league, not an error
description:
**Manual test finding (P2).** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

When a player who is already an active member opens an invite link and taps join, `POST /invites/:token/accept` returns **409 "already a member"** (`invites.py:113`) and `JoinLeagueRoute` surfaces it as an error. They should just be taken to the league.

## Fix

Make accept **idempotent**: if the caller is already an active member, return the league (200) instead of 409. The frontend already navigates to `/leagues/{id}` on a successful accept, so no client change is needed beyond removing the now-dead error path. Update `test_invites_preview_accept` accordingly.

title: Vibing rules: votable vibers + anonymous voting + viewer-gated reveal
description:
Implements the **behavioral** half of the [MYS-112](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-112/define-andquotjust-vibingandquot-behavior-decision-unblock-vibing-ui) decision. Revises [MYS-20](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-20/voting-system-and-just-vibing-mode) (voting) and [MYS-23](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-23/round-results-endpoint) (results). Under the decision, "just vibing" is private and the only difference from a player is that a viber doesn't cast votes — their song still competes, anonymously.

## Voting (revises [MYS-20](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-20/voting-system-and-just-vibing-mode))

* Remove the "can't vote for a vibing song — leave a note instead" guard: vibing songs are votable.
* Keep: a vibing submitter can't cast votes; nobody can vote for their own song.
* Playlist response: **stop exposing each entry's** `participation_mode`; remove the separate "just vibing" section + per-entry badges → one anonymous, votable list. A *vibing viewer* still sits out voting (derived from their own submission via `getMySubmission`, not from the entries).

## Reveal (revises [MYS-23](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-23/round-results-endpoint))

* Leaderboard now **includes vibers** (they compete and can win).
* **Gate the reveal by the viewer's** `participation_mode` **for the round, server-side:**
  * Player → full reveal (winner(s), Most Noted, leaderboard, all picks).
  * Viber → **winner(s) + Most Noted only**; omit the leaderboard, the picks list, and all vote counts.
  * A member who never submitted → treated as a player.
* Remove "just vibing" badges from the reveal (vibing stays private).

## Dependencies / notes

* Blocked by [MYS-112](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-112/define-andquotjust-vibingandquot-behavior-decision-unblock-vibing-ui) (decision). Pairs with [MYS-60](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-60/no-ui-to-set-just-vibing-participation-mode) (the schema/toggle that actually lets users be vibers).
* The [MYS-101](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-101/show-submission-progress-x-of-y-players-submitted-on-the-round-league) / [MYS-102](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-102/show-voting-progress-x-of-y-votednoted-z-just-vibing-on-the-voting) progress displays remain valid (aggregate counts, not identities).
* Decide commit ordering with [MYS-60](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-60/no-ui-to-set-just-vibing-participation-mode); the rules changes key off `submissions.participation_mode` (already exists), so they can be developed/tested against seeded modes independently.

title: UX overhaul (epic)
description:
**Epic / parent** for the design-led UX overhaul. From the ideas list (`docs/idea-scratch.md`).

## Context

A coordinated pass on the app's experience rather than piecemeal UI tweaks. **New wireframes are expected from Claude Designer (\~2 days from 2026-06-22).** This epic is the container; child tickets get carved as wireframes land — **pick low-hanging fruit opportunistically** and pull it forward when it's cheap.

## In scope (children)

* **3-step help overlays** per page (dismissable, re-openable via info icon, with an animation showing how to play) — deferred here from the ideas list until the redesign.
* **WCAG accessibility** — bring the app to full WCAG conformance as part of the overhaul (same surfaces, do it once).
* Further children to be added from the forthcoming wireframes.

## Guardrails

All work stays within the style guide (`docs/design/style-guide.md`) — quiet/restrained aesthetic, concentric-ring motif, one Rust accent per screen, DM Serif/Mono, underline inputs, rotating-ring loaders (no spinners).

## Done when

The overhaul children are scoped from the wireframes and shipped; the app reflects the new design and meets WCAG.

title: Surface a comment on your own submission in the submit UI
description:
From the ideas list (`docs/idea-scratch.md`): *"Leave a comment on the song YOU are submitting."*

## Scope is small — backend is already done

`submissions.note` exists in the model (`app/models/submission.py`) and is **fully wired** through `app/api/routes/submissions.py`: the create/update payload accepts `note`, and it's returned in the submission response. So this is **frontend-only**.

## Display rule (decided 2026-06-22)

The comment is shown **during the voting round (**`open_voting`**) but anonymously** — voters see the submitter's "why I picked this" next to the (anonymous, shuffled) song to add context, **without revealing who wrote it**. This is *different* from voting notes ([MYS-67](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-67/voting-notes-left-by-other-players-are-visible-before-the-reveal)), which stay hidden until reveal. Attribution surfaces at reveal along with everything else.

* The submitter always sees/edits their own comment.
* Must not leak authorship during voting — align with the anonymous playlist (PlaylistEntry has no owner; [MYS-68](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-68/voting-playlist-mark-the-callers-own-submission-enabler)).

## Build

* Add an optional **comment input** to the song-submission form (short "why I picked this", max 280 to match the model/notes convention). Underline-style input per the style guide.
* Render the comment on each anonymous voting playlist entry during `open_voting`.
* Verify existing frontend `note` references (LeagueHome / RoundDetail) are the voting `SongNotes` feature, not this — avoid duplication.

## Done when

A player can attach/edit a comment on their own submission; it shows anonymously alongside the song during voting and is attributed at reveal, with a frontend test confirming no authorship leak pre-reveal.

title: Define "Just Vibing" behavior (decision) — unblock vibing UI
description:
**Decision recorded** (was: define the semantics). "Just vibing" is a **private, per-round participation mode**. The only behavioral difference from a normal player is that a viber does not cast votes — their song still competes, fully and anonymously.

## Behavior

1. **Vibers don't cast votes.** They can listen to the whole playlist and optionally leave notes.
2. **A viber's song competes like any other** — it's in the voting pool, votable by players, and can win (counts toward votes + leaderboard).
3. **Vibing is invisible to others.** During voting, players vote on every song and cannot tell which were submitted by vibers (no badge anywhere). Nobody ever sees who vibed.
4. **Reveal is gated by the viewer's mode for that round:**
   * **Player** → full reveal: winner(s), Most Noted, full leaderboard/rankings, all picks.
   * **Viber** → winner(s) + Most Noted only — no leaderboard, no per-round rankings, no picks list, no vote counts.
   * A member who never submitted is treated as a **player** for reveal gating.
5. **Setting it:** league default (admin, at creation) → seeds each member's per-league toggle (changeable anytime) → per-round override ("Just Vibes for this Round").

## Data model

Precedence: **round override → per-league member setting → league default**.

* `leagues.default_vibe_mode` (bool) — admin default at creation. **(new)**
* `league_members.vibe_mode` (bool) — per-league member setting, seeded from the league default at join, toggleable anytime. **(new)**
* `submissions.participation_mode` (playing|vibing) — per-round override; at submit, defaults from the member's per-league setting if not overridden. *(exists)*
* `users.default_vibe_mode` — **dropped**, superseded by the per-league setting (remove column + onboarding/profile plumbing). *(exists)*

## Implementation tickets

* [MYS-60](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-60/no-ui-to-set-just-vibing-participation-mode) — toggle UI + schema (league default, per-league toggle, per-round override; drop `users.default_vibe_mode`).
* **\[competition-rules ticket\]** — votable vibers + anonymous voting playlist + viewer-gated reveal. Revises [MYS-20](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-20/voting-system-and-just-vibing-mode) / [MYS-23](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-23/round-results-endpoint).

Note: the [MYS-101](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-101/show-submission-progress-x-of-y-players-submitted-on-the-round-league) / [MYS-102](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-102/show-voting-progress-x-of-y-votednoted-z-just-vibing-on-the-voting) progress displays remain valid — they show aggregate counts, never identities.

Deliverable still open: write this decision into `docs/` (and/or PRD).

title: Auto-refresh round/league state via 60s polling
description:
From the ideas list (`docs/idea-scratch.md`).

## What

Auto-update **round and league state** in the browser via lightweight ~60s polling so players see transitions (submission→voting→closed, counts, new submissions) without a manual refresh. **State only — depending on the screen** (don't poll heavy/full payloads).

## Grounding

No client polling exists today (no `setInterval` in `frontend/src`). Pairs with [MYS-88](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-88/spike-streamline-page-load-api-calls-reduce-calls-collapse-the-round) (page-load API-call spike) — coordinate so polling doesn't reintroduce the round-view waterfall. Lean on a narrow state endpoint (round.state, current_round, counts) rather than re-fetching the full round/playlist each tick.

## Build

* Per-screen polling: round detail polls round/league state; league home polls league + round states. Stop/pause when the tab is hidden (`visibilitychange`) to save calls.
* ~60s interval, configurable; clean up on unmount.
* Reconcile gracefully when state changes mid-view (e.g. voting opened) — update UI without jarring resets.

## Done when

Open round/league views reflect state changes within ~60s with no manual refresh, polling pauses on hidden tabs, and call volume stays modest (verified against [MYS-88](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-88/spike-streamline-page-load-api-calls-reduce-calls-collapse-the-round) concerns).

title: Round progress visibility: submitted/voted counts (no names)
description:
From the ideas list (`docs/idea-scratch.md`).

## What

Show **progress counts only** for the active round:

* On the **round tile** (league home): how many members have **submitted** (during `open_submission`) / **voted** (during `open_voting`) — e.g. `4/6 submitted`, `3/6 voted`.
* The same count is fine in round detail.

## Product decision (2026-06-22): counts only — NO names

**We do not surface who has / hasn't acted.** This deliberately drops the original idea's "clicking into the round shows who has NOT yet submitted/voted" — only aggregate counts are shown, to no one's name. Keeps anonymity and avoids singling people out.

## Grounding
