The quorum/who-has-acted computation already exists for [MYS-69](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-69/auto-advance-round-lifecycle-when-everyone-has-acted) (auto-advance keys off "members active when the round opened"). Reuse its denominator/rules for the count (late joiners, vibing players don't count toward the voting quorum — confirm against [MYS-69](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-69/auto-advance-round-lifecycle-when-everyone-has-acted)'s resolved design). We only need the **count**, not the identities.

## Build

* **Backend:** expose per-round `submitted_count` / `voted_count` + the quorum denominator. No member identities, no per-member acted/not-acted list.
* **Frontend:** count badge on the tile; same in round detail.

## Done when

Tile + round detail show live `n/total` submitted/voted counts with no identities exposed, with tests.

title: Apple Music: ISRC catalog matching upgrade in song_links.py (Phase A)
description:
**Phase A — cheapest, highest-value Apple work; no user auth** (spike: [MYS-79](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-79/spike-apple-music-integration-links-playlist-generation), `docs/discovery/spike-apple-music.md` §2, §7). Recommended first build once the developer token exists.

## What to build

Replace the current **keyless, fuzzy** Apple Music link path with an **exact ISRC catalog lookup**.

* Today: `_apple_exact` in `app/services/song_links.py` searches the iTunes Search API by `term=title+artist` and takes the first result.
* Change: call `GET https://api.music.apple.com/v1/catalog/{storefront}/songs?filter[isrc]={ISRC}` with the **developer token** ([MYS-105](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-105/apple-music-developer-token-service-es256-jwt-signing)). Use the user's storefront where known (default e.g. `us`); one ISRC can map to multiple songs → score/pick (ISRC + title/artist/duration), mirroring [MYS-76](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-76/spike-auto-generate-streaming-playlists-youtube-deezer-spotify-as) §8.
* **Graceful fallback** to the existing iTunes-Search result, then the deep link, exactly like the current best-effort pattern — no caller changes.
* Developer token only; **no Music User Token / no user auth** for this ticket.

## Done when

Apple links resolve via ISRC catalog lookup with the existing fallback chain intact, covered by tests (mocked transport) for the ISRC-hit, multi-result-scoring, and fallback paths.

title: Show voting progress (X of Y voted/noted, Z just vibing) on the voting screen
description:
**Manual test finding (P2).** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

On the voting screen, show **"X out of Y players have voted or noted, and Z are just vibing."** Sibling of the submission-progress display; needs vote/note participation counts + the vibing count for the round.

title: Show submission progress (X of Y players submitted) on the round + league card
description:

1. The **round submit screen** (`RoundDetailRoute`, open_submission).
2. The **league round card** (`LeagueHomeRoute`) when the round is open.

Needs the league member count + the round's submission count surfaced to the client. Pairs with the voting-progress display (separate issue) and the `docs/idea-scratch.md` "see who has submitted/voted on the tile" idea.

title: League: allow the organizer to grant another member admin (co-organizers)

Leagues currently have a **single** `organizer_id` (`leagues` table). Add the ability to promote another member to **admin / co-organizer**. New capability — needs a data-model change (multiple admins per league, e.g. a role on `league_members` or a join table) plus authorization updates everywhere organizer-only actions are gated. Bigger than the remove-player UI ([MYS-98](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-98/league-ui-for-the-organizer-to-remove-a-player)); scope deliberately.

title: League: UI for the organizer to remove a player
description:
League: UI for the organizer to remove a player.

**Closed as delivered by** [MYS-128](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-128/platform-admin-hard-delete-user-organizer-kick-ui) **(PR #69):** the organizer-only "remove from league" action is wired into the league members list, backed by the existing `DELETE /leagues/{id}/members/{userId}` (`remove_member`). Reopen if the shipped UI doesn't meet the intended scope.

title: League: let a member leave a league
description:
**Manual test finding (P2)** — the "or leave league" half of an account finding. `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

A player has no way to **leave a league** they've joined. Add a self-removal action.

* Backend: `DELETE /leagues/:id/members/:userId` exists but is organizer-only (`removeMember`) — needs a self-leave authorization path (a member removing themselves), with sensible handling if the leaver is the organizer or has active submissions.
* Frontend: a "leave league" affordance on the league screen.

(The other half of the finding — "change name" — is folded into the profile/settings work, [MYS-61](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-61/no-profilesettings-screen-preferred-service-account-deletion).)

title: Round/league: live-refresh state for non-admins (poll ~30s or websocket)
description:
**Manual test finding (P2).** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

Non-admin players don't see round/league state changes (a round opening, voting closing, advancing) without a manual refresh. Add **live refresh of round + league state** for non-admins — polling (~30s) or websockets, whichever fits best.

**Decide:** poll vs websocket; and the interval (tester said 30s; `docs/idea-scratch.md` said 60s — pick one). Scope to round + league state only (not full data), per screen.

title: Round: "Opening…" button stays on screen after the round opens
description:
**Manual test finding (P2) — bug.** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

When the organizer opens a round, the **"Opening…"** (loading) button stays visible after the round has opened. It should clear once the round transitions to open (the loading state isn't reset / the view doesn't reflect the new state). `frontend/src/pages/RoundDetailRoute.tsx` (organizer open-round action).

title: Spotify connect: return to the originating round after OAuth, not /home
description:
**Follow-up to** [MYS-92](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-92/authspotify-oauth-connect-return-lands-authenticated-user-on-login)**.** After connecting Spotify, the user now lands on `/home` (fixed the login bounce), but should land back on the **round they connected from** so they can immediately generate.

## Approach

Thread the return path through the OAuth `state` (the only value that round-trips through Spotify):

* Frontend: `connectSpotify(returnTo)` passes `?return_to=/rounds/:id`; `SpotifyPlaylist` supplies its `roundId`.
* Backend `GET /spotify/connect`: validate `return_to` is a safe in-app path and encode it in the signed `state` JWT.
* Backend callback: decode `return_to` from state and redirect to `{app_base_url}{return_to}?spotify=connected` (fallback `/home`).

## Security

`return_to` is **signed into the state** (tamper-proof) and validated to be a single-slash-rooted relative path (reject `//`, schemes, backslashes) — no open-redirect. The callback concatenates it after our own `app_base_url`, so the target is always our domain.

## Reference

`backend/app/auth/jwt.py` (`create_oauth_state`/`decode_oauth_state`), `app/api/routes/spotify.py` (connect + callback), `frontend/src/services/api.ts` (`connectSpotify`), `frontend/src/components/SpotifyPlaylist.tsx`.

title: Spotify playlist: persist playlist id per (round, user) instead of name-matching reuse
description:
**From the PR #54 (**[MYS-87](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-87/spotify-playlist-reuse-same-named-playlist-instead-of-creating)**) code review — altitude finding.**

[MYS-87](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-87/spotify-playlist-reuse-same-named-playlist-instead-of-creating) makes playlist generation idempotent by matching on the playlist **name** (`find_playlist_id_by_name`). That works for the common case but the title is mutable and not guaranteed unique, so name-matching stays fragile:

* **Title drift defeats reuse** → duplicate + orphan: organizer edits the round theme or league name (both feed the title), or the user renames the playlist in Spotify → the next generate finds no match and creates a second playlist.
* **Title collision overwrites the wrong playlist**: two rounds in a league sharing a theme, or names that truncate to the same 100 chars → regenerating one replaces another round's tracks (silent cross-round data loss).
* **Heavy libraries**: the 500-playlist scan cap means users with many playlists never hit reuse → duplicate every time.

## Deeper fix

Persist the created playlist id and reuse by id (O(1), rename-proof, collision-free):

* Add a nullable `spotify_playlist_id` keyed on **(round_id, user/connection)** — either a column on a per-round-per-user record or a small `spotify_round_playlists` table (round_id, user_id, playlist_id, created_at).
* On generate: look it up; if present, replace tracks on that id directly (no `/me/playlists` scan); else create and store the id. Optionally refresh the title/description on reuse so a renamed round's playlist re-titles.
* Handle the case where the stored playlist was deleted in Spotify (404 on PUT → recreate + update stored id).

## Reference

`backend/app/services/spotify_client.py` (`find_playlist_id_by_name`), `app/api/routes/spotify.py` (`create_round_spotify_playlist`). Cheap mitigations already applied in PR #54: owner-filter, transient-error surfacing, `next`-only pagination.

title: Spike: streamline page-load API calls (reduce calls + collapse the round-view waterfall)
description:
**Spike / research — do not implement from this ticket.** Scope follow-up tickets once we pick an approach.

## Why

Page load fires a lot of API calls, and the heaviest screen (round detail in `open_voting`) has a **serial waterfall** before its parallel batch:

```
getRound(id)
  → getLeague(round.league_id)        # waterfall — waits on getRound
     → Promise.all[ getPlaylist, getMyVotes, getMySubmission ]   # 3 parallel
     + getSpotifyStatus                # SpotifyPlaylist mounts separately
```

~6 calls with a 2-step waterfall. (`frontend/src/pages/RoundDetailRoute.tsx` `load()`.)

## Findings / candidate wins (validate + measure)

1. `getSpotifyStatus` **is user-global** (configured/connected don't change per round) but is fetched on every voting view — should be fetched once per session and cached. *Low effort.*
2. `getMySubmission` **in** `open_voting` **looks redundant** — the playlist already returns `is_own` + `participation_mode` per entry ([MYS-68](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-68/voting-playlist-mark-the-callers-own-submission-enabler)), so "which is mine / am I vibing" is derivable from `getPlaylist`. *Low–med.*
3. `getRound` **→** `getLeague` **waterfall** — include a league summary in the round response (or fetch in parallel) to drop a serial round-trip. *Med.*
4. **Consolidated** `GET /rounds/:id/view` returning round + league + playlist + my votes (+ my submission) in one shot — collapses the whole waterfall to 1 call. *Higher; biggest win.*
5. **No client-side query cache** — round→round navigation refetches the same league; home refetches leagues each visit. Evaluate SWR/React Query (or a light cache). *Higher; broad.*
6. Also review `LeagueHomeRoute` (getLeague + getRounds + getLeagueMembers + getResults) for similar collapsing.

## Questions to answer

* Measure actual on-load call counts + timing per screen (round detail by state, league home, home).
* Which approach gives the best latency win per effort: per-call caching (#1/#2/#5) vs. a server-side bootstrap endpoint (#4)?
* Does a bootstrap endpoint fit the existing API design (`docs/technical/technical-design.md` §7), or add a read-model/BFF-style endpoint?
* Staleness/caching policy if we add a client cache (invalidation on vote/submit/state-change).

## Deliverable

Short findings doc (recommend `docs/discovery/`) with measured call counts, a recommended approach, and a proposed ticket breakdown. No production code.

Context: surfaced after the Spotify playlist work ([MYS-83](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-83/playlist-spotify-per-user-oauth-create-saved-playlist-for-a-round)/87) added the per-round `getSpotifyStatus` call.

title: Spotify playlist: include league name in the playlist title
description:
**Manual test finding (P2) from** [MYS-83](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-83/playlist-spotify-per-user-oauth-create-saved-playlist-for-a-round)**.** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

The generated Spotify playlist title is currently `MysteryMixClub — Round N: Theme` (`backend/app/services/spotify_playlist.py` `playlist_name`), with **no league name**.

**Want:** `MysteryMixClub: {League Name}, {Round theme}` — e.g. `MysteryMixClub: Friday Mixtape, Late Summer Feels`. Fall back to `Round N` when the round has no theme yet.

## Sketch

* `playlist_name` needs the league name; the create-playlist route (`create_round_spotify_playlist` in `backend/app/api/routes/spotify.py`) has `round_.league_id` but not the league record — load the league (or pass its name) to build the title.
* Update `playlist_description` similarly if desired.
* Update the `spotify_playlist` unit tests for the new format.

## Reference

`backend/app/services/spotify_playlist.py`, `backend/app/api/routes/spotify.py`.

title: Spotify playlist: login should be a popup/modal, not a full-page redirect
description:
**Manual test finding (P1) from** [MYS-83](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-83/playlist-spotify-per-user-oauth-create-saved-playlist-for-a-round)**.** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

The "connect spotify" flow currently does a **full-page redirect** to Spotify's consent page (`window.location.assign(authorize_url)` in `frontend/src/components/SpotifyPlaylist.tsx`), and the backend callback redirects the whole tab back to `APP_BASE_URL/?spotify=connected`. The user loses their place in the app (the round they were on).

**Want:** open consent in a **popup window** (or modal), complete the OAuth there, then close it and refresh connect status in place — the round view stays put.

## Sketch

* Frontend: `window.open(authorize_url, "spotify-connect", "width=…,height=…")` instead of `location.assign`; poll for the popup closing (or listen for a `postMessage`) then re-fetch `getSpotifyStatus()`.
* Backend callback (`GET /spotify/callback`): when the flow runs in a popup, return a tiny HTML page that `postMessage`s success/failure to `window.opener` and `window.close()`s, instead of a `303` back to the SPA. Keep the redirect form as a fallback (e.g. when there's no opener).
* Mind origins: popup is on `127.0.0.1:8000` (the callback), opener on `localhost:5173` — `postMessage` must target the app origin explicitly.

## Reference

`frontend/src/components/SpotifyPlaylist.tsx` (`handleConnect`), `backend/app/api/routes/spotify.py` (`spotify_callback`).

title: Playlist: Spotify per-user OAuth + create saved playlist for a round
description:
**Phase 2 of the streaming-playlist rollout** (spike: [MYS-76](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-76/spike-auto-generate-streaming-playlists-youtube-deezer-spotify-as), `docs/discovery/spike-playlist-generation.md`). Phase 1 (keyless YouTube `watch_videos` link) shipped in [MYS-78](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-78/playlist-one-click-youtube-playlist-link-for-a-round-watch-videos-no). This is the first OAuth-backed "real playlist" service. Spotify is sequenced before Deezer because its API access is the most reliable and ISRC matching is clean (spike §5 recommendation).

## Goal

From a round's set of submissions, let a player create a **real saved Spotify playlist in their own library** containing the full mix, surfaced as a clickable link — via an explicit "Connect Spotify" action.

## Auth model

Per-user OAuth (Authorization Code flow). There is **no anonymous / link-only Spotify playlist creation** (spike §3.1). Scopes: `playlist-modify-public` and/or `playlist-modify-private`.

* OAuth token exchange and refresh-token storage **must be server-side** (client secret never reaches the browser).
* Gate behind an explicit connect-account action; persist the user↔Spotify connection so it's a one-time consent.

## Track resolution (no Odesli)

⚠️ **Correction to the spike:** the spike's "re-resolve through Odesli" path is dead — **Odesli was dropped entirely in** [MYS-81](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-81/migrate-off-odesli-public-api-before-it-is-retired-2026-07-31). Resolve each submission directly against Spotify:

* `GET /v1/search?q=isrc:{ISRC}&type=track` using an **app token (client-credentials)** — ISRC-exact, no user auth needed for matching. We already store `submissions.isrc`.
* Cache the resolved Spotify track URI on the submission to avoid repeat lookups.
* **Unmatched-tracks escape hatch** (spike §8): show the player anything we couldn't place rather than silently dropping it.

## Build outline

* Spotify app registration; `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID` / `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET` as secrets (local `.env.example`, staging, prod — follow the secret-adding steps in CLAUDE.md / `docs/ci-cd.md`).
* Backend: connect/callback OAuth endpoints (server-side token exchange + refresh), a resolver that maps a round → Spotify track URIs (client-credentials ISRC search, cached), and a create-playlist flow (`POST /v1/users/{id}/playlists` → `POST /v1/playlists/{id}/tracks`).
* Frontend: "Connect Spotify" + "Generate Spotify playlist" affordance on the round (open_voting and/or closed views), per the design system. Returns a clickable playlist link + an unmatched-tracks summary.

## Risks to validate before/while building

* New Spotify apps start in **development mode** (capped users until a quota-extension review). Confirm the approval/quota path.
* Several Web API endpoints were deprecated in late 2024; confirm playlist + search endpoints are current against live docs before coding (spike volatility note).

## Reference

`docs/discovery/spike-playlist-generation.md` §3.1, §4, §5; Odesli removal in [MYS-81](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-81/migrate-off-odesli-public-api-before-it-is-retired-2026-07-31); YouTube Phase 1 precedent in [MYS-78](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-78/playlist-one-click-youtube-playlist-link-for-a-round-watch-videos-no) (`youtube_playlist.py`, `PlaylistResponse` shape).

title: Enforce league participation cap (max 20 players)
description:
**Gap found during** [MYS-78](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-78/playlist-one-click-youtube-playlist-link-for-a-round-watch-videos-no)**.** A league is *intended* to cap participation at **20 players**, but nothing in the backend enforces it. Today `invites.py` only computes a `member_count` for the invite-preview display, and the only numeric league cap in code is `total_rounds ≤ 50` (rounds, not people). Nothing rejects the 21st member from joining.

## Goal

Enforce the 20-player cap at the join path so a league can't exceed it.

## Scope / questions

* Add a capacity check when a user accepts an invite / joins a league → reject (409/422) with a clear "this league is full (20 players)" message when at capacity.
* Confirm the exact number (20) and whether the organizer counts toward it.
* Consider surfacing remaining slots in the invite preview (we already compute `member_count`).
* Make the limit a named constant, not a magic number.
* Guard against the race where two concurrent joins both pass the check (DB-level constraint or transactional count).

## Notes

Until this lands, downstream code must not assume ≤20 participants — e.g. [MYS-78](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-78/playlist-one-click-youtube-playlist-link-for-a-round-watch-videos-no) keeps a defensive `_MAX_VIDEOS = 50` cap on the YouTube playlist link rather than relying on the unenforced rule.

title: Playlist: one-click YouTube playlist link for a round (watch_videos, no auth)
description:
**Pilot from** [MYS-76](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-76/spike-auto-generate-streaming-playlists-youtube-deezer-spotify-as)**. Re-scoped 2026-06-21** — the original Odesli-based approach is unworkable and has been abandoned (PR #49 closed).

## Why re-scoped

The original plan resolved YouTube video ids at playlist time via Odesli. Verified against real data: keyless Odesli returns **no youtube/spotify/apple** links (only long-tail platforms), and the Odesli public API is being **retired 2026-07-31** (see [MYS-81](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-81/migrate-off-odesli-public-api-before-it-is-retired-2026-07-31)). iTunes/Apple returns no YouTube data either. There is no keyless/free path to a YouTube video id — the only supported source is the **YouTube Data API**.

## Revised approach — YouTube Data API, resolved & cached at submit time

* When a song is submitted/resolved, call YouTube Data API `search.list` (title + artist) to get the top video id and store it in `submissions.youtube_video_id` (column already exists). One-time per song; playlist build makes zero live calls.
* `get_round_playlist` builds the `watch_videos` URL purely from stored ids (remove the per-view Odesli resolve).
* Quota is trivial: `search.list` = 100 units / 10,000 per day; ≤20 songs per round, cached.

## Reusable from the shelved Odesli branch (PR #49)

* `youtube_playlist.py` — `build_watch_videos_url`, `normalize_video_ids` → **keep**.
* `submissions.youtube_video_id` column + migration → **keep**.
* Frontend `YouTubePlaylistLink` + `PlaylistResponse` fields (`youtube_playlist_url`, `youtube_track_count`) → **keep**.
* **Replace:** the Odesli resolve-at-playlist-time logic in `rounds.py` (`_resolvable_track_url`, `_youtube_video_id_for`) → YouTube Data API resolution at submit time.

## Blocked on

* A Google Cloud **YouTube Data API key** (`YOUTUBE_API_KEY`) — needs creating and adding as a secret (local `.env`, staging, prod).

## Reference

`docs/discovery/spike-playlist-generation.md`; Odesli sunset context in [MYS-81](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-81/migrate-off-odesli-public-api-before-it-is-retired-2026-07-31).

title: Voting: make your own submission visually obvious
description:
On the voting screen, make it obvious which song is the player's own — both a visual indicator and a short text label ("your pick") — so they understand why it isn't selectable.

**Blocked by** the playlist owner flag ([MYS-68](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-68/voting-playlist-mark-the-callers-own-submission-enabler)). Pairs with [MYS-73](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-73/voting-prevent-selecting-your-own-song-in-the-ui) (prevent selecting your own song).

**Style-guide note:** keep it in the Sage/Ink family; Rust is reserved for one signal per screen.

Source: manual testing (`docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`), 2026-06-21.

title: Voting: prevent selecting your own song in the UI
description:
A player can select their own song on the voting screen. The API already rejects it (`POST /rounds/:id/votes` → 409 "you can't vote for your own song", `backend/app/api/routes/votes.py:104`), so this is a UI gap: the song shouldn't be selectable in the first place — currently you only find out at cast time.

**Blocked by** the playlist owner flag ([MYS-68](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-68/voting-playlist-mark-the-callers-own-submission-enabler)): the playlist is anonymous, so the UI can't currently identify the player's own entry to disable it.

**Expected:** the player's own song is rendered non-selectable (and clearly marked — see related issue).

Source: manual testing (`docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`), 2026-06-21.

title: Results: make the notes under each song collapsible
description:
On the results/reveal screen, the notes listed under each song can get long. Make each song's notes collapsible (collapsed or summarized by default, expandable) to keep the reveal scannable.

Source: manual testing (`docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`), 2026-06-21.

title: Results: add a winners highlight (keep Most Noted on top)
description:
Surface the round's winning song(s) prominently on the results screen.

**Constraint (per decision):** keep **Most Noted** as the top element and the single Rust moment of the reveal (established in [MYS-24](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-24/round-reveal-and-results-ui)). Add the winners highlight as a secondary element rather than reordering it above Most Noted — so the one-Rust-per-screen rule stays intact.

Ties: name every co-winner (winner detection already handles ties via top `vote_count`).

Source: manual testing (`docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`), 2026-06-21.

title: Voting: highlight which songs you voted for
description:
On the voting screen, give the songs the player has selected a clear highlighted state so the current vote set is obvious at a glance.

**Style-guide note:** use the Sage family for the selected state (e.g. Sage Pale fill / Sage border) — not Rust, which is reserved for a single signal per screen.

Source: manual testing (`docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`), 2026-06-21.

title: Voting playlist: mark the caller's own submission (enabler)
description:
The voting playlist is anonymous by design — `PlaylistEntry` carries no owner field and entries are shuffled (`backend/app/api/routes/rounds.py:276`, `:330`). As a result the frontend can't tell which song belongs to the current player, which blocks two voting UX asks (preventing self-vote selection in the UI, and highlighting your own submission).

**Proposed:** add an `is_own` boolean to `PlaylistEntry` (true for the caller's submission), without exposing any other player's identity. Anonymity for everyone else is preserved.

Enabler for the two follow-ups it blocks.

Source: manual testing (`docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`), 2026-06-21.

title: Voting: notes left by other players are visible before the reveal
description:
While a round is `open_voting`, a player can see notes other players have left on submissions — they should stay hidden until the reveal.

Confirmed: `GET /submissions/:id/notes` (`list_notes`) has no state gate, and the voting playlist's `SongNotes` component lazily loads and displays all notes (`frontend/src/pages/RoundDetailRoute.tsx:716+`).

**Expected:** during `open_voting`, a player sees only their own notes (the ones they're authoring); everyone's notes appear at close on the results screen.

**Fix options:** gate the notes list endpoint by round state (return only the caller's own until closed), and/or hide others' notes in the voting UI. Backend gating is the safer fix.

Source: manual testing (`docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`), 2026-06-21.

title: Show round winner + Most Noted on closed-round cards (league page)
description:
## Summary

On the league page, each closed round's card should surface that round's outcome at a glance: the **winner** (most votes) and the **Most Noted** submission. Ties show all tied entries.

Builds on the [MYS-62](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-62/pre-created-rounds-bulk-creation-pending-state-and-admin-descriptions) round cards (RoundRow in LeagueHomeScreen). Today the winner/most-noted are only available via the per-round results endpoint (`GET /rounds/:id/results`) and the `most_noted` service; the rounds-list payload (`GET /leagues/:id/rounds`) does not carry them.

## Definitions

* **Winner**: the *playing* submission(s) with the highest vote count (> 0), consistent with the results leaderboard (vibing submissions don't compete). Display submitter display_name + "Title — Artist". Tie → show all.
* **Most Noted**: submission(s) with the highest note count (> 0), participation-mode-agnostic (reuse `compute_most_noted`). Display "Title — Artist" + submitter. Tie → show all.
* Only on **closed** rounds. No votes → omit winner line. No notes → omit Most Noted line.

## Backend

* Add a per-round summary for closed rounds to the rounds-list response (extend RoundResponse with an optional `result_summary`, populated only when state == "closed"; null otherwise).
* Compute efficiently for all closed rounds in the league (batch aggregate queries, not N+1): vote tally per submission (join submissions/users, playing only) → winners at max>0; note tally → reuse/mirror `compute_most_noted` for the tie set.
* `result_summary` shape: `{ winners: [{display_name, title, artist, vote_count}], most_noted: [{title, artist, note_count, submitter_display_name}] }`.

## Frontend

* In RoundRow (closed state) show a compact winner line and a Most Noted line, within the design system (small mono labels, Sage/Ink; NO Rust — multiple closed cards would each want it, violating one-Rust-per-screen). Ties list all entries compactly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Closed round cards on the league page show the winner (most votes) and the Most Noted submission.
- [ ] Ties display all tied winners / all tied most-noted.
- [ ] Rounds with no votes omit the winner line; rounds with no notes omit the Most Noted line.
- [ ] Non-closed rounds show no summary.
- [ ] Rounds-list summary computed without N+1 queries; backend + frontend tests cover ties, no-votes, no-notes.

title: Pre-created rounds: bulk creation, pending state, and admin descriptions
description:
## Summary

Let an admin (organizer) create all of a league's rounds up front. All rounds are visible to every player, but only one round is active at a time. Admin can edit a round's theme and description any time **before** it opens.

This inverts today's model: rounds are currently created one at a time and are born already active (`open_submission`); `create_round` blocks creating a new round until the current one is `closed`.

## Data model (`rounds`)

* Add `description TEXT NULL` — free-text, admin's space to expound / add color. (`theme` stays as the round's name/prompt.)
* Add a new lifecycle state `pending`. Machine becomes (still forward-only): `pending -> open_submission -> open_voting -> closed`.
* Bulk-created rounds are born `pending`.

Note: this is design drift from technical-design §6 (rounds had only `theme` and a 3-state machine). Reconcile the doc as part of the work.

## Creation — bulk

* New endpoint to create all rounds at once as `pending` (e.g. `POST /leagues/:id/rounds:batch`, organizer only), payload a list of `{theme, description?, deadlines?, votes_per_player?}`.
* The bulk payload sets `leagues.total_rounds` to the count.
* Guards: league not `complete`; no existing rounds.

## Activation — admin can do both

* **Auto:** closing round N auto-opens round N+1 (`pending -> open_submission`). Closing the final round completes the league (existing behavior).
* **Manual:** admin can open a `pending` round via `PATCH /rounds/:id` (state -> `open_submission`), guarded so it only works when no other round is currently active.
* Round 1 has no prior close, so the admin opens it manually to start the league.
* The single-active-round guard moves from create-time to open-time.

## Edit lock — lock theme/description at open

* `theme` and `description`: editable **only while** `pending`; frozen once the round opens.
* `submission_deadline` / `voting_deadline`: editable until `closed` (unchanged).

## Viewing

* `GET /leagues/:id/rounds` already returns all rounds to members, so `pending` rounds (themes, descriptions, order) become visible to all players. Response carries `state` so the UI can render them as "upcoming." Players can see future themes — intended.

## Frontend

* Admin bulk-create form (all rounds at once).
* "Upcoming rounds" view showing pending rounds to all members.
* `description` field in create/edit; edit form disables theme/description once a round is open.
* Must follow docs/design/style-guide.md.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Admin can create all rounds for a league in one action; they land as `pending` and set `total_rounds`.
- [ ] All members can view all rounds, including upcoming/pending ones.
- [ ] Only one round is ever active (`open_submission`/`open_voting`) at a time.
- [ ] Admin can edit theme + description while a round is `pending`; both are rejected once it opens.
- [ ] Closing round N auto-opens round N+1; admin can also manually open a pending round; round 1 is opened manually.
- [ ] Closing the final round completes the league.
- [ ] Backend tests cover the above; technical-design §6 updated.

title: No UI to set "just vibing" participation mode
description:
Implements the **toggle UI + schema** half of the [MYS-112](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-112/define-andquotjust-vibingandquot-behavior-decision-unblock-vibing-ui) decision. Vibing is per-league with a per-round override (precedence: round override → per-league member setting → league default).

## Schema

* Add `leagues.default_vibe_mode` (bool, default false) — admin default set at league creation.
* Add `league_members.vibe_mode` (bool) — per-league member setting, seeded from `leagues.default_vibe_mode` at join, toggleable anytime.
* **Drop** `users.default_vibe_mode` (superseded) and remove its onboarding/profile plumbing.
* `submissions.participation_mode` already exists (per-round override).

## Admin story

> As a league admin, when I create a league I set the default participation mode (playing | just vibing) for all members.

* CreateLeague form gains a default-vibe control; `POST /leagues` accepts `default_vibe_mode`.

## Player story

> As a player, I can toggle my "just vibing" preference for a league at any time (seeded from the league default), and override it for a single round.

* Per-league toggle (changeable anytime) on the league screen and/or profile, backed by a new endpoint to set `league_members.vibe_mode`.
* Per-round "Just Vibes for this Round" toggle on the submit card; overrides the per-league setting for that round (re-submit while the round is open to change). `POST /rounds/:id/submissions` already accepts `participation_mode`; submit defaults from the member's per-league setting when not overridden.

## Acceptance

A player can choose vibing **per-league** and **per-round** through the UI; the Section E/G vibing branches of the E2E plan (`docs/qa/e2e-test-plan.md`) become testable.

Blocked by [MYS-112](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-112/define-andquotjust-vibingandquot-behavior-decision-unblock-vibing-ui) (decision). Pairs with the competition-rules ticket.

title: HSTS at the nginx edge (staging Droplet)
description:
Add an HSTS header at the nginx edge on the staging Droplet as defense-in-depth alongside the app-layer security headers middleware.

In the 443 server block of `scripts/nginx-mysterymixclub-staging.conf`:

```
add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains" always;
```

The `always` flag ensures the header is sent on error responses too. The http→443 redirect already exists; this completes "HTTPS enforced at the infrastructure level" (technical-design §9 item 1) by preventing protocol downgrade on the edge.

**Acceptance**

* HSTS `add_header` present on the 443 block with `always`
* Deploy/reload runbook step noted (nginx -t && reload) in `docs/staging-setup.md` if not already covered
* Prod (App Platform) HSTS is handled by the API middleware issue, not here

Housekeeping: there is currently an uncommitted change in this file setting `server_name staging.mysterymixclub.com` (leftover [MYS-40](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-40/staging-replace-self-signed-cert-with-lets-encrypt) work) — commit or revert it as part of this issue.

title: Results-available notification email on round close
description:
Split out of [MYS-24](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-24/round-reveal-and-results-ui) (deferred to its own issue). When a round transitions to `closed` (organizer closes voting, PATCH /rounds/:id state → closed), email all active league members that results are available, via the existing Resend email service (`app/services/email.py`).

Scope:

* Trigger on the round-close transition in the rounds update path.
* Recipients: active members of the round's league.
* Email-only per technical-design §12 (push notifications are out of scope for v1).
* A calm template with a deep link to the round results screen, in the app's voice.
* Decide delivery mechanism (inline vs background task) and failure handling so a send failure never blocks the close.

Relates to round state machine ([MYS-18](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-18/round-creation-state-machine-and-playlist-generation)) and the results endpoint ([MYS-23](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-23/round-results-endpoint)).

title: Input sanitization pass on user-supplied text fields
description:
Technical-design §9: "Input sanitization on all text fields (submission notes, display names)." Audit and harden every user-supplied free-text field.

Fields: display_name, league name/description, round theme, submission note, notes body. Confirm length limits, trimming, and that values are safely rendered on the frontend (no raw HTML injection). Add tests for boundary/abuse inputs.

title: Dependency audit before launch (pip audit + npm audit)
description:
Technical-design §9 pre-launch item: run a dependency vulnerability audit on both stacks and remediate before the production promotion.

* Backend: `pip-audit` (or `uv pip audit`) against the resolved env.
* Frontend: `npm audit` (prod deps), triage advisories.
* Document findings + fixes; pin/upgrade as needed.

Consider wiring a non-blocking audit step into CI so this doesn't silently regress.

title: Sprint 6: Hardening & Pre-Launch
description:
Parent issue for the final hardening, security, and cleanup pass before MVP launch — the catch-all that ensures review-surfaced debt and the technical-design pre-launch requirements don't ship unaddressed.

Two kinds of work live here:

1. **Review-surfaced debt** discovered during earlier sprints and previously orphaned in the backlog (re-parented here): [MYS-25](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-25/handle-soft-deleted-user-re-login-unique-email-collision), [MYS-32](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-32/harden-league-join-against-concurrent-first-join-race), [MYS-33](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-33/flaky-magic-link-expiry-test-created-at-and-expires-at-use-different), [MYS-36](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-36/re-home-the-log-out-of-all-devices-affordance), [MYS-40](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-40/staging-replace-self-signed-cert-with-lets-encrypt).
2. **Security Checklist / pre-launch tasks** from the technical design that were never ticketed (stubbed as children).

See `docs/technical/technical-design.md` §9 (Security Checklist), §10 (Privacy Architecture), §12 (Out of Scope). Items in §9 already satisfied by Sprint 1 auth work (magic-link single-use/expiry, token storage rules, refresh-cookie flags, magic-link rate limiting, Odesli key server-side) are intentionally not re-ticketed.

Do this pass before the develop → main production promotion.

title: Dev/staging: show magic-link on sign-in page for easy testing
description:
Staging has no email provider configured (and email to a raw IP / self-signed host isn't deliverable yet), so testers can't complete magic-link sign-in. As a stopgap for **dev and staging only (never prod)**, surface the sign-in link directly in the UI.

## Approach

* Backend `POST /api/v1/auth/request`: include the raw token in the response **only when** `environment != "production"` (`dev_token`), omitted entirely in prod.
* Frontend: after a successful request in non-prod, render a clickable **relative** link (`/auth/verify?token=...`) on the sign-in page below the submit button. Relative so it works over the proxy regardless of host/cert.
* Styling: understated (ink, underlined mono) — not Rust, since the sign-in screen's one Rust use is the ring dot.

## Out of scope

Real email delivery (Resend + domain) — separate from this; see [MYS-40](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-40/staging-replace-self-signed-cert-with-lets-encrypt) for the cert/domain.

title: Re-home the log out of all devices affordance
description:
Surfaced during [MYS-15](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-15/frontend-league-and-invite-screens). When /home was reworked from the old post-auth shell (HomeScreen) into the My Leagues list, the "log out of all devices" control was dropped, and the orphaned HomeScreen was deleted.

The capability still exists end to end: `logoutAll()` in frontend/src/services/api.ts (POST /api/v1/auth/logout-all) and `logoutAll` on the useAuth context. It is simply no longer reachable from any screen.

Technical-design section 5 lists "log out of all devices" / invalidate-all-sessions as part of the session model, so it should remain reachable in the UI.

Fix: surface logoutAll on a future account/settings screen (or a profile menu). No backend work needed; the endpoint and context method already exist. Just needs a UI home and wiring.

Non-blocking; [MYS-15](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-15/frontend-league-and-invite-screens) shipped without it intentionally (out of that ticket's leagues/invites scope).

title: Flaky magic-link expiry test: created_at and expires_at use different clock sources
description:
Surfaced during [MYS-14](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-14/league-management-extend-shorten-remove-member) review (unrelated to that ticket).

`tests/test_auth_request.py::test_expiry_is_created_at_plus_15_minutes_and_unused` intermittently fails locally, asserting `expires_at - created_at` is ~15 minutes (within 5s) but observing deltas as large as ~27 minutes. It passes on CI and often passes locally in isolation, so it is environment-dependent, not deterministic.

Root cause (suspected): the magic-link row mixes two clock sources. `created_at` is populated by Postgres `func.now()` (database server clock), while `expires_at` is computed in the application process as `now + 15 minutes` (app/process clock). When the two clocks drift apart, the measured delta skews. On CI the app and database share one clock so the test passes; locally a Dockerized Postgres VM can drift several minutes from the host after sleep/wake (macOS Docker Desktop), producing the ~27 minute delta. Restarting the DB container realigns it and the test goes green.

Proposed fix:

* Compute `created_at` and `expires_at` from a SINGLE clock source so the 15-minute relationship is invariant regardless of DB/app clock skew. Either set both from the app (`created_at = now`, `expires_at = now + 15m`) or both from the DB (`expires_at = func.now() + interval '15 minutes'`). Pick one and make `created_at` not rely on a server_default while `expires_at` is app-computed.
* Keep the test's intent (expiry is exactly 15 minutes after creation), but base it on one clock.

Reference: backend/app/api/routes/auth.py (magic-link request handler), backend/app/models/magic_link_token.py, backend/tests/test_auth_request.py:62.

title: Harden league join against concurrent first-join race
description:
Pre-existing data-integrity gap surfaced during [MYS-13](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-13/invite-link-generation-and-join-flow) review.

`league_members` has no unique constraint on `(league_id, user_id)`. The `POST /api/v1/invites/:token/accept` first-join path is a read-then-write (check `membership is None`, then insert) with no row lock, so two concurrent accept calls for a brand-new member could both pass the check and insert two active membership rows.

The 409 (already-active) and reactivation paths update an existing row and are not exposed to this; only the never-before-member first join is.

Origin: this stems from the [MYS-12](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-12/create-league-endpoint) schema (no unique index), not from [MYS-13](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-13/invite-link-generation-and-join-flow)'s code. Flagged non-blocking by the reviewer.

Proposed fix:

* Add a partial unique index on active memberships, e.g. `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... ON league_members (league_id, user_id) WHERE removed_at IS NULL`, via a new Alembic migration.
* Make the accept insert resilient (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` / catch IntegrityError and re-resolve to the duplicate path), so the race yields a clean 409 instead of a 500 or a duplicate row.
* Add a test simulating the concurrent/duplicate insert.

Reference: backend/app/api/routes/invites.py (accept handler), backend/app/models/league_member.py.

title: Fix lint-staged so the pre-commit hook can lint frontend files
description:
Pre-existing tooling bug surfaced while committing [MYS-27](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-27/frontend-onboarding-capture-display-name-on-first-login). The fix already rode along in PR #1, so this issue tracks it for visibility.

## Problem

`.husky/pre-commit` runs `npx lint-staged` from the repo root, but the root lint-staged config invoked bare `eslint` / `prettier` — binaries that only exist in `frontend/node_modules`, with an ESLint flat config (`frontend/eslint.config.js`) discoverable only from the `frontend/` cwd. As a result, committing **any** staged frontend `*.ts/tsx` file failed the hook with `ENOENT` (`Task failed to spawn: eslint --fix`). The hook could never successfully lint a frontend file from a clean root install.

## Fix (already in PR #1)

Replaced the package.json `lint-staged` block with a root `.lintstagedrc.mjs` that lints frontend files from inside `frontend/` against paths made relative to it, resolving the local bins via `npx --no-install`:

```js
"frontend/**/*.{ts,tsx}": (files) => {
  const rel = files.map((f) => path.relative("frontend", f)).join(" ");
  return [
    `cd frontend && npx --no-install eslint --fix ${rel}`,
    `cd frontend && npx --no-install prettier --write ${rel}`,
  ];
}
```

Backend `ruff` commands unchanged.

## Acceptance

* Committing a staged frontend `.ts/tsx` file runs eslint + prettier successfully via the hook (verified on the [MYS-27](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-27/frontend-onboarding-capture-display-name-on-first-login) commit).
* No regression for backend `*.py` (ruff) staged files.

Commit: `f6d6a62 fix: make lint-staged resolve the frontend toolchain` (PR #1).

title: Handle soft-deleted user re-login (UNIQUE email collision)
description:
Surfaced during [MYS-7](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-7/magic-link-verification-and-session-issuance) review (magic link verify / session issuance).

## Problem

`GET /api/v1/auth/verify` looks up the active user by `email` filtered to `deleted_at IS NULL`. If a user has been soft-deleted but not yet hard-purged (§10 allows up to 30 days), re-logging in with the same email:

1. passes magic-link token validation,
2. finds no *active* user,
3. attempts to INSERT a new `users` row,
4. hits the `users.email` UNIQUE constraint and raises an unhandled error (500).

By that point the magic-link token has already been hard-deleted (single-use), so the user is effectively locked out behind an opaque error until the purge runs. No data is corrupted (the transaction rolls back) and nothing sensitive leaks — it's a UX/correctness gap, not a security or integrity defect.

## Why deferred

This is intentionally out of [MYS-7](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-7/magic-link-verification-and-session-issuance) scope. Resolving it is a product/architecture decision tied to §10 (right to be forgotten): should a soft-deleted account be *reactivated* on re-login before purge, or should deletion be final until purge completes?

## Options to weigh

* Reactivate on re-login: clear `deleted_at` instead of inserting (needs an explicit reactivate path + a decision on whether that violates the deletion intent).
* Keep deletion final until purge: detect the collision and return a clear, non-leaking message instead of a 500.
* Partial unique index `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` to allow a fresh row alongside the tombstoned one (changes the §10 purge/uniqueness model).

## Acceptance

* Decide the §10 reactivation policy.
* Re-login by a soft-deleted, not-yet-purged email no longer 500s; behavior matches the chosen policy and is covered by a test.

title: Round reveal and results UI
description: Round reveal and results UI\\n\\n- Results screen: full submission list with submitter names revealed\\n- Score display per submission (Playing players)\\n- Leaderboard section (Playing players ranked by votes received)\\n- Most Noted section: winner prominently displayed with note count and all notes surfaced\\n- Just Vibing players' submissions displayed fully and equally -- no score shown, no absence noted awkwardly\\n- Notes visible per submission\\n- The reveal should feel like a moment -- consider progressive reveal animation (fast follow if too complex for v1)\\n- Notification sent to all players when results are available
