title: Sprint 5: Results and Round Reveal
description: Parent issue for round results, reveal UI, and scoring display.\\n\\nSee: `docs/prd/prd.md` Section 5.5 (Voting and Scoring)\\nThe reveal is a shared moment -- it should feel like an event, not just a data dump.

title: Google OAuth callback: add per-IP rate limiting
description: Reviewer LOW finding on ali8.2: /auth/google/callback has no rate limit, unlike every other unauthenticated auth endpoint in auth.py. Those are all per-email, DB-row-counted (login_attempts) — the callback has no email until after exchange_code, which is exactly the call being abused, so that pattern doesn't transfer directly. The in-memory IP limiter in waitlist.py doesn't transfer either — see MysteryMixClub-<waitlist-limiter-issue> for why. A correct fix needs a DB-backed per-IP table (login_attempts shape) plus a cleanup job, and storing IPs is a PII/retention decision that touches docs/security/data-residency.md — needs a real design pass, not a copy-paste. Partial mitigation already landed as a side effect of the ali8.2 nonce fix: one /google/login now yields exactly one callback attempt that can reach exchange_code, so unlimited replay of a single state is no longer possible.

title: Add PKCE to Google OAuth sign-in flow
description: Reviewer finding (LOW) on ali8.2: the Google OAuth code-exchange has no PKCE (code_challenge/code_verifier). The nonce cookie binds browser-to-state but not code-to-flow — an attacker who obtains a victim's authorization code via a separate leak (referrer, open redirect, log exposure) could replay it from their own browser. Not exploitable without a separate leak (confidential client, fixed HTTPS redirect URI), so defense-in-depth rather than a live hole. Google recommends PKCE for web server apps regardless.

title: Decision: how (or whether) to queue Apple Music playlist generation
description:
Split out from MysteryMixClub-y49x0v (MYS-258) Slice 1 during implementation, 2026-07-26 - see docs/adr/0006-postgres-backed-job-queue.md's 'Apple Music carve-out' section for full reasoning.

POST /mixes/{id}/apple-playlist was NOT wired into the new Postgres-backed playlist_jobs queue that Spotify generation now uses. Apple's Music User Token is an explicitly never-persisted, per-request credential (a deliberate privacy property, stated in backend/app/services/apple_playlist_generation.py's own docstring) - a job dequeued later by a separate worker process would need that token to still exist by then, which means persisting it somewhere, even transiently, directly contradicting why it is never persisted today.

Separately, playlist_jobs's UNIQUE(mix_id, provider) shape has no way to represent Apple's per-player generation anyway (Spotify is one playlist per mix; Apple is one per player) - the schema itself would need rework, not just a token-handling fix.

## Scope (needs its own design, not solved here)

Most likely direction per the ADR: don't queue Apple Music generation at all, and instead address its request-path cost some other way (e.g. tightening its own per-submission fan-out, since it is a per-player action rather than a fan-out-at-round-close event like Spotify). Confirm this is actually lower-risk than the shared-account Spotify path before assuming it does not need queueing.

title: Test coverage: no real-concurrency test for votes.py quorum/auto-close race
description: Flagged by reviewer during MYS-235 (MysteryMixClub-prdicl) test-isolation review, 2026-07-26. backend/app/api/routes/votes.py:145 uses with_for_update() on the same kind of quorum/auto-close path that participation-cap (MYS-80), invite-accept, and submission-cap races already have a real asyncio.gather + real_client concurrency test for (post-MYS-235's conftest.py real_session_factory/real_db_session/real_client fixtures). Pre-existing gap, not a regression introduced by MYS-235 - just the same class of untested race the other three now cover.
notes: See docs/adr/0005-test-isolation-transaction-rollback.md for the real_* fixture pattern to follow.

title: Align local docker-compose Postgres version with CI's service container
description:
Local docker-compose.yml runs Postgres 16-alpine (mmc-postgres, used for local dev + backend tests) while .github/workflows/ci.yml's backend job uses a postgres:15 service container. Noticed incidentally during the MYS-235 test-suite-speed investigation (MysteryMixClub-prdicl), not caused by or related to that fix.

A version mismatch between local/test and CI database engines is a latent source of hard-to-reproduce CI-only failures (behavior differences between major Postgres versions - e.g. planner changes, deprecated features, extension availability) that would otherwise look like flaky CI rather than an environment difference.

## Scope
- Confirm which version is actually intended as canonical (likely whatever prod/staging run, per ADR 0002's self-managed droplet setup).
- Align local docker-compose.yml and CI's postgres service container to the same major version.
- Check docs/technical/technical-design.md and staging/prod runbooks for any version pin that should also be reflected here.
notes: Flagged by the devops subagent during MYS-235 investigation, 2026-07-26. Out of scope for that ticket.

title: Test coverage: concurrent new-signup race for the last club slot
description: MysteryMixClub-y8r2ki (MYS-80) added an early (non-authoritative) capacity check in auth.py's verify_magic_link before account creation, with the authoritative check inside _join_via_invite under a row lock. The code comment at backend/app/api/routes/auth.py (~line 255) explicitly documents a narrow race window where two simultaneous new signups for the last slot could both pass the early check; one loses at the authoritative check and completes as a logged-in account without club membership (no welcome email, no error surfaced). No regression test exercises this exact window. Flagged by reviewer during MYS-80 review as a coverage gap, not a known defect — the fallback behavior (account created, join silently skipped) is intentional and documented.

title: Test coverage: rejoin-after-removal on a full club
description: MysteryMixClub-y8r2ki (MYS-80) added a 20-member cap check inside _join_via_invite's reactivation branch (backend/app/api/routes/invites.py), but no test exercises a previously-removed member trying to rejoin a club that's now at cap. Flagged by reviewer during MYS-80 review as a coverage gap, not a known defect.

title: Make it clear mystery mixes run one at a time, not in parallel
description:
**Improvement** (from user testing)

Testers weren't clear that a club runs exactly one mystery mix at a time (sequential: `open_submission → open_voting → closed`, up to `total_mixes` — see `mix {current_mix} of {total_mixes}` in `frontend/src/pages/ClubHomeScreen.tsx:173`). They expected multiple mixes could run in parallel.

**Scope:** copy-only. Add explicit copy making the sequential model clear — candidates: where an organizer sets `total_mixes` on `CreateClubScreen.tsx`, and/or on the club home screen near the mix progress indicator.

Parallel mixing itself is a separate, much bigger idea — tracked as its own backlog ticket, not in scope here.

title: Upgrade to ruff 0.16.x and fix its new lint violations
description:
## Problem

`backend/pyproject.toml` pinned `ruff>=0.6.0` with no upper bound. CI has no
lockfile, so a fresh `pip install` on the develop→main promotion PR (#182)
picked up the just-released `ruff==0.16.0`, which flags **518** violations
across files nobody touched in that PR — `datetime.UTC` alias (UP017),
import-sort changes (I001), and others. This isn't a real regression, it's a
new-version default-behavior change hitting an unpinned dependency.

Temporarily fixed by pinning `ruff>=0.6.0,<0.16.0` in `backend/pyproject.toml`
(see the commit pinning this) so CI stays green on the version that's
actually been validated (0.15.14).

## Goal

Deliberately upgrade to ruff 0.16.x (or whatever's current then) on its own
PR: bump the pin, run `ruff check --fix` + `ruff format`, hand-fix whatever
isn't auto-fixable, confirm the full suite stays green, then remove the
upper-bound pin (or move it forward).

## Done when

`ruff>=0.6.0` (or a fresh floor) with no upper-bound pin, full backend tree
clean under the new version, CI green.

title: WCAG audit follow-up: automated a11y checks in CI + manual zoom/text-spacing verification
description:
## Context

[MYS-121](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-121/wcag-accessibility-conformance) (WCAG 2.2 AA audit + remediation) auto-closed when its PR (#178) merged, since Linear's GitHub integration ties issue state to the linked PR title. That PR fixed all 24 actionable findings from the audit, but two pieces of [MYS-121](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-121/wcag-accessibility-conformance)'s original scope were explicitly left undone rather than silently dropped:

## Scope

* **Automated accessibility checks wired into CI.** [MYS-121](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-121/wcag-accessibility-conformance)'s own "Done when" criteria asked for this ("with automated checks wired into CI where practical") and it was never done — no `jest-axe`/`@axe-core` (or similar) exists anywhere in the frontend test suite today. Add automated a11y assertions to at least the frontend `vitest` suite so contrast/ARIA/semantic regressions get caught before merge, not just in a manual audit.
* **200% browser zoom reflow check.** Flagged in the original audit as needing live browser testing (Chrome/Firefox at 200% zoom) rather than a guessed pass/fail from static code — never actually performed.
* **Live text-spacing override check.** Same — WCAG 1.4.12 requires no loss of content when a user overrides line-height/paragraph/letter/word spacing via a bookmarklet or extension; flagged as needing manual verification, never actually performed.

## Not in scope

Everything else from the original audit (color contrast, forms/aria-describedby, semantic structure, keyboard nav, motion, touch targets, readability) already shipped in [MYS-121](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-121/wcag-accessibility-conformance)/PR #178 — don't re-litigate those.

## Done when

CI fails on a real a11y regression (verified with a deliberately-broken test), and both manual checks have been performed against a real authenticated screen (not just the public landing page), with any findings from either becoming their own follow-up tickets.

title: Adopt Doppler as secrets manager for staging/prod (replace manual env-file SSH edits)
description:
## Why

2026-07-23 production outage: no playlists generated for any service (Spotify/YouTube/Apple). Root cause: the prod Droplet cutover ([MYS-213](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-213/devops-and-maintenance-schedule-playbook)/[MYS-225](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-225/prod-move-off-do-app-platform-onto-self-managed-droplet-terraform-cicd)) shipped with `/etc/mysterymixclub/prod.env` missing all playlist-integration credentials (`YOUTUBE_API_KEY`, `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID/SECRET/REDIRECT_URI/PLAYLIST_ACCOUNT_USER_ID`, `APPLE_MUSIC_TEAM_ID/KEY_ID/PRIVATE_KEY`). All three integrations degrade silently by design (no crash, feature just hidden), so the gap went unnoticed until a user reported it. `docs/prod-setup.md`'s env setup step only calls out the strictly-required keys and never told whoever bootstrapped the box to carry the playlist credentials over from the prior setup — a manual copy-paste step with no diff/audit to catch a miss.

Dawn's ruling (2026-07-23): **never SSH into the prod droplet again** — not for deploys (already handled via the self-hosted GitHub Actions runner on the droplet, `b2c9bc4`), and not for config/secret edits either. Config/secrets should live in a secrets manager both Dawn and Claude can manage without a droplet login.

## Decision

Doppler, chosen over 1Password Connect / Infisical for this scale (small team, free tier covers it, syncs into a systemd service without needing SSH, gives a real diff between staging's and prod's secret sets — which would have caught this exact gap immediately).

## Scope (draft — confirm before implementing)

* Doppler project with `staging` and `prod` configs mirroring the two existing `.env` files (`scripts/staging.env.example`, `scripts/prod.env.example`).
* Wire secret delivery into the existing deploy path (self-hosted runner on each droplet) rather than a manual file edit — e.g. `doppler run` wrapping the systemd `ExecStart`, or Doppler's secrets-sync writing the env file as part of `deploy-staging.sh`/`deploy-prod.sh`.
* Migrate existing staging secrets into Doppler first (staging already works, use it as the known-good source), then populate prod (six of the eight missing playlist keys are safe to copy verbatim; `SPOTIFY_REDIRECT_URI` needs prod's own domain and `SPOTIFY_PLAYLIST_ACCOUNT_USER_ID` needs prod's own OAuth-linked row, not staging's — see engineering notes).
* Update `docs/ci-cd.md` / `docs/prod-setup.md` / `docs/staging-setup.md` "adding a new secret" flow to describe the Doppler-based process, replacing the current `/etc/mysterymixclub/*.env` SSH-edit instructions.
* Needs an ADR per `docs/adr/README.md` (vendor/hosting choice) before implementation.

## Immediate unblock (separate, don't wait on this ticket)

The current playlist outage is being unblocked via a targeted fix through the existing deploy pipeline (GitHub Actions secrets → self-hosted runner writes the env file), not by SSHing in — this ticket tracks the durable secrets-manager migration, not the immediate fix.
notes: Deprioritized 2026-07-26 per Dawn — not urgent right now, vendor choice (Doppler) not re-litigated, just lower priority until revisited.

title: No bootstrap path for the first user/admin on a fresh database
description:
Discovered 2026-07-22 while bootstrapping the prod droplet for the first time ([MYS-225](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-225/prod-move-off-do-app-platform-onto-self-managed-droplet-terraform-cicd)). Prod's database was created fresh (new droplet, migrations run for the first time), and signing in as `dgabriel@gmail.com` silently no-op'd — `POST /auth/request` returns a neutral `200 OK` with no email sent whenever the requesting email isn't an *existing* user and has no valid invite (`backend/app/api/routes/auth.py`, anti-enumeration by design, [MYS-127](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-127/invite-gated-sign-up-global-user-cap-1500)).

The gap: there's no code path to create the very first user on a brand-new database. `POST /admin/invites` (the way to mint a club-less signup invite) itself requires an existing platform admin (`get_platform_admin`), which requires an existing `users` row matching an email in `SEED_ADMIN_EMAILS` — a genuine chicken-and-egg problem with zero users.

**Workaround used this time:** seeded the first `users` row directly via `psql` (`INSERT INTO users (id, email, display_name, email_notifications, created_at) VALUES (...)`), since `SEED_ADMIN_EMAILS` was already set to `dgabriel@gmail.com` — any user row with that email is automatically treated as platform admin (computed at request time, not a DB flag).

**Not urgent** — this only matters when standing up a brand-new environment from scratch (a fresh prod, a disaster-recovery restore, a new deployment target), which is expected to be rare. If it ever recurs, the same manual SQL insert works fine; this ticket is just to consider a real fix (e.g. a one-time bootstrap CLI command, or a documented runbook step in `docs/prod-setup.md`) if it comes up more than once.

title: Bandcamp resolve: support labels with a custom domain (Bandcamp Pro redirect)
description:
Reported by Dawn 2026-07-20: pasting `https://wereleasewhateverthefuckwewantrecords.bandcamp.com/track/1224-live` into the paste-a-link resolve flow fails with the generic "couldn't find that song" error.

## Root cause

The label uses Bandcamp Pro's custom-domain feature: `wereleasewhateverthefuckwewantrecords.bandcamp.com` returns an HTTP 301 to `https://wrwtfww.com/track/1224-live`, where the actual track page (with a perfectly parseable `og:title`) lives.

[MYS-200](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-200/bandcamp-platform-link-out-paste-a-link-resolution)'s SSRF hardening in `_bandcamp_redirect_target` (`backend/app/services/link_resolver.py`) only follows redirects that stay within the `*.bandcamp.com` host family — any off-family target is treated as unsupported, the same as a hostile redirect aimed at an internal address would be. That guard is working as designed; it just wasn't scoped for legitimate Bandcamp Pro custom domains, which are indistinguishable from an SSRF attempt using a hostname-only check.

## Interim fix (shipped 2026-07-20)

`SongNotFoundError` now carries an optional `code` (`"bandcamp_custom_domain"`), and the resolve endpoint surfaces a specific, accurate message for this case instead of the generic one: "this bandcamp link redirects to a custom domain, which isn't supported yet. try a link that stays on [bandcamp.com](<http://bandcamp.com>)." No security surface changed — the redirect is still refused.

## Real fix (this ticket)

Replace the host-family allowlist in `_bandcamp_redirect_target` with a resolved-IP validation: follow the redirect, but resolve the target host's IP first and reject private/loopback/link-local/reserved ranges (plus non-http(s) schemes, non-standard ports) rather than rejecting based on hostname family alone. This is the standard mitigation for "must safely fetch a user-supplied redirect target" and would let legitimate custom-domain labels resolve while keeping real SSRF protection.

No existing test covers a *legitimate* off-family redirect (only hostile/spoofed ones) — add one alongside the fix, e.g. against a stubbed resolver.

title: Bandcamp mix player page — embedded-player "playlist" (future release)
description:
Later-release enhancement (Dawn, 2026-07-19): auto-generate something playlist-like for Bandcamp.

## Honest feasibility

A true auto-generated Bandcamp playlist (like Spotify/Apple/YouTube) is **impossible** — Bandcamp has no public API and no third-party playlist concept. What IS feasible and officially supported: Bandcamp's **embedded player** (per-track iframe embeds). So the realistic feature is an in-app "mix player" page: the mystery mix's Bandcamp-sourced tracks rendered as a sequence of official embedded players, in playlist order, styled to the design system.

## Implementation notes (from 2026-07-19 scoping)

* Embeds need Bandcamp's **numeric track id**, not the URL slug. That id is present in the track page HTML we already fetch at resolve time (`data-tralbum` / the `og:video` EmbeddedPlayer URL) — capture and persist it during [MYS-201](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-201/isrc-less-submissions-bandcampyoutube-only-tracks-playlist-gap) source-only resolution to avoid a re-fetch later. Cheap to add then; annoying to backfill after.
* No cross-iframe auto-advance (each embed is isolated) — players click per track. Set expectations in the UI.
* Each embed streams from Bandcamp with full artist attribution + buy links — very on-brand for supporting small artists.
* Design: embeds are third-party UI; frame them within our card/tracklist chrome, mind the style guide.

Not scheduled; revisit after launch.

title: In-app search results from YouTube (future enhancement)
description:
Future enhancement — explicitly NOT a release blocker (Dawn, 2026-07-19).

Today the in-app search box queries only the Deezer catalog; YouTube/Bandcamp-only tracks are reachable solely via paste-a-link ([MYS-200](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-200/bandcamp-platform-link-out-paste-a-link-resolution)/[MYS-201](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-201/isrc-less-submissions-bandcampyoutube-only-tracks-playlist-gap)). This ticket: surface YouTube results in the in-app search alongside catalog results.

Notes from scoping:

* YouTube Data API is already integrated (keyed) for exact-link resolution and playlist generation — search is the same API, so no new credentials. Mind quota: search.list costs 100 units/call vs ~1 for lookups; needs debounce/caching thought.
* Results without a catalog match should flow into the [MYS-201](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-201/isrc-less-submissions-bandcampyoutube-only-tracks-playlist-gap) source-only submit path (`youtube:<video_id>`), including the no-fuzzy-guess rule.
* **Bandcamp cannot be added here** — no public search API exists; paste-a-link remains its ceiling. Don't scope it in.
* UX question for whenever this is picked up: mixed result lists (catalog + YouTube) need clear source labeling so players know what they're submitting.

title: Confirm and document hosting data residency (DO region) for EU data-transfer compliance
description:
GDPR restricts transferring EU personal data outside the EEA without a valid safeguard (SCCs, adequacy decision, etc.). We haven't documented which DigitalOcean region hosts the staging droplet (`67.207.81.183` per staging-droplet memory) or the prod App Platform app/managed Postgres, or whether any EU beta users' data is in scope.

**Scope**

* Confirm the DO region(s) currently in use for staging and prod.
* If any current or planned users are in the EEA/UK, confirm DO's standard contractual clauses cover the transfer (DO publishes these) and note this in the Privacy Policy subprocessors section.
* Document the finding in `docs/staging-setup.md` or `docs/ci-cd.md` so it isn't re-litigated later.

Filed from a 2026-07-16 compliance gap review; not previously scoped in Linear.

title: Document a data-breach notification process (GDPR 72-hour rule)
description:
No documented process exists for what happens if user data is exposed (staging droplet compromise, leaked credentials, etc.). GDPR Art. 33 requires notifying the relevant supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach affecting EU users' data, and Art. 34 may require notifying affected users directly.

**Scope**

* Write a short runbook (alongside `docs/staging-setup.md` / `docs/security/`) covering: who gets notified internally, how affected users are identified, notification templates/timeline, and the 72-hour authority-notification trigger.
* This is a docs/process ticket, not a code change.

Filed from a 2026-07-16 compliance gap review; not previously scoped in Linear.

title: Apple Music: no match in catalog presents a wrong track as if it were exact
description:
Spun out of [MYS-175](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-175/search-relevance-wrongirrelevant-matches-and-wrong-versions-in-song) during manual testing.

## Problem

When a track genuinely isn't in Apple Music's catalog under any close title, the iTunes Search API still returns its single closest same-artist guess — and the app currently presents that as if it were a confident exact match, with no visual distinction from a real match.

## Repro

Search "Storm II" by GENER8ION:

* Confirmed the track is not in Apple's catalog under any query variant (checked GENER8ION's full indexed catalog directly — not present).
* iTunes Search still returns one result: "ARAE II" by GENER8ION (same artist, unrelated song), which the app links to as the Apple Music result.
* Relevance-scored, this candidate is a poor match (title score ~0.35 out of the pool), but since it's the *only* candidate returned, [MYS-175](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-175/search-relevance-wrongirrelevant-matches-and-wrong-versions-in-song)'s best-match picker takes it by default — there's nothing better to rank it against.

## First steps

1. Add a minimum-confidence floor to the Apple (and Deezer fallback-search) best-match pick in `app/services/song_links.py` — below the floor, treat it as no match and fall back to the deep link instead of presenting a low-confidence guess as exact.
2. Pick the floor empirically against a few known-missing-track repros (this one, plus any others collected) so it doesn't reject genuinely good matches that just have minor title differences.
3. Consider surfacing this distinction in the UI (e.g. "we couldn't find an exact match" vs. a real result) rather than silently swapping to a deep link.

## Boundaries

Distinct from [MYS-175](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-175/search-relevance-wrongirrelevant-matches-and-wrong-versions-in-song) (ranking among multiple candidates) — this is about what to do when the *only* candidate is a bad one. Same shape as [MYS-166](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-166/allow-submission-without-isrc-for-songs-not-in-deezer-catalog)'s Deezer-coverage problem, but for Apple.

title: Help overlays: animation pass on the step vignettes (phase 3)
description:
Post-beta follow-up to [MYS-120](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-120/3-step-help-overlays-per-page-info-icon-replay) (split out 2026-07-12: beta ships static vignettes).

Add the quiet CSS loop animations to the 12 help-overlay vignette SVGs, per the approved design mockup (attached to [MYS-120](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-120/3-step-help-overlays-per-page-info-icon-replay)): opacity/transform/stroke-dashoffset only, ~2.4s ease-in-out cycles, nothing faster than the system's 150–200ms vocabulary at transition edges. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` keeps the static final frame (already the beta behavior, so this ticket is purely additive).

Vignette-by-vignette animation specs are in the design mockup linked on [MYS-120](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-120/3-step-help-overlays-per-page-info-icon-replay) — the mockup's "animated (phase 3)" toggle demonstrates every loop.

title: Voting screen: checkmark icon on songs you've voted for
description:
## What

On the round voting screen, show a small checkmark icon on each song/submission the current player has already cast a vote for, so it's visually clear at a glance which selections are "locked in" without needing to re-check vote state per song.

## Notes

* Sage accent for the checkmark (not Rust — Rust is reserved as the one-per-screen signal color).
* Should read from the player's existing vote state for the round (already fetched via `getMyVotes`).
* Pure frontend/UI change — no new backend endpoint expected.

## Origin

Pulled in as a UI tweak alongside the deadline-epic wrap-up and organizer-safety tickets for the next sprint.

title: Allow submission without ISRC for songs not in Deezer catalog
description:
Currently all song submissions require an ISRC, and the only keyless source of ISRCs is Deezer. This means any song not in Deezer's catalog (e.g. obscure punk tracks, regional releases, very old recordings) cannot be submitted via link paste — the resolve endpoint returns 404 even when the YouTube/Spotify/Apple Music link is valid.

Discovered during [MYS-164](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-164/link-tab-service-selector-auto-detect-for-spotify-youtube-apple-music) testing: `https://youtu.be/9LdTe2EbrLk` ("Hombre Secreto" by Plugz, 1979) resolves fine through YouTube oEmbed but fails the Deezer search funnel.

## Root cause

`link_resolver.py` documents the constraint explicitly:

> The linchpin: a submission REQUIRES an ISRC, and only Deezer returns one keyless. So every path funnels through Deezer.

## Proposed fix

Make ISRC optional on submissions.

### Backend changes

* Remove the implicit ISRC requirement from the submission flow — a song without an ISRC can still be submitted with title + artist + thumbnail.
* Cross-platform link assembly in `song_links.py` already degrades gracefully when no ISRC is present (it skips ISRC-based lookups); verify this path is clean.
* When the Deezer search funnel returns no results, fall back to the identity already obtained from the platform (oEmbed title/artist) rather than raising `SongNotFoundError`.
* The `SongIdentity` model already allows `isrc: str | None = None` — the blocker is the resolver raising before returning it.

### Schema / data considerations

* Check whether the `submissions` table has a NOT NULL constraint on `isrc`; if so, make it nullable in a migration (additive, safe for live staging).
* Deduplication logic (duplicate-ISRC rejection, [MYS-147](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-147/block-duplicate-isrc-within-a-round-warn-on-league-repeat)) must degrade gracefully when `isrc` is None — don't block a no-ISRC submission against another no-ISRC submission unless title+artist match closely.

### Trade-offs

* Songs without an ISRC will have fewer platform links in the "listen on" row (only the source platform link is known).
* Leaderboard / voting mechanics are unaffected — they key on submission ID, not ISRC.

title: Spike: cross-platform native app wrapper (Capacitor/Expo) — no Swift/Kotlin rewrite
description:
**Spike / research — do not implement.** Future consideration once app is past MVP/enhancement phase.

## Why now

MMC is a React/TypeScript PWA. Goal is App Store + Play Store presence without rewriting the UI in native Swift/Kotlin.

## Options to evaluate

1. **Capacitor** — wraps existing PWA in a native shell, gives native API access (push, share sheet) where needed, single codebase stays source of truth. Likely best fit given current Tailwind/React design system.
2. **PWA-only, push installability** — check if iOS/Android home-screen install covers actual needs (push, camera, etc.) without app store presence at all.
3. **React Native / Expo** — shares business logic and API layer but requires rebuilding UI layer in RN primitives or NativeWind (bigger lift given current design system: Tailwind tokens, underline inputs, concentric ring motif).

## Questions to resolve

* Do we actually need native APIs beyond what a well-built PWA offers, or is this purely about app store distribution / "feels native" polish?
* If Capacitor: what's the native build/signing/release pipeline look like (Xcode/Play Console requirements)?
* Any design system casualties from going Capacitor vs RN?

## Output

Recommendation + rough effort estimate, to inform whether/when this gets scheduled.

title: UI: show music note icon on Spotify connect + playlist generate CTAs before playlist exists
description:
Currently the music note icon only appears after a playlist has been generated. It should also appear on the "Connect to Spotify" and "Generate a playlist link" action buttons/links so the affordance is consistent regardless of playlist state.

Acceptance:

* Music note icon is visible next to "Connect to Spotify" CTA
* Music note icon is visible next to "Generate a playlist link" CTA
* Icon remains after playlist is generated (no regression)

title: Queue UI: auto-advance behavior
description:
## Overview

Layer auto-advance behavior on top of the queue UI ([MYS-153](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-153/queue-ui-persistent-player-panel-with-manual-advance)), so tracks progress without requiring manual interaction where technically possible.

## Behavior by service

**Spotify**

* Integrate Spotify iframe embed SDK
* Listen for `playback_update` events to detect track end
* Auto-mount next track in queue on end event

**Bandcamp / Apple Music**

* No playback events available from these iframes
* Fall back to timer-based advance
* Show visible countdown timer (user-configurable, default 3 min)
* Controls: Skip (advance immediately), Extend (add time), Pause countdown

## UX

* Auto-advance mode is opt-in — toggle in the player panel
* Clear visual indication of which advance mode is active (event-based vs timer)
* When timer is active, countdown is prominent and easy to dismiss

## Dependencies

* Blocked by [MYS-153](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-153/queue-ui-persistent-player-panel-with-manual-advance) (Queue UI: persistent player panel with manual advance)

## Notes

* Spotify is the primary submission source so event-based advance covers most of the queue in practice
* Timer default of 3 min should be revisited based on actual average track lengths in MMC rounds

title: Queue UI: persistent player panel with manual advance
description:
## Overview

Build a persistent player panel that gives users a continuous listening experience across a round's submissions, without requiring them to manually locate and play each embed independently.

## UX

* Persistent bottom or side panel appears when a user starts playing a round
* Current track is displayed with service badge (Spotify, Apple Music, Bandcamp), title, and artist
* Queue of upcoming tracks visible and scrollable
* Manual Next/Previous controls — one tap to advance
* Each track card in the queue includes its external link (e.g. "Open in Spotify", "Open in Bandcamp")
* Panel persists as user navigates within the round

## Data model

```
Queue {
  id
  leagueId
  roundId
  tracks: [
    { submissionId, service, url, title, artist, order }
  ]
  currentIndex
}
```

## Notes

* No auto-advance logic in this ticket — that is handled in a follow-up (see: Queue UI: auto-advance behavior)
* Queue order should default to submission order, with vote-rank order as a stretch option
* This ticket is the foundation for all future playback UX improvements

title: Add Bandcamp embedded player support
description:
## Overview

Allow members to submit Bandcamp track/album URLs and have them render as embedded players within the app, alongside existing Spotify/Apple Music support.

## Implementation

**Backend**

* Add server-side oEmbed fetch: `GET https://bandcamp.com/oembed?url=<track_url>&format=json`
* Must be server-side — Bandcamp's oEmbed endpoint does not allow browser-side cross-origin calls
* Handle custom Bandcamp domains (artists may use their own domain, not just `*.bandcamp.com`)

**Frontend**

* Add Bandcamp URL detector utility (check for `bandcamp.com` and known custom domains)
* Create `BandcampPlayer` component that renders the returned iframe within the existing track card shell
* Constrain iframe dimensions via CSS to fit card layout
* Add "Open in Bandcamp" link on the track card that opens the original submission URL in a new tab

## Notes

* Bandcamp previews are often 30-second clips unless the artist enables full streaming — consider surfacing this caveat to members at submission time
* Detection of custom Bandcamp domains may require a fallback (e.g. attempt oEmbed fetch and handle gracefully if it fails)

title: "Set" submission: two related songs, back-to-back on the playlist
description:
From the ideas list (`docs/idea-scratch.md`): *"Set submission; players submit two songs at a time that are related and will be back-to-back on the playlist."*

## What

A submission mode where a player submits **two related songs as a set**, and the round playlist keeps them **adjacent / in order**.

## Dependency

**Blocked by** [MYS-116](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-116/allow-more-than-one-song-per-submission) (more than one song per submission) — a "set" is a constrained (n=2, ordered, adjacency-preserving) case of multi-song. Resolve the multi-song data model / voting / scoring questions there first, then layer the set semantics:

* Adjacency + order preservation in playlist generation (Spotify/YouTube/Apple all append; ordering must be enforced — note Apple/Deezer append-only).
* Voting/scoring on a set (one vote for the pair? per song?).

## Done when

Players can submit an ordered 2-song set that stays back-to-back in the round playlist, with voting/scoring rules defined and tested.

title: WCAG accessibility conformance
description:
From the ideas list (`docs/idea-scratch.md`): *"Make 100% accessible to meet all WCAG benchmarks."* (Idea said "OWALA" — confirmed that meant **WCAG**.) Stand-alone accessibility effort (decoupled 2026-07-23 — the UX overhaul epic it was originally scoped under, [MYS-114](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-114/ux-overhaul-epic), was canceled).

## Target (decided 2026-06-22): WCAG 2.x **AA**

## Scope

* Semantic structure, landmarks, headings, focus order, visible focus states.
* Keyboard operability for all interactive elements (submit/vote/notes/playlist).
* **Color contrast** — audit the palette (Cream/Ink/Sage/Rust/Muted) against **AA**; the quiet/low-contrast aesthetic needs checking, especially Muted text and Sage-on-Cream.
* Alt text / labels (album art, icons, the concentric-ring motif), form labels (underline inputs), ARIA where needed.
* Motion-reduction support (`prefers-reduced-motion`) for the rotating-ring loader and overlay animations.
* Screen-reader pass on the core flows.

## Done when

Core flows pass an accessibility audit at **WCAG AA**, with automated checks wired into CI where practical.

title: Social integrations (Discord / Snapchat / Instagram / WhatsApp)
description:
From the ideas list (`docs/idea-scratch.md`): *"Integration with discord, snapchat, instagram, whatsapp."* **Too broad to scope as-is — needs definition first.**

## Open question: what does "integration" mean here?

Could be any of several very different efforts, each per-platform:

* **Share-out** — post a round/playlist/results to a channel or story (lightest; mostly share links/cards).
* **Notify-via** — deliver lifecycle notifications into Discord/WhatsApp instead of email (overlaps [MYS-109](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-109/email-notifications-for-round-lifecycle-events); Discord webhooks are easy, WhatsApp needs Business API).
* **Auth/login** — sign in with a social account (heavy; changes auth model — magic-link only today, technical-design §5).
* **Invites** — share invite links into these apps (arguably already possible via any share sheet).

## Needed first

A product decision narrowing this to a concrete capability + the priority platform(s). Each platform is its own integration with its own API/approval. No build until scoped. Likely best sequenced after the core email/notification work.

## Done when

Scope narrowed to specific capability + platform(s), then split into per-platform tickets.

title: Inbound song submissions via SMS and email
description:
From the ideas list (`docs/idea-scratch.md`): *"sms and email submissions."* **Hardest of the messaging ideas — defer behind notifications.**

## What

Let a player submit a song for the active round by **replying to/sending an SMS or email** (e.g. paste a streaming link), instead of opening the app.

## Why hard

* **Inbound channel infra** — inbound email parsing (Resend inbound or similar) and/or inbound SMS (Twilio); webhooks.
* **Sender → user/round matching** — map a phone/email to a user and to *their* active round; reject ambiguous/closed cases.
* **Link resolution** — run the pasted link through the existing resolve path (`song_links.py`) to get ISRC/metadata.
* **Spam/abuse + auth** — inbound channels are unauthenticated; need to verify the sender owns the account.

## Done when

A verified member can submit to their active round via SMS/email, resolved into a normal submission, with abuse handling. Build after [MYS-109](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-109/email-notifications-for-round-lifecycle-events) (email) and the SMS notification groundwork.

title: Musicology round type (one song, a dozen notes)
description:
From the ideas list (`docs/idea-scratch.md`): *"Musicology round: one song, a dozen notes."* **New round format — needs its own mini-PRD.**

## What (as understood — confirm)

A distinct round *type* where the focus is one song annotated with many notes, rather than the standard submit→vote→reveal competition. Exact mechanics TBD: who picks the song, what "a dozen notes" means (annotations/commentary from members?), how/if it's scored.

## Needed first

A short spec defining the format and how it coexists with the existing round state machine (`rounds.py`, technical-design §6) — is it a `rounds.type`, a separate flow, etc. No build until defined.

## Done when

Format specced, then implemented as a selectable round type with tests.

title: SMS notifications for round lifecycle events
description:
From the ideas list (`docs/idea-scratch.md`). The SMS half of "sms and email notifications" — **split from email (**[MYS-109](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-109/email-notifications-for-round-lifecycle-events)**)** because it's materially heavier.

## Why heavier than email

* **New vendor** (e.g. Twilio) + per-message cost (email via Resend is effectively free at our scale).
* **Phone number capture + verification** (no phone field today).
* **Opt-in compliance** (TCPA/STOP handling) — can't just send.

## Build (later)

Mirror [MYS-109](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-109/email-notifications-for-round-lifecycle-events)'s event hooks but deliver via SMS, gated by an explicit opt-in and phone verification, with STOP/unsubscribe handling. Do **after** email notifications prove the event-hook layer.

## Done when

Opted-in members with a verified phone receive SMS on lifecycle events, with compliant opt-out.

title: Spotify playlist: auto-open the new playlist after creating it
description:
**Manual test finding (P4) — future enhancement.** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

After generating a Spotify playlist, **auto-open / redirect to the new playlist** rather than only surfacing the "open playlist in Spotify" link. We already return `playlist_url` from `POST /rounds/:id/spotify-playlist` ([MYS-83](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-83/playlist-spotify-per-user-oauth-create-saved-playlist-for-a-round)), so this is a small frontend touch (e.g. `window.open(playlist_url)` on success) — mind popup-blockers; the link stays as the fallback.

title: Round: drop "it's up next in the queue." from the pre-open message
description:
**Manual test finding (P3).** `docs/qa/manual-test-findings.md`.

A pending (not-yet-open) round shows "this round hasn't opened yet — it's up next in the queue." (`frontend/src/pages/RoundDetailRoute.tsx`). Drop the "— it's up next in the queue." tail; keep just **"this round hasn't opened yet."**

title: Playlist: Deezer API access go/no-go (can we still register an app + complete OAuth?)
description:
**Phase 3 gate of the streaming-playlist rollout** (spike: [MYS-76](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-76/spike-auto-generate-streaming-playlists-youtube-deezer-spotify-as), `docs/discovery/spike-playlist-generation.md` §3.3, §5). **Do not build the Deezer playlist generator until this go/no-go passes.**

## Why this is a gate, not a build

Deezer is the **biggest risk of the three services**. Playlist creation needs OAuth (`manage_library` scope), and per the spike: "obtaining new app credentials / OAuth approval has been unreliable for years and **may not be available at all**." Building matching/OAuth/UI before confirming write access is obtainable risks wasted work.

## Investigate / confirm

1. Can we still **register a new Deezer developer app** and obtain client credentials today?
2. Can we complete the **OAuth flow end-to-end** and obtain a token with `manage_library`?
3. Can we successfully `POST /user/me/playlists` + `POST /playlist/{id}/tracks` against a real account?

## If GO

Mirror the Spotify flow ([MYS-83](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-83/playlist-spotify-per-user-oauth-create-saved-playlist-for-a-round)). Matching is the easy part: **keyless** `GET /track/isrc:{ISRC}` **is already in our codebase** (`app/services/song_links.py` `_deezer_exact`) and the Deezer exact track URL is already stored in `submissions.platform_links`. File the build ticket then.

## If NO-GO

Document the dead end and drop Deezer playlist creation from scope (keyless per-track Deezer links already exist for playback). Revisit only if Deezer reopens access.

## Reference

`docs/discovery/spike-playlist-generation.md` §3.3, §5 (phased recommendation), §7 (risk summary).

title: Voting: don't allow leaving a note on your own submission
description:
Follow-up to the own-submission voting work ([MYS-73](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-73/voting-prevent-selecting-your-own-song-in-the-ui)/74/75). On the voting screen, the card for the player's own submission currently still renders the `SongNotes` affordance (the "notes" view toggle and the "leave a note" composer). You shouldn't be able to leave a note on your own song.

**Change:** remove the notes / "leave a note" toggle from the own-submission (`is_own`) card in the voting playlist. UI-only — other players' cards and vibing cards keep their notes affordance unchanged.

Relates to [MYS-73](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-73/voting-prevent-selecting-your-own-song-in-the-ui), [MYS-74](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-74/voting-make-your-own-submission-visually-obvious), [MYS-75](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-75/voting-label-your-own-submission-your-submission).

title: Voting: label your own submission "Your Submission"
description: Follow-up to [MYS-74](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-74/voting-make-your-own-submission-visually-obvious): on the voting screen, the card for the player's own submission should carry the label **"Your Submission"** (was "your pick"). It remains non-selectable ([MYS-73](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-73/voting-prevent-selecting-your-own-song-in-the-ui)). UI-only change on the voting screen.

title: Allow appending a round to a league that already has a pre-created slate
description:
## Context

Follow-up to [MYS-62](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-62/pre-created-rounds-bulk-creation-pending-state-and-admin-descriptions) (pre-created rounds). After that change, a league's rounds are created as a full slate up front via `POST /leagues/:id/rounds:batch`, and the original single-create endpoint `POST /leagues/:id/rounds` now 409s once any round exists (its guard treats `pending` rounds as blocking). So the two creation paths are mutually exclusive in practice: once you pre-create the slate, you cannot append another round mid-league.

This is consistent with the pre-creation model and was an accepted trade-off in [MYS-62](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-62/pre-created-rounds-bulk-creation-pending-state-and-admin-descriptions). This issue tracks the enhancement if/when "add one more round" becomes desired.

## Scope (to define when picked up)

* Let an organizer append a single new round to an existing league, numbered `max(round_number) + 1`, created as `pending`.
* Increment `leagues.total_rounds` accordingly.
* Decide interaction with league completion: appending should only be allowed while the league is still `active` (not `complete`), and must not violate the single-active-round invariant.
* Decide UX: where the "add a round" affordance lives now that the bulk-create form is hidden once rounds exist.

## Not doing now

Deferred — no current product need. Filed so the trade-off from [MYS-62](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-62/pre-created-rounds-bulk-creation-pending-state-and-admin-descriptions) is tracked rather than forgotten.

title: No profile/settings screen (preferred_service, account deletion unreachable)
description:
Surfaced while writing the E2E manual test plan (`docs/qa/e2e-test-plan.md`).

The route map (`frontend/src/App.tsx`) has no profile/settings route. As a result, two backend capabilities have no UI and can't be exercised by a human tester:

* `preferred_service` (spotify | youtube | deezer) — per `PATCH /users/me`. Drives which platform link is surfaced first on the round playlist. No way to set it in-app.
* **Account deletion** — `DELETE /users/me` (right to be forgotten, per technical-design §10). No UI entry point.

**Impact:** privacy/account-management commitments and the playback `preferred_service` behavior can't be validated through the UI.

Acceptance: a settings screen lets a user edit display name + preferred service and delete their account, making the corresponding E2E checks testable.

title: Upgrade frontend dev tooling (vite/vitest) to clear dev-only advisories
description:
Split out of the [MYS-47](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-47/dependency-audit-before-launch-pip-audit-npm-audit) dependency audit. After remediating prod-facing advisories (react-router-dom, form-data), 5 dev-only advisories remain in the frontend build tooling:

* vitest (critical) — Vitest UI server arbitrary file read (only when UI server is run)
* vite (high) — dev-server path traversal in optimized deps
* esbuild (high) — dev-server request issue
* @vitest/mocker, vite-node (moderate) — vitest ecosystem

These are exploitable only against a running local dev server, never in the production build, so they were deferred from the hardening pass. Clearing them requires breaking major bumps (vite 6→7, vitest 3→x).

Scope: bump vite + vitest (and the @vitejs/plugin-react / vitest config that comes with them) to current majors, fix any breaking config/test API changes, confirm `npm run build`, typecheck, and the full vitest suite pass, then re-run `npm audit` to confirm the dev advisories clear. See `docs/security/dependency-audit.md`.

title: Progressive reveal animation for the results screen
description:
Fast-follow split out of [MYS-24](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-24/round-reveal-and-results-ui). The round reveal should feel like a shared moment — add a progressive/staged reveal animation to the results screen (e.g. sections or rankings appearing in sequence) rather than the static reveal shipped in [MYS-24](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-24/round-reveal-and-results-ui).

Must stay within the style guide's restrained motion: subtle fades (~200ms page transition, 150ms ease), no bounces, no spring physics. The concentric-ring motif may be used for transitions.

Builds on the static results screen delivered in [MYS-24](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-24/round-reveal-and-results-ui) and the `GET /rounds/:id/results` endpoint ([MYS-23](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-23/round-results-endpoint)).

title: Staging: replace self-signed cert with Let's Encrypt
description:
Follow-up to [MYS-39](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-39/staging-environment-on-a-digitalocean-droplet). Staging (DigitalOcean Droplet, 67.207.81.183) currently serves HTTPS with a **self-signed** cert, so testers get a browser warning to click through. Once a domain points at the box, swap it for a trusted Let's Encrypt cert.

## Steps (see docs/staging-setup.md §5)

1. Point a subdomain (e.g. `staging.mysterymixclub.com`) at `67.207.81.183`.
2. Set `server_name` in `/etc/nginx/sites-available/mysterymixclub-staging` to the domain.
3. `sudo certbot --nginx -d staging.mysterymixclub.com` (certbot takes over the `ssl_certificate` directives + installs auto-renew).
4. Update `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` / `APP_BASE_URL` in `/etc/mysterymixclub/staging.env` to the new domain and restart `mysterymixclub-api`.
5. Update the `STAGING_HOST` GitHub secret if testers should use the hostname.

## Notes

* No code changes needed; the committed nginx config already has the SSL placeholder certbot expects.
* Optional: with a real domain + HTTPS, consider setting `environment == "production"`-style secure cookies for staging (currently `ENVIRONMENT=staging` leaves auth cookies non-`Secure`).

Blocked on: acquiring/pointing a domain.

title: Decision: move prod Postgres off the droplet to a managed instance (deferred)
description:
Split out from MysteryMixClub-s7bv2t (MYS-259) on 2026-07-26 — Dawn agreed to deprioritize this rather than bundle it into the runtime-tuning ticket.

## Why this exists as its own ticket

This proposal directly contradicts an existing documented decision: infra/terraform/README.md's own 'what breaks first at 10x users' section explicitly says to split Postgres onto its own plain droplet BEFORE ever reaching for managed Postgres, which would reintroduce the vendor lock-in ADR 0002 (docs/adr/0002-prod-platform-self-managed-droplet.md) specifically moved off App Platform to avoid.

MMC is currently at 5-10 users on a droplet that has never even been resized once - the trigger condition ('traffic or operational burden outgrows what a single droplet can reasonably carry') that would justify revisiting this has not fired.

## If this gets picked up later

- This is a genuine strategy reversal from a documented prior decision, not a routine infra change - it needs its own ADR (per docs/adr/README.md) explicitly naming the lock-in cost (DO Managed Postgres is still a DO-specific Terraform resource type with no cross-cloud equivalent, though the underlying data is trivially portable via pg_dump/logical replication - a narrower lock-in than App Platform's, but real) and the exit path, not a bullet folded into an unrelated ticket.
- Consider the documented intermediate step first: Postgres on its own plain droplet (still portable, no managed-service lock-in) before jumping to a managed instance.
- Real migration risk if pursued: needs a new digitalocean_database_cluster Terraform resource, a connection-pooler decision (PgBouncer vs DO's built-in pooling), a cutover mechanism (pg_dump/restore with a downtime window, or logical replication), a DATABASE_URL change in /etc/mysterymixclub/prod.env (through Dawn's hands per the no-prod-SSH rule, not an agent SSH session), and a verified rollback plan keeping the old on-droplet Postgres intact through a burn-in period.
- MysteryMixClub-aqz0tt's backup/restore work would need rescoping (not duplicating) if this ever ships - DO Managed Postgres has its own automated backups/PITR, a different implementation than the pg_dump-to-Spaces design aqz0tt currently owns.
notes: Do not pick this up without re-confirming the scale trigger has actually fired and without writing the ADR first. Related: MysteryMixClub-s7bv2t (where this was split from), MysteryMixClub-aqz0tt (backup/restore, would need rescoping if this ships).

title: New feature idea: make a mix for a friend (needs scoping)
description:
**Raw idea from user testing** — exact shape not yet defined. Candidates raised while triaging:

* A one-off gift mix outside the normal club structure (just you + one friend)
* A one-time guest invite into an existing club's current mix, without full membership

Needs a product conversation to pick a direction before anyone scopes or estimates this. Do not start build against this description as-is.

title: Parallel mode: support multiple mystery mixes running at once
description:
**Feature idea** (from user testing, explicitly requested as a backlog ticket, not near-term)

Today a club runs exactly one open mystery mix at a time (sequential, `total_mixes` cap). Some testers want the option to run several mixes concurrently ("parallel mode").

This is a large change, not yet scoped — touches the deadline job (`app.jobs.advance_mixes`), per-club state machine, leaderboard aggregation, and club home UI, all of which currently assume a single active mix. Needs a design pass before estimation. No priority until then.

title: Add Tidal playlist generation support
description:
## Summary

Add Tidal as a fourth playlist-generation target, alongside existing Spotify, YouTube, and Apple Music support. No embedded player — matches existing pattern of generating a real playlist in the user's account for each service.

## Scope

* Register MMC app in the Tidal developer portal; request `playlists.read`, `playlists.write`, `user.read` OAuth scopes
* Add Tidal to existing OAuth flow alongside Spotify/Google/Apple (per-user authorize step)
* Reuse existing resolve-tracks → create-playlist → add-items pipeline; add Tidal branch using Tidal Open API v2 create-playlist and add-tracks endpoints
* Track matching via ISRC against Tidal catalog search, consistent with existing matching approach for other services

## Risks / open questions

* Tidal's Open API v2 is newer than Spotify/YouTube/Apple equivalents — team has stated they're still opening up endpoints over time, and some functionality remains SDK-only (not REST)
* Write-scope approval (`playlists.write`) has had reported friction in the developer community — may need back-and-forth with Tidal before scopes are granted
* Tidal's catalog is smaller — expect a higher miss rate on ISRC track matching than Spotify; need a fallback/reporting path for unmatched tracks (consistent with whatever pattern exists for other services)
* Do not use the unofficial `tidalapi` Python library or similar reverse-engineered clients — ToS risk for a public-facing product; official Open API only

## Out of scope

* Embedded Tidal player (explicitly not wanted)
* One-off catalog links (tracked separately if needed — simpler, no-OAuth catalog search + link construction)

title: Feature flag: disable email sending on staging and dev environments
description:
Add a feature flag (env var, e.g. `EMAIL_ENABLED=false`) that disables outbound email sending when running on staging and dev. Prevents accidental emails to real users/test accounts during testing and demos.

**Acceptance criteria:**

* Flag defaults to `false`/off on dev and staging environments
* Flag defaults to `true`/on in production
* When disabled, email send calls are no-op'd or logged instead of sent (log the would-be email content for debugging)
* Documented in `.env.example` / relevant config docs

title: Add "Beta" badge to header and login page
description:
Add a "Beta" tag/badge to:

* The app header
* The login page

Keep it lightweight (small badge next to logo/wordmark) — just signals the app is in beta.

title: Email login link redirects to login even when already authenticated
description:
**Bug**

Clicking an email link (e.g. magic link / notification link) sends the user to the login screen even when they already have an active, logged-in session.

**Expected**: If a valid session exists, the email link should take the user directly to the destination content instead of forcing re-login.

**To investigate**

* Check how session/auth state is checked before rendering the login route
* Confirm whether it's a stale token/cookie check or a redirect that fires before auth state hydrates client-side

title: Invite via email: club admin enters an email, invite link is sent there
description:
Currently a club invite is a shareable link the organizer copies and sends themselves (any channel). Add a direct path: the organizer enters an invitee's email address in-app, and MysteryMixClub sends the club invite link to that address via Resend (same mailer as magic-link/notification email).

**Why:** lowers friction for organizers who'd rather not manually copy/paste a link into a text or email themselves, and gives a more traditional "invite a friend" flow alongside the existing shareable link.

**Scope (initial pass):**

* Club admin/organizer UI: an email input alongside (not replacing) the existing shareable invite link.
* Backend: reuse the existing club-invite token/model — this only changes delivery (email instead of copy-link), not the invite mechanics themselves.
* Send via the existing `EmailSender`/Resend integration, matching the notification email brand shell ([[[MYS-237](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-237/revisit-email-notifications-and-messages)]]-style wrapper).
* Sent invite should behave identically to a copy-pasted link once clicked (same token, same expiry, same waitlist-skip behavior noted in the FAQ/create-club copy).

**Open questions to resolve during implementation:**

* Resend/reuse an invite if the email hasn't clicked it yet, or require a fresh one?
* Any rate limiting on how many email invites an organizer can fire off?
* Does the organizer get any confirmation/error if the email bounces?

Not scoped here: bulk/CSV invite, invite reminders, or tracking accept/decline state beyond what already exists for link invites.

title: Inconsistent field validation and unclear error messages on new club form
description:
## Bug

Validation behaves inconsistently across fields on the new-club form, and the resulting error messages are unclear to the user.

## Needs investigation

* Audit each field on the create-club form for its validation trigger (on blur vs on submit vs live), and align them to one consistent pattern.
* Audit error message copy for each field — messages should be direct and calm per the style guide's voice/tone rules (e.g. "That link didn't work. Try another." not vague/technical text).
* Confirm whether this is frontend-only (validation logic/timing) or also surfaces backend validation errors verbatim (e.g. raw Pydantic/HTTP error text leaking through).

## Done when

All fields on the new-club form validate consistently (same trigger pattern) and every validation error reads as clear, calm, user-facing copy.

title: Spike: music-metadata provider + caching strategy for progressive scaling (alpha → 1000s of leagues)
description:
**Spike / research — do not implement.** Scope follow-up tickets once findings land.

## Why now

The app's song identity/search currently centers on **keyless Deezer** (`api.deezer.com`) for search + ISRC, with the [MYS-81](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-81/migrate-off-odesli-public-api-before-it-is-retired-2026-07-31) resolver funneling everything through it. That's fine for the alpha, but it's the *same risk class* that just bit us with Odesli — a free, best-effort, undocumented public API. Two structural limits show up as we grow:

* **Durability:** keyless public APIs can be rate-tightened or retired with little notice (Odesli → retired 2026-07-31). No SLA, no guaranteed commercial terms.
* **Scale ceiling:** keyless limits are **per-IP**, and all our traffic egresses from one server IP — so quota does *not* grow as we add users/leagues. At ~1000 active leagues, search-as-you-type + deadline bursts would blow past an undocumented ~10 req/s/IP ceiling and 429 for everyone at once.

## Goal

Define a metadata/identity strategy and resolver architecture that is **right-sized for the alpha (a few leagues) but has a clear, staged path to thousands** — progressive scaling, not premature over-engineering. Center the design on what's durable (ISRC + a pluggable resolver + caching), not on any single vendor. Must honor the principle: **Spotify-friendly but never Spotify-required**; degrade gracefully, keyless baseline.

## Progressive scaling tiers (define adequacy + the trigger to advance for each)

* **Tier 0 — alpha (a few leagues):** keyless Deezer primary + basic caching. Lowest cost/complexity.
* **Tier 1 — 10s–100s of leagues:** first-class shared cache, client-side search debounce/throttle, outbound rate-limiting + backoff; evaluate a keyed provider.
* **Tier 2 — 1000s of leagues:** remove the per-IP ceiling — **keyed/commercial provider** (per-account quota) and/or **self-hosted metadata** (MusicBrainz mirror / local ISRC table) for the hot path.
  For each tier, specify the **metrics/thresholds that signal it's time to move up** (e.g. provider 429 rate, p95 resolve latency, quota headroom, cache hit-rate).

## Questions to answer

* **Durability / governance / ToS** (the column we skipped on Odesli): per candidate — ownership, funding model, API versioning + deprecation history, commercial-use terms, attribution requirements, whether caching/storing results is permitted.
* **Access & quota model:** keyless-per-IP vs keyed-per-account vs OAuth; documented rate limits; cost at 10 / 100 / 1000-league projections.
* **Coverage & data quality (empirical):** run a real ~75–100 song test set spanning eras/genres/regions/obscurity through each candidate; measure **ISRC hit-rate, correct-match rate, latency, coverage gaps**. Don't decide from reputation/docs alone.
* **Load model:** enumerate what generates provider calls (search-as-you-type, submit-time resolve + ISRC + link assembly + YouTube id) and burst patterns (round-deadline clustering); project calls/sec at each tier.
* **Caching strategy (first-class deliverable):** a shared, **ISRC/query-keyed cache across all leagues** (popular songs resolve once globally); what to cache (search results, resolution, platform links, video ids), TTL/invalidation, and modeled hit-rate impact on provider load.
* **Resolver abstraction:** confirm a provider is a single-file swap and supports a **fallback chain** (e.g. Deezer → MusicBrainz → optional Spotify/Apple as exactness boosters). Keep ISRC as the identity backbone (open ISO standard, vendor-independent).

## Candidates to evaluate

Deezer (current), MusicBrainz/AcoustID (open, nonprofit — durable fallback), iTunes Search (keyless, no ISRC), Spotify Web API (exact ISRC, needs secret — enhancement only), Apple Music API (needs paid dev token), commercial aggregators (ACRCloud / Gracenote / Musixmatch), and **self-hosted MusicBrainz** mirror.

## Deliverable

A findings doc in `docs/discovery/` covering: recommended primary + fallback chain, the caching design, the **staged scaling plan with concrete advance-triggers/metrics**, the resolver interface, and a proposed implementation-ticket breakdown. No production code.

## Out of scope / relationships

* Does NOT block [MYS-81](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-81/migrate-off-odesli-public-api-before-it-is-retired-2026-07-31) — that resolver ships now on Deezer-primary; this spike changes *what sits behind the interface*, not the interface.
* Relates to [MYS-81](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-81/migrate-off-odesli-public-api-before-it-is-retired-2026-07-31) (resolver), [MYS-78](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-78/playlist-one-click-youtube-playlist-link-for-a-round-watch-videos-no) (YouTube ids), [MYS-76](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-76/spike-auto-generate-streaming-playlists-youtube-deezer-spotify-as) (playlist spike). Honors the "Spotify-friendly, not required" and ISRC-backbone principles.

title: Spike: Apple Music integration (links + playlist generation)
description:
**Spike / research — do not start implementation.** Scope follow-up tickets once findings land. Apple Music is flagged as a must for next steps (`docs/idea-scratch.md`) and already appears in our platform-link set.

## Goal

Assess what it takes to support **Apple Music** as a first-class service: playback linking (largely done) and, in line with the broader playlist work ([MYS-76](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-76/spike-auto-generate-streaming-playlists-youtube-deezer-spotify-as)), generating an Apple Music playlist for a round.

## Current state

* We already build Apple Music **playback links** keylessly via the iTunes Search API (`app/services/song_links.py`).
* No write/playlist capability or MusicKit integration exists.

## Questions to answer

* **Auth model:** Apple Music API requires a **developer token** (signed JWT, from an Apple Developer Program membership) plus a per-user **Music User Token** obtained via MusicKit (JS/native). Map the full flow and where tokens live (server vs client).
* **Playlist creation:** can we create a playlist in the user's Apple Music library and add tracks? Required scopes/endpoints, limits.
* **Track matching:** resolve our ISRC → Apple Music catalog track ID (catalog search by ISRC). Accuracy vs. the iTunes Search path we use today.
* **Cost / gating:** Apple Developer Program membership (~$99/yr) is required; any review/approval for MusicKit; platform constraints (web vs iOS).
* **Keyless / link-only fallback:** is there any anonymous Apple playlist link analogous to YouTube's `watch_videos`? (Expected: no — likely OAuth/MusicKit only.)
* **Where it fits** relative to the YouTube pilot and Spotify/Deezer OAuth phases.

## Deliverable

A short findings doc (`docs/discovery/`) — feasibility, recommended auth approach, and a proposed ticket breakdown. No production code.

## Reference

Relates to [MYS-76](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-76/spike-auto-generate-streaming-playlists-youtube-deezer-spotify-as) (streaming playlist spike) and the existing Apple Music linking in `song_links.py`.

title: Spike: auto-generate streaming playlists (YouTube, Deezer, Spotify) as clickable links
description:
**Spike / research — do not start implementation from this ticket.** Scope follow-up work into separate tickets once findings land.

## Goal

For a round's set of submitted songs, generate a ready-to-open playlist on each supported streaming service, surfaced as a clickable link:

* **YouTube** — auto-generate a playlist and produce a clickable link.
* **Deezer** — generate a playlist.
* **Spotify** — generate a playlist.

## Questions to answer

* Per service: what does each API require to create a playlist and add tracks? (auth model, OAuth scopes, app registration, rate limits, quotas.)
* Can a playlist be created without per-user OAuth (e.g. a shareable link / anonymous or app-owned playlist), or does each user have to authorize? Document the tradeoffs.
* Track matching: we store submissions per service — how do we resolve a song to each *other* service's track ID for cross-service playlists? Is cross-service even in scope, or one playlist per service using that service's own submissions?
* What identifiers do we already persist per submission, and what's missing to support this?
* Where does playlist generation live — backend endpoint vs. client-side link construction? (See `docs/technical/technical-design.md`.)
* Cost / quota implications (notably YouTube Data API quota).

## Deliverable

A short findings doc (recommend `docs/discovery/`) covering feasibility per service, the recommended auth approach, and a proposed breakdown of implementation tickets. No production code.

## Notes

Relates to the existing "Better playlists; ability to generate whole playlist in youtube, deezer, spotify" idea in `docs/idea-scratch.md`.

title: League page: show winner + most-noted on closed round cards
description:
On the league home page, each **closed** round card now surfaces a compact reveal summary so members can scan outcomes without opening every round:

* **Winner** — the top of the vote leaderboard. Because the backend assigns *sequential* leaderboard ranks (no shared rank for ties), a first-place tie is detected by matching the top `vote_count`; every co-winner is named. A top score of 0 (nobody voted for) shows no winner.
* **Most noted** — the song(s) that drew the most notes (`most_noted.winners`, already tie-aware). Ties list every pick.
* A closed round with no votes and no notes shows no summary at all (kept calm — no empty-state line).

Stays entirely in the Sage/Ink family — no Rust, since the league screen reserves its single Rust use for the league-complete badge.

**Implementation**

* `frontend/src/pages/LeagueHomeRoute.tsx` — fetch `getResults()` for every closed round in parallel once the slate loads; store in a `roundResults` map. Failures are non-fatal (card just shows no summary).
* `frontend/src/pages/LeagueHomeScreen.tsx` — `topVoteWinners()` helper + `ClosedRoundSummary` component (label-left / value-right).
* `frontend/src/pages/LeagueHomeRoute.test.tsx` — coverage for single winner, tie (co-winners + multiple most-noted, non-tied excluded), and no-votes/no-notes (summary omitted).

All 181 frontend tests pass; typecheck + eslint clean.

Branch: `feature/mys-62-pre-created-rounds`. Related reveal work: [MYS-23](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-23/round-results-endpoint) / [MYS-24](https://linear.app/mysterymixclub/issue/MYS-24/round-reveal-and-results-ui).

title: Dev logging: surface app logs so magic-link sign-in works under plain uvicorn
description:
## Problem

In local development there is no `RESEND_API_KEY`, so the auth flow falls back to `ConsoleEmailSender`, which logs the magic link instead of emailing it:

```
logger.info("Magic link for %s: %s", email, link)   # logger = "app.services.email"
```

But the app never configured Python logging, and uvicorn's default logging config does not attach a handler to the `app.*` loggers. So under a normal `uvicorn app.main:app` invocation that INFO record is **dropped** — the magic link never appears anywhere.

Because magic-link tokens are stored **hashed** (`token_hash`), the log line is the *only* way to recover a usable sign-in link locally. With it swallowed, there is no way to log in during local development without manually reconfiguring logging.

## Impact

* New contributor follows the README, runs `uvicorn`, requests a sign-in link → nothing to click, login is impossible.
* Discovered while bringing the stack up locally to test the new CI/CD pipeline.

## Fix (implemented, pending commit)

Added `_configure_dev_logging()` in `backend/app/main.py`, called from `create_app()` only when `ENVIRONMENT=development`. It attaches a stdout handler to the `app` logger at INFO. Idempotent (guards against duplicate handlers) and a no-op in production, so it does not risk leaking plaintext sign-in links in prod logs.

Verified: under plain `uvicorn app.main:app --log-level info`, requesting a link now prints:

```
INFO:app.services.email:Magic link for devtest@example.com: http://localhost:5173/auth/verify?token=...
```

All 45 backend tests still pass; ruff clean.

## Follow-up (out of scope)

Production logging strategy (structured/JSON logs, log levels per environment) is intentionally not addressed here — this change is dev-ergonomics only.

title: Connect your tools
description:
Integrations turn Linear into your source of truth around product development. Keep data in sync, and eliminate manual updates between tools.

![connect-your-tools.png](https://uploads.linear.app/fe63b3e2-bf87-46c0-8784-cd7d639287c8/c2eae035-37e2-4754-adcb-b8305431aa1f/c92d70c7-e6d0-4fa2-a0fd-78f6e780993a)

### **Key integrations**

* [**Slack**](<https://linear.app/settings/integrations/slack>)
  Create issues from Slack messages and sync threads
* [**GitHub**](<https://linear.app/settings/integrations/github>)** / **[**GitLab**](<https://linear.app/settings/integrations/gitlab>)
  Automate your pull request, commit workflows, and keep issues synced both ways
* [**Agents**](<https://linear.app/integrations/agents>)
  Deploy AI agents that work alongside you as teammates

### **Browse all integrations**

Discover 150+ available connections in our [integration directory](<https://linear.app/integrations>) – from bug creation via support tools (Intercom, Zendesk), to issues created from design explorations (Figma).

### **Linear API**

If you need something more custom, you can build directly on the Linear API (built on GraphQL). [See our Dev Docs to learn more](<https://linear.app/developers>).
